title: G100 Global Chairs Retreats, Fort Barwara Six Senses, Rajasthan, India, 1-4 June, July, August 2024.
excerpt: Retreating: Soul, Solitude, Serenity, Sisterhood, Sustenance, Sustainability & Self-Discovery. A… Read more
content_html:
Retreating: Soul, Solitude, Serenity, Sisterhood, Sustenance, Sustainability & Self-Discovery. A Journey Within in Search of our Better Selves, our Better World. 

G100 Global Chairs Retreats, Fort Barwara Six Senses, Rajasthan, India, 1-4 June, July, August 2024.


The Global Chairs retreats were held across three months of June, July and August 2024, in small cohorts. They were held at the Fort Barwara Six Senses, a spacious sanctuary, royal retreat, and an epic sustainable vision, providing an exceptional opportunity for exchanging ideas and thoughts on advancing G100’s global mission in solidarity, friendship and inspiration. 

As we immersed in the serene environs, protected by the power of the mighty fort, a tranquil ambiance pervaded our spirit, enveloping us in its lap of luxury and love, taking our breath away – and in the process, giving our breath back to ourselves. Retreating to nourish the core of our being became a precious opportunity to look within and see further. Breaking from the rhythm of daily lives, we took the opportunity to reflect and relax, enjoying the company of nature, ourselves, and one another, replete with a vision of what our world can be when we decide to dedicate ourselves to a vision of wellness and wellbeing, in every sense possible. 

During the three retreats, we were joined by almost 100 members, including global chairs, denim club members, along with their families and friends in solidarity. Together, we strengthened our commitment to creating an equitable world, building on common grounds and shared interests. Each retreat became an enriching occasion to better connect with our global chairs and their families. Each one offered incredible inspiration, offering many learnings and takeaways, especially regards envisioning the future toward building our network and strengthening the agenda of diversity, inclusion, and representation. 

The retreat didn’t have an agenda by design; the agenda being to unwind and connect to oneself and others, with the fullness of our presence and positivity. We were particularly moved by the wisdom and philosophy shared from different cultures and continents, which will stay with us as we strive to be better and do better for society. We explored new business opportunities and made new plans, for our personal growth as also the growth of the collective, the two being intertwined. 

The connections made during the retreat were truly special, and the feeling of being connected in global solidarity was palpable and powerful. The extensive network of wonderful individuals seemed like an endless ocean of love, learning and kindness. In our microcosm of meaningful connections, with generosity and receptivity, no challenge seemed overwhelming and everything seemed possible; such was the reservoir of energy and upliftment that we were able to tap into, just by retreating. 

We realised that ‘retreating’ should also become more woven into our lifestyles. Just as we talk nowadays about work-life balance, we need to also grow awareness, through experiences such as this, around the important of retreating, which helps awaken a certain deeper quality of listening, connecting, sharing. Just as we dig deeper to find water within the earth, likewise the waters of sustenance are within us, and we can bring them up by diving deep in self-discovery, in serenity and soulfulness, as enabled in a retreat. Retreating takes us back to our self, back to the basics, and back to the beginnings. We can take better perspective and be able to declutter our minds and unburden our hearts in powerful ways, thereby coming up with easy and innovative solutions to intransigent issues of our times. Retreating, we can win the wars in our own hearts, and thus be able to find ways to peace in newfound ways. 

All appreciated the opportunity to connect with one another, in a relaxed vacation like setting. The spa and the safari provided added energy and enthusiasm. We laughed, learned and lifted one another in our shared commitment to making a better world, keen to collaborate on projects across wings to create meaningful impacts. In addition to the wellness and healing programs at the resort such as spa and yoga, we also experienced an inner empowerment and commitment to wellness in other senses and from other sources, such as the the robust expression of continuity, heritage, culture, innate in the external designs and principles animating the space of the retreat. Reverberating with a sense of respect for community, environment, energy, conservation and restoration, we could feel the pulse of sustainability everywhere. 

We had an immersive experience on how all can can coexist, and how we can blend and balance all kinds of imperatives, when we are able to access intention and inspiration, knowing that we are never alone and can find communities of support and strength. In these communities of solidarity, we can also harness a treasure trove of talents and abilities, which are in readiness for growth in mutual enrichment, powered by the purpose of the collective. When the collective grows, we all grow automatically, as we are part of it. When we grow individually, the collective is energised as well, as each and everyone can contribute to the collective through one’s own knowledge, initiatives, networks and actions. We are all connected and the currents of transformation can easily move through us all, enabling us to bridge all kinds of dualities and divides. Together we can drive impact within our communities and thereby many such communities can drive change worldwide. 

Toward the close of the retreats, one could feel the renewed sense of energy and passion toward one’s future tasks. Learning and listening created new spaces for improved ideation and intentional actions. We delved into strategies for taking the wings forward with gusto and guidelines, ensuring the vital participation of members and proactive leadership of chairs. Our discussions focused on how to accelerate our actions and enlighten our imagination to ensure that G100 remains a persevering and visionary organization, passing the test of time, with its strong foundations in enduring values of inclusion and connection. 

We were delighted to see ever greater participation from the Denim Club in the successive retreats. Our brothers reaffirmed their commitment to promoting women empowerment, equity, and inclusiveness on a global scale, engaging in dialogue with influential leaders, and making headway to engage with the highest levels of leadership across institutions. With a million gender champions activated, as is the blueprint of the G100, our ambitious goal becomes accessible: to effect change now, and not to wait another 100 years. 

Indeed, we also recognised that the task ahead is challenging, especially in a male-dominated world. However, with passion, determination, and a willingness to achieve against all odds, we can come closer and closer to our aims. Just as women leaders of the past century persevered and gifted us the times of today, we too had to continue to do our part, embracing the challenges en route, and surmounting them with our collective strength and intelligence. Amidst us, we have all kinds of capabilities and endless opportunities. As we say at the network, together we can, and together we will. Every step we take brings us closer to our ultimate goal. 

By the end of the 21st century, in a few years from now, we envision G100 as an organisation of immense power and influence, with a voice that cannot be ignored by any government or people. We aim to have our message reverberate through the corridors of power, compelling those in charge to implement meaningful changes.
One of the key highlights of the retreat was the development of ideas for the coming years, such as on increasing our global outreach, enhancing our advocacy efforts, and building strategic partnerships with like-minded organisation. We need to persevere on our path to dismantle systemic barriers and create a more inclusive society. 

The respective retreats concluded with good news of women leaders being elected to lead their countries, such as in Iceland and Mexico. And perhaps, the US might also elect its first female President. These developments serve as a powerful reminder of the impact that empowered women can have on global governance and policy-making, as also promoting peace. 

However, in order to support women to lead longer and stronger, we need to underscore the importance of creating robust support structures for women leaders, in order to reduce burnout and ensure their leadership remains resilient, overcoming the challenges en route. We have examples of many women leaders who had to quit prematurely, either due to the ‘glass cliff’ phenomenon, or because of it being lonely at the top, with scant support and inordinate pressure and personal attacks. 

To stay strong and upbeat and on the upward curve is an uphill task. All the more reason that retreating needs to become part of our lives, especially for all leaders in high octane environments, in order to reclaim our own soul through solitude and solidarity, embracing the inner reservoir of happiness, optimism, inspiration and solidarity. 

Overall, the G100 global chairs retreats were a resounding success, laying a solid foundation for our future endeavours. The retreats will continue through the rest of the year as well, with the various country clubs across wings. The G100 CEOs retreats would also be engaged in furtherance of these objectives. 

To conclude, the retreats created a most fulfilling experience of self-discovery and self-sustenance through solitude, soulfulness and the strength of sisterhood, uplifted by a vision of sustainability. We became more inspired and more united than ever, ready to face the challenges ahead and make a lasting impact on the world.  Together we can. 
 
Convenors & Hosts: 
Founder & President, G100 Club, Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai
Founder & President, Denim Club, Vinay Rai

title: G100 CEOs Retreats, Fort Barwara Six Senses, Rajasthan, India 17-20 August & 17-20 September 2024
excerpt: The Wholeness and Emptiness of Rest: Reset with Rest, for… Read more
content_html:
The Wholeness and Emptiness of Rest: Reset with Rest, for Reflection, Reprioritisation, and Recalibration. 

G100 CEOs Retreats, Fort Barwara Six Senses, Rajasthan, India 17-20 August & 17-20 September 2024

The G100 CEOs Retreats brought together inspiring entrepreneurs and C-suite leaders for respective three-day gatherings, across August and September. Set amidst the serene and spiritually uplifting environment of Six Senses Fort Barwara, in Rajasthan, India, the retreats fostered friendships, cultivating supportive networks, particularly empowering women’s leadership in senior roles and entrepreneurial paths. Many attendees joined with their families, highlighting the essential role of personal support in professional advancement.
 
The retreats drew global participation from 25 countries, including: Argentina, Armenia, Austria, Cameroon, Canada, Costa Rica, Cyprus, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Israel, Italy, Lebanon, Luxembourg, Poland, Slovenia, South Africa, Switzerland, UAE, UK, USA, Uzbekistan, and India.
 
The retreats held the objective and intention of bridging gaps in women’s support systems, especially in entrepreneurship and leadership, in order to embolden women to take the leaps as necessary, in their personal and professional lives. 
 
It was deeply moving to see beautifully bonds blossoming among participants from across cultures and contents. With ample networking opportunities in a spirit of friendship and camaraderie, many explored new partnerships and possibilities for growth. 
 
Indeed, a standout feature of the retreat was the opportunity to connect with people of calibre from diverse cultural backgrounds. As we shared our stories, passions, and perspectives, our open hearts and minds ignited inspiration, creativity, and aspiration. Not only did we foster a global community in a family-feeling, but we also enhanced opportunities for personal and professional growth, in an immersive experience that brought out the person and human behind every leader. 
 
Some key learnings were: 
 
• A global mix of leaders always enriches all with a sense of solidarity and common purpose, notwithstanding the political uncertainty or cultural differences.
• Such shared experiences in a relaxed setting enable us to interact from generous and authentic perspectives, deepening bonds and building relationships with the power of perspective softened with receptivity on all sides.
• Top leadership and entrepreneurs need the stimulus of such solidarity in exchange, inspiration and cooperation, to up their game and lead better with depth of insight and understanding, overcoming inner biases and barriers.
• Concepts such as diversity, harmony, equality, sustainability can be better understood (and not just superficially as buzzwords) through lived settings such as these, improving the implementation of policies and culture-setting around them.
• CEOs need such retreats to learn from other CEOs, women and men, and especially across the Global North – South divide, to truly embrace leadership diversity, and self-growth. As leaders are transformed, so is their leadership. 
 
An intriguing observation from our retreats has been the request for an agenda, which we intentionally omitted to foster an environment of informal connection. In the absence of an external agenda, the internal agenda took center stage: rejuvenating each individual from the inside out, and enabling us to connect with depth. 
 
Of course, we offered various kind of activities which one could choose from, including spa and yoga. However, senior leaders and high-achievers being ever in pursuit of action and performance struggle with the idea of doing “nothing”. Little do we realise that it is by embracing the present moment in all its wholeness, or emptiness, that we can reassess our onward path, and rewire our brains and beings, transforming all that we bring to our future. 
 
In today’s fast-paced world, where rushing often masquerades as progress, embracing rest is crucial. Rest is not a luxury; it’s essential for reflective energy, creativity, and change. Rest renews our perspective and helps us in reprioritisation. Rest empowers reflection, enhancing our capacity for connection and creation. When rested, we have improved focus and clarity. Rest helps us cope better with life’s challenges. Simply put, rested, we live better, work better. Our retreats have taught us this most valuable lesson.
 
Convenors & Hosts: 
Founder & President, G100 Club, Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai
Founder & President, Denim Club, Vinay Rai

title: G100 Caribbean & Commonwealth Meetings, Jamaica,  19-20 September 2024
excerpt: Collaboration across the Commonwealth: Overcoming Barriers, Succeeding Together G100 Caribbean… Read more
content_html:
Collaboration across the Commonwealth: Overcoming Barriers, Succeeding Together 

G100 Caribbean & Commonwealth Meetings, Jamaica-UK

19-20 September 2024.

 
On Thursday, September 19th, 2024, the University of East London’s (UEL) Royal Docks School of Business and Law (RDSBL) became the stage for a groundbreaking two-day symposium, “Women Overcoming Barriers to Success: A Cross-Sector Narrative Perspective of Hope.” The event, organized by Dr. Doirean Wilson, UEL Associate Professor of Sustainability in Management and G100 Club UK Country Chair of the Higher Education & Industry Connect Wing, ignited a dynamic conversation on gender equity, leadership diversity, and the power of resilience in overcoming professional challenges.
 
The symposium opened with a moment of pure emotion as Dr. Patti Boulaye OBE, renowned singer, actress, and artist, delivered a stunning rendition of Etta James’ classic “At Last,” setting the tone for two days filled with inspiration and empowerment. Boulaye’s soulful performance received rapturous applause, marking the beginning of an event that would explore the diverse narratives of women leaders who have defied the odds.
 
The prestigious event was a collaborative effort with the Jamaican High Commission, supported by UEL’s Centre for Innovation Management and Enterprise (CIME), and sponsored by Supply Care Solutions. Guests included ambassadors, thought leaders, entrepreneurs, UEL students, and staff—all eager to gain insights from some of the most distinguished women in leadership today.
 
Central to the symposium was G100 Club’s bold “Mission Million” initiative, presented by Founder and President, Dr Harbeen Arora Rai. This global campaign seeks to fast-track gender equity in leadership by drastically shortening the time it would take to achieve balanced representation at the highest levels—an ambition that, without intervention, could take 130 years. G100 aims to achieve this in just ten.
 
Throughout the event, VIP keynote speakers shared their career-life journeys, offering insight into the barriers they encountered and the strategies they used to overcome them. These personal stories, marked by resilience and determination, deeply resonated with the audience. Zeinab Badawi, the award-winning journalist and broadcaster, discussed the challenges women face in maintaining career momentum while balancing family life. “Regardless of where you are in the world,” she noted, “there are still disproportionately fewer women in top positions. How do we balance the desire to have children with the momentum needed to stay on our career paths?”

Other distinguished speakers included Paulette Simpson CBE, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of Jamaica National Bank UK & Executive Director of The Voice Media Group; Dr.Yvonne Thompson CBE, President of the European Federation of Black Women Business Owners; and The Worshipful Mayor of Southwark, Naima Ali. Each speaker added their voice to the symposium’s central theme—how women, across sectors and industries, can rise above systemic barriers to achieve success.

One of the key moments came when His Excellency Alexander Williams, Jamaica’s High Commissioner to the UK, emphasized the importance of diversity in leadership. “Diverse leadership teams, including women, can improve organizational performance, innovation, and governance,” he said. His sentiments were echoed by Dr. Stuart Lawrence, a G100 Denim Club member and “He-for-She” advocate, who delivered an impassioned speech on the limitless potential of women to overcome challenges. This belief was echoed by Dr. Leroy Logan MBE, a former senior black British police officer, whose life as an officer was portrayed by British Actor John Boyega of `Star Wars` fame, in the award-winning film `Small Axe` Red, White, and Blue feature, by Director Steve McQueen.
A series of prestigious awards were presented throughout the event, recognizing leaders whose work has had a profound impact on advancing gender equity. The “Women of the Decade” award was bestowed upon Professor Fatima Annan-Diab, Executive Dean of RDSBL; Zeinab Badawi; and Her Excellency, The Rt Hon Baroness Patricia Scotland, Commonwealth Secretary-General. These women, through their contributions in education, media, and international leadership, embody the spirit of progress toward a more inclusive future.

The Rt Honourable Dr. Stuart Lawrence, son of Baroness Doreen Lawrence, and brother of  Stephen Lawrence who was murdered in a 1993 racist attack, and Colin Burton, National Reference Lead for the National Police Chiefs’ Council, were honoured with the “Legendary Leaders of the Decade” award, while several others received accolades for their groundbreaking work in creating a better world for all. Notable among them were Professor Amanda Broderick, UEL’s Vice Chancellor and President, recognized as an “Iconic Woman Creating a Better World for All,” and Dr. Jak Beula, CEO of Nubian Jak Community Trust, Darren Johnson Founder XLTRAINING, Rudi Page CEO MCW Connectivity, and Michael Mowatt Founder & CEO BVTV, who all received an “Iconic Companies Creating a Better World for All” award.
 
In addition to the awards, young leaders and innovators were also celebrated for their contributions to creating a brighter future, with awards going to Aret Komlosy and Adam White-Johnson, and Remeez Saleem.

The event also served as a platform for future academic contributions. Dr. Doirean Wilson announced that she had been invited to be a lead guest editor for a special issue of the Journal of Applied Accounting Research, an output of the symposium. This publication will feature research papers from symposium speakers, including UEL academics and global thought leaders, furthering the conversation on gender equity and leadership diversity.

As the symposium came to a close, Dr. Doirean Wilson reflected on its profound significance: “This event has showcased the power of hope, resilience, and collaboration. Together, we are not just imagining a better future for women; we are actively creating it.”

With its message of optimism and collective action, the G100 Club Global Symposium left attendees inspired to continue the work of breaking down barriers and advancing women’s leadership across sectors, industries, and geographies.

content_html:
H.E. Natalia Royo de Hagerman

H.E. Natalia Royo de Hagerman

H.E. Natalia Royo de Hagerman is Former Ambassador and public figure, Excellency Natalia comes from a legacy of political and diplomatic leadership. Excellency Royo has held several positions in the Panamanian foreign service and international organizations. In her last position as Ambassador of Panama in the UK and Ireland, she was in charge of lobby and negotiations to elect a Panamanian as Secretary General to the International Maritime Organization (IMO). During her tenure she was elected Vice President of Women in Diplomacy organisation and representative of latin american countries to negotiate multilateral and regional cooperation in the UK. During her tenure, she achieved the increase of scholarships awarded by government, foundations and private universities in the UK and Ireland, the hiring of seafarers in multinational shipping companies, the establishment of new UK and Irish companies in Panama to operate regionally and the cooperation from UK gov to projects related to the protection of the environment. Previously, she was Counsellor at the Mission of Panama to the United Nations, where she oversaw the economic commission and led the negotiations of the Development Agenda and the action programmes of the IV World Conference on Women and the World Summit for Social Development. Natalia Royo was also the coordinator for the Rio Group, formed by 14 Latin American countries and was in charge of conciliating the group’s positions before the United Nations and presenting them to the various commissions. She continued her diplomatic career at the Mission of Panama to the Organisation of American States (OAS) during the XXVI General Assembly hosted by Panama and she also worked with the Permanent Mission of Panama to the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO). She spent 8 years at the Ibero-American General Secretariat (SEGIB) based in Madrid where she managed evaluations of the multilateral cooperation programmes among Latin American governments approved at the Ibero-American Summits of Heads of State and Government. She was also in charge of communication and visibilty campaigns and organisation of dialogues between the public and private sector. Ambassador Royo was in charge of Communications Dpt at the CODESPA Foundation for economic and social development in Latin America. Natalia Royo was also Counsellor at the Embassy of Panama in Spain, overseeing political and economic affairs. Excellency Natalia Royo has published articles on Panama in the Fundacion Real Instituto Elcano and a study on the Panama Canal and other alternate routes published in Acta Geographica No. 21 of Paris, France. She studied journalism at the New York University (NYU) in the United States and has a master’s degree on International Relations from the School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) at Columbia University, a master’s degree in Political Communications and a second master’s degree on International Affairs from Fundacion Ortega y Gasset/Universidad Complutense in Madrid, Spain.

Collaboration across the Commonwealth: Overcoming Barriers, Succeeding Together

G100 Caribbean & Commonwealth Meetings, Jamaica-UK 19-20 September 2024 

On Thursday, September 19th, 2024, the University of East London’s (UEL) Royal Docks School of Business and Law (RDSBL) became the stage for a groundbreaking two-day symposium, “Women Overcoming Barriers to Success: A Cross-Sector Narrative Perspective of Hope.” The event, organized by Dr. Doirean Wilson, UEL Associate Professor of Sustainability in Management and G100 Club UK Country Chair of the Higher Education & Industry Connect Wing, ignited a dynamic conversation on gender equity, leadership diversity, and the power of resilience in overcoming professional challenges.

The symposium opened with a moment of pure emotion as Dr. Patti Boulaye OBE, renowned singer, actress, and artist, delivered a stunning rendition of Etta James’ classic “At Last,” setting the tone for two days filled with inspiration and empowerment. Boulaye’s soulful performance received rapturous applause, marking the beginning of an event that would explore the diverse narratives of women leaders who have defied the odds.

The prestigious event was a collaborative effort with the Jamaican High Commission, supported by UEL’s Centre for Innovation Management and Enterprise (CIME), and sponsored by Supply Care Solutions. Guests included ambassadors, thought leaders, entrepreneurs, UEL students, and staff—all eager to gain insights from some of the most distinguished women in leadership today.

Strength of Solidarity: Bridging the gaps, Driving Change

G100 Country Clubs Retreats, Fort Barwara Six Senses, Rajasthan, India 2-5 October & 7-10 October 2024

The Country Clubs Retreats, held in India, from 2-5 October 2-5 and 7-10 October brought over 100 country chairs, region chairs, advisory council members, and global chairs, in empowering togetherness. These momentous gatherings united chairs from diverse countries, fostering in-person connections and consolidating global efforts in the common purpose of empowerment. 
 
The retreat marked a significant milestone, culminating previous efforts and launching a new chapter of collaboration. The retreat also presented opportunities for personal, professional, and collective growth through meaningful connections and networking in mutual support and enrichment. 
 
Participants shared experiences and forged stronger bonds. This unity ignited unprecedented strength, synergy, and a deep understanding that we are not alone, but together in this journey of bridging the gaps; one step at a time, with the powers of Consistency, Consolidation and Consciousness. 
 
We can never underestimate the power of small actions to foster big changes over a period of time, by both incremental and ripple effects. Small, sustained actions accumulate momentum over time, gaining traction for impact and gathering influence for lasting change. 
 
Relating in restful ways opens our hearts and broadens our mind, enables peaceful perspectives, calm communication and creative consciousness – bringing more clarity and awareness, and empowering our choices and decisions with intention and purpose. 
 
As we connect, collaborate and co-create, we further unify and diversify our strengths and resources, consolidating collective power with ever more strength, resourcefulness and resilience. 
 
Cultivating consistency, consolidating strengths, and clearing consciousness empowers us to change the status quo, bridge the gaps and forge new paths with intentional efforts, collective power, and mindfulness.
 
The Power of Solidarity is universal in its power to bridge all kinds of gaps and drive change at multiple levels. When we stand together, work together and build together, every gap can be bridged and no challenge is insurmountable. Solidarity is our strength. Unity is our power.
 
The mode of the retreats began in June 2024 and concluded in October 2024. At the final retreat, a new wing was proposed in the name of “Retreats, Recreation & Restoration,” with the purpose of spreading globally the power of retreating and re-creating, re-mineralising the inner power of the self with rest and restoration.

Founder & President, G100 Club, Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai

content_html:
Empowering Women for Sustainable Growth

G100 Balkans Meetings, Skopje, along with WEF Balkans, 2-3 October 2024

 
The Women Economic Forum (WEF) and G100 Meeting – Balkans 2024, held in Skopje, North Macedonia on October 2-3, 2024, brought together over 350 participants from the Western Balkans, Europe, and beyond. Co-organized by the Women Economic Forum (WEF), G100 Communication Advocacy and Mediation Wing for North Macedonia, and the Association of Women Managers ELIT, the event focused on empowering women in business, fostering leadership, and promoting collaboration among women leaders from various sectors.
 
The forum served as a dynamic platform for women to share their experiences, discuss challenges, and explore opportunities for growth. Key discussions centered around breaking barriers, promoting gender equality in traditionally male-dominated sectors, and building sustainable, responsible leadership for the future.
 
During her address, North Macedonia’s President, Prof. Dr. Gordana Siljanovska Davkova, highlighted that while progress in gender equality is undeniable, much remains to be done. She emphasized the importance of global networks in sharing knowledge, resources, and support systems for women, pointing out that true democracy is measured by how well women’s rights are respected and realized.
 
The forum addressed the urgent need to dismantle barriers to women’s economic participation and leadership. Discussions also focused on ensuring women’s rights go beyond legal frameworks to actual lived experiences and opportunities.
 

Key Takeaways

Throughout the event, participants reaffirmed the importance of empowering women in business to drive long-lasting, positive change. A major concern expressed was the tendency of crisis management to overshadow growth, development, and progress. In a divided world, the forum participants underscored the existential need for responsible leadership and thorough commitment to human rights.
 
Key recommendations for driving progress included:
 
• Enhancing Women’s Economic Participation: Creating policies and programs to support women’s entry into and advancement in the workforce, particularly in leadership roles.
 
• Promoting Gender Equality in STEM: Encouraging women to pursue careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics through scholarships, mentorship, and awareness campaigns.
 
• Sustainability in Business: Integrating Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting into business practices to ensure sustainable growth and corporate responsibility.
 
• Supporting Women’s Health: Investing in women’s health research and care to bridge the gender health gap, thereby boosting economic growth and quality of life.
 
• Networking and Collaboration: Fostering opportunities for women to network, share experiences, and collaborate on solutions.

High-Level Participants and Opening Session Highlights
 
The Women Economic Forum & G100 Meeting – Balkans 2024 was officially opened by Prof. Dr. Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova, President of North Macedonia. The event featured keynote addresses from prominent figures, including Ms. Sanja Bozinovska, Minister of Energy and Mining, as well as the Governors of the National Bank of North Macedonia and the National Bank of Montenegro. Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of G100 and the Women Economic Forum, was also among the distinguished speakers. These high-level participants, along with other influential women leaders from government, business, and civil society, underscored the significance of the event.
 
The forum commenced with a Welcome Address by Her Excellency, Prof. Dr. Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova, President of North Macedonia, followed by a Keynote Speech by Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai on the topic of “Empowering Women in Business for Long-lasting Positive Change.” Opening remarks were delivered by Ms. Lenka Ugrinovska, PhD Honors, Country Chair of North Macedonia, and Ms. Linda Pereira, Global Chair of G100.
 
The opening session set the tone for the event, emphasizing the critical role of women in economic participation and leadership, and laying the groundwork for the discussions and panel sessions that followed.
 

Panel Discussions

Panel 1: Breaking the Glass Ceiling and Shaping the Future of Women in Business
This panel focused on strategies for overcoming gender barriers in the business world. Highlights included:
• Personal Journeys: Panelists shared stories of resilience and triumph as they navigated obstacles to reach leadership positions.
• Mentorship Programs: The panel emphasized the role of mentorship in guiding and supporting women throughout their careers.
• Inclusive Policies: Discussions covered policies promoting gender equality, such as flexible working arrangements and equal pay initiatives.
• Networking and Community Support: Participants highlighted the importance of building strong support networks for women in business.
• Future Trends: The evolving business landscape, digital transformation, and sustainability were recognized as areas offering new leadership opportunities for women.

Panel 2: Women as Catalysts of Sustainable Development and Green Transition
This session explored the pivotal role of women in driving sustainable development and the transition to a green economy. Topics included:
• Empowering Women in Green Industries: Encouraging women to participate in sectors like renewable energy, environmental conservation, and sustainable business practices.
• Gender-Responsive Policies: Advocating for policies that promote women’s leadership in environmental decision-making.
• Education and Training: Providing women with the skills and education needed for green economy jobs.
• Community Engagement: Highlighting the role of women at the local level in leading sustainability projects.
• Role Models and Mentorship: Featuring successful women in green industries and offering mentorship opportunities.

Panel 3: Access to Finance and the Power of Networking
This panel addressed the critical need for access to finance and networking opportunities to empower women entrepreneurs. Key points included:
• Access to Finance: Emphasizing the importance of financial resources, such as loans, grants, and investments, for women to start and grow their businesses.
• Networking: Recognizing the power of networking to create business opportunities and foster collaboration.
• Mentorship: The panel discussed how mentorship can help women navigate business and finance challenges.
• Policy Recommendations: Proposed policies included government-backed funding programs and networking events to support women’s access to finance.

The forum concluded with a strong call for collective action to advance gender equality and sustainable development. Participants stressed the need for continued commitment to gender equality in both policy and practice. Promoting women’s active participation in the economy and leadership roles, supporting sustainability initiatives, and fostering collaboration among women leaders were all highlighted as key priorities for the future.
The Women Economic Forum & G100 Meeting – Balkans 2024 left a lasting impression, reinforcing the importance of women’s leadership in driving economic progress and sustainability for generations to come.

H.E. Jakov Milatović

He is the current President of Montenegro and a leading pro-European politician dedicated to economic reform and European Union integration. Educated in economics with degrees from universities in the UK and Italy, Milatović’s career spans both international finance and national governance. Before entering politics, he held a notable position at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), where he worked on initiatives to bolster economic growth in emerging markets.

In Montenegro, Milatović gained recognition as Minister of Economic Development in 2020, championing policies aimed at reducing poverty, increasing wages, and promoting transparency. He co-founded the Europe Now Movement, a political platform committed to structural economic reforms and advancing EU membership for Montenegro. Elected President in 2023, Milatović continues to advocate for policies that improve living standards, reduce unemployment, and position Montenegro as a competitive economy within the European landscape.

As President, his vision is to deepen Montenegro’s ties with the European Union, ensuring a prosperous and stable future aligned with European values and standards.

content_html:
Women, Earth, Future: A Global Dialogue on Leadership and Sustainable Growth

G100 Leadership Summit, Powered by Women of Wisdom, Albufeira, Portugal, 18-20 October 2024

The G100 Leadership Summit 2024, held from October 18-20 in Albufeira, Portugal, was a remarkable gathering of influential women leaders from around the world, united in their commitment to advancing gender equality and empowering women across various sectors. 
This year’s theme, “Women – Earth – Future,” underscored the vital role of female leadership in building a sustainable, inclusive global future.
 
With the generous support of the Municipality of Albufeira and CARMA CPLP, the Summit featured several distinguished G100 Chairs representing different Wings, alongside influential male allies, all contributing to the event’s success.
The Summit opened with an address from Linda Pereira, G100 Global Chair for Communication, Advocacy & Mediation, followed by welcome remarks from Catarina Olim (Country Chair), a warm video message from Harbeen Arora Rai, founder of the G100, and José Carlos Martins Rolo, Mayor of Albufeira, which set a collaborative tone for the event.
 
Highlights of the Programme: 
The programme was structured around key topics impacting female leadership and social responsibility, including sessions on sustainable economic practices, conflict resolution, and strategic global governance. Keynotes, panels, and workshops explored:
The Summit also facilitated Submitted Speaker Sessions in parallel, featuring Chairs and participants from a wide array of G100 Wings. These sessions covered leadership innovation, empowerment strategies, and sector-specific insights, enabling attendees to gain diverse perspectives.
 
Themes and key insights from the G100 Leadership Summit 2024 in Albufeira:
 
– COMING OF AGE – the advancement of equality around the world: Explored global progress in gender equality, emphasising normalising gender parity as an everyday standard.
– Empowering Women to Think Glocal: How To Thrive in a Globalised World: Encouraged women to integrate global perspectives with local impact, leveraging international opportunities for community benefit.
– Leadership and High-Level Performance – powered by Mental Health: Addressed mental health as a foundation for sustained leadership, highlighting resilience practices for high-pressure roles.
– HR Technology and the Rise of Women in the Workplace: Examined AI and HR technologies as key enablers of women’s career growth, promoting unbiased organisational practices.
– Transformation and Female Leadership in Law: Shared insights on legal reforms driven by women in leadership, focusing on diversity and equity within the legal sector.
– Inner Happiness, Outer Transformation: Women Shaping the Future: Discussed inner contentment as vital for effective leadership, advocating for personal fulfilment over external validation.
– The Office-People Dynamic: How Workspaces Shape Human Interaction and Vice Versa: Explored how workspace design impacts employee well-being, encouraging collaborative, flexible environments.
– Beyond Band-Aids: Creating Lasting Health Solutions through Community and Authentic Harmony: Emphasised community-driven approaches to health, fostering long-term, holistic solutions.
– Female Leadership in ESG Implementation: Strategies for Sustainable Governance: Focused on strategies for women to lead in Environmental, Social, and Governance practices, advocating sustainable governance models.
– The Power Within: Unlocking Female Energy for Authentic Leadership: Highlighted the unique strengths women bring to leadership, particularly through intuition and empathy.
– Your Presence Matters!: Stressed the value of presence and engagement, reminding attendees that each voice contributes to the collective impact.
– REINVENTING OURSELVES – Twilight Careers: Discussed career reinvention at later stages, encouraging resilience and adaptability in evolving industries.
– Living My Dream Through the Camera!: A personal account of how photography enabled self-discovery, shared by a participant as a metaphor for following one’s passions.
– Women and SDGs: The Key for Sustainable Development: Linked women’s empowerment directly with achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
– Cracking The Leadership Life Code – The Power of Authentic Harmony: Promoted harmony-based leadership, where inclusive dialogue and empathetic relationships drive success.
– How Culture Influences Women in Leadership: Examined cultural influences on female leadership styles and the diverse challenges faced by women globally.
– Overcome Fear and Doubt in Career Choices: Encouraged women to address career fears and embrace bold decisions to pursue fulfilling paths.
– Sustainability – Quality of Life for Future Generations: Discussed the need for sustainable business practices to safeguard future generations’ quality of life.
– 4D Leadership – From Self-Awareness to Contribution: Proposed a leadership model emphasising self-awareness, growth, and service as essential qualities.
– Love & Peace in Companies: How to Thrive in Transformation: Presented concepts for nurturing peaceful, productive workplaces amidst corporate transitions.
– Green Transformation of Businesses: Emphasised eco-friendly practices in business, encouraging leaders to champion sustainable transformation.
– Where is the Conflict?: Discussed various conflicts around the world, highlighting the importance of addressing root causes for lasting peace.
– Three Generations of Women in Portugal: A Cautionary Tale: Traced gender equality progress across generations in Portugal, highlighting lessons learned.
– A Roadmap to Your Dreams: A motivational talk guiding participants in creating actionable plans to realise their aspirations.
– Painting Masterclass: An artistic session inspiring creativity as a means of personal growth and stress relief.
– Talk by Exklusiva: A brand-focused discussion showcasing luxury industry insights and brand-building in a global context.
– Financial Literacy for Small Business Owners: Covered essential financial knowledge, empowering women to run successful, financially sustainable businesses.
– Peer-to-Peer Session: Encouraged peer mentoring, where participants shared advice and support, fostering community and shared growth.
– I Confess – To Being an Entrepreneur!: A candid account of entrepreneurial challenges, encouraging honesty and resilience in business.
– Creative Session: Hands-on art and creativity session promoting self-expression as a form of leadership development.
– The Power of a Mission: Explored how purpose-driven leadership creates meaningful, positive impact, urging participants to align personal missions with their professional goals.
 
Throughout the three days, networking sessions, and the Summit Dinner with a keynote address by Dr. António Saraiva (former President of the Portuguese Business Confederation), offered meaningful opportunities for attendees to build lasting connections and foster collaborations.
 
The G100 Leadership Summit 2024 in Albufeira underscored the power of collaborative, values-driven leadership. By uniting voices from around the globe, the Summit facilitated a collective commitment to advancing gender-responsive policies, promoting inclusive practices, and shaping a more equitable world. As we look to the future, the insights and partnerships formed at this year’s Summit will continue to inspire impactful change across industries and communities worldwide.

EMPOWERING LEADERSHIP FOR A BETTER TOMORROW

G100 Online Global Summit: Mentoring & Motivation, 29-30 October 2024

excerpt: H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao H.E. Euphrasie… Read more
content_html:
H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao

H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao

H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao has served as the Minister for the Promotion of Women, Family and Child Protection, and holds a UNESCO chair on their committee on Water, Women and Decision-making. She serves as special advisor in charge of gender to the Honorable President of Côte d’Ivoire. She has been a major player in the development of gender policies in Côte d’Ivoire for more than thirty-five years. She led with great success, the institutionalization of the Gender approach in Côte d’Ivoire, wrote the Gender policy of Côte d’Ivoire in 2007, thus contributing to establishing a framework favorable to the promotion of gender and the empowerment of women. At the continental level, she contributed substantially to the drafting of the African Union Gender policy (2008) and then that of ECOWAS (2009).

H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao is also the National Coordinator of the Compendium of Women’s Skills of Côte d’Ivoire (COCOFCI). Implemented by the UNESCO Chair “Water, Women and Decision-Making Power”, COCOFCI is a presidential program launched on October 4, 2011, at the initiative of His Excellency Mr. Alassane Ouattara, President of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire. As part of the dynamic of further promoting equal opportunities, the Compendium aims to strengthen the visibility of women, regardless of ethnicity, political party, religion, and to encourage their appointment to decision-making positions for greater participation in the management of public and private affairs. Under her leadership, the Compendium was elected, in 2018, by the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), the best African program for the promotion of female skills.

She has served as the Chair of the Technical Advisory Group (GTC), from June 2020 to June 2022, during the development of the SIGI Côte d’Ivoire Report conducted and piloted by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), her mission consisted of supporting the completion of the study on gender discrimination in social norms in Côte d’Ivoire.

Excellency Yao has been a member of the steering committee and the governance committee of the Francophone Observatory for Inclusive Development through Gender (OFDIG). In July 2023, Minister Euphrasie Kouassi Yao was requested by the government of the Republic of Guinea to provide support for the establishment of the Compendium of Women’s Skills of Guinea (COCOFGUI). She

leads a mission to this effect punctuated by meetings at the top of the Guinean State with the head of government, the president of parliament, ministers, technical and financial partners, as well as with the entire network of agencies of the United Nations system.

At UNESCO, she has made a major contribution to promoting equal opportunities, peace and sustainable development. With the UNESCO Chair “Water, Women and Decision-Making Power”, Euphrasie Kouassi Yao worked on the implementation of United Nations Security Council Resolution 1325/2000 on women, peace and security. She designed the CREA-PAIX tools on the empowerment of women and young people in resolving community conflicts, and set up the Bank of Love and Effective Solidarity (BASE) at the height of Covid-19. In 2018, she set up the Gender Engineering Training (FIG) for decision-makers, which brought more than 400 gender experts to the market. She opened within the Félix Houphouët-Boigny University of Cocody, in 2022, the Master in Gender, Economics and Sustainable Water Management aimed at students and which has 35 auditors (18 women and 17 men), before launching in 2020, the Gender and Business Competitiveness Label (GECE Label).

She is also the author of 3 books that are widely used for learning and education. She was a Gold medalist at the 6th International Water Symposium in Cannes in 2004, 2013 National Excellence Award from the President of the Republic of Côte d’Ivoire for the promotion of female skills, because as mentioned in the 2013 Excellence Awards booklet on page 31, “she is at the root of anchoring the concept of Gender in the mentality of Ivorians” and contributes substantially to the promotion of female skills. 

The only woman to hold a UNESCO Chair in Côte d’Ivoire, Euphrasie Kouassi Yao is an international expert consultant in Gender and Development, monitoring and evaluation with agencies of the United Nations system such as UNDP, UNFPA and UN-Women in particular, or the African Development Bank (AfDB). Excellency Yao is an inspiring leader with impactful leadership who pursues the dream of a peaceful world. Through her actions, she impacts and inspires the community, and works to transform society.

Paulina Chotrova

Paulina Chotrova

Paulina Chotrova is an influential leader in technology, business, and innovation. As Group Chief Executive Officer of PSK Group, Paulina drives innovation, digital transformation, and sustainable business practices, ensuring the company stays at the forefront of technological advancements. Her outstanding contributions to the company earned her a spot in the prestigious 40 under 40 award, recognizing her leadership and impact in the industry. As the President and Founder of Women in Deep Tech, she has created a leading platform that supports and promotes women in technology, helping them lead in cutting-edge industries. Through her leadership, she has directly impacted over 10,000 women in science and technology, providing them with the resources, mentorship, and opportunities to excel. Her reach extends to more than 200,000 women working across the IT, innovation, and GIG industries, empowering them to thrive and lead in these rapidly evolving sectors.

In addition to her work with Women in Deep Tech, Paulina is a Google for Startups mentor, helping women entrepreneurs grow and scale their businesses. She is also a Women Techmakers Ambassador, amplifying her mission to champion women’s leadership in technology and innovation globally. Paulina is also the Founder of iSTEB, an organization dedicated to fostering innovation, driving technological advancements, and supporting the growth of the tech ecosystem, creating pathways for greater diversity and inclusion in these fast-paced industries.

With a degree in Computer Engineering from TU Sofia, Plovdiv branch, Paulina’s technical expertise has been key to her leadership and advocacy. She has received numerous awards and recognitions for her work in driving change in technology and empowering women in the tech industry. Through her strategic vision, Paulina remains a powerful force for change, working to create a more inclusive and innovative future for women in technology and entrepreneurship.

excerpt: Dr. Anush Gasparyan Dr. Anush Gasparyan Dr. Anush Gasparyan is… Read more
content_html:
Dr. Anush Gasparyan

Dr. Anush Gasparyan

Dr. Anush Gasparyan is a renowned expert in women’s empowerment from Armenia. With two decades of experience, she is a distinguished authority in the field, with a remarkable track record of advocacy, research, and education.Dr. Gasparyan established the RoMana Center for Women’s Rights and Leadership, a pioneering initiative dedicated to empowering individuals to recognize their rights and supporting organizations in eliminating gender bias and creating harassment-free environments. She specializes in comparative law, bridging insights across diverse legal systems.Her primary academic interests include women’s rights, human rights, and gender discrimination. Her doctoral research focused on working women’s rights, conducting a comparative analysis of Indian and Armenian laws.Dr. Gasparyan is a legal scholar with an LL.B. from the MYUD Institute of Law, Armenia, and holds an MCL and Ph.D. from the Faculty of Law, University of Delhi, India. During her time at Delhi University, she served as President of the International Women’s Student House, representing women from over 100 countries and fostering cross-cultural dialogue and empowerment.An accomplished author and lecturer on gender justice, Dr. Gasparyan has written a book on Women’s Human Rights in India, along with numerous articles and research papers on gender equality, maternity rights, and workplace sexual harassment. Her PhD thesis, “Working Women’s Rights: A Comparative Study of Laws and Practices in India and Armenia,” examines the legal frameworks and societal contexts in both countries, highlighting judicial approaches, identifying gaps, and offering key recommendations.She has designed and delivered workshops globally on topics such as prevention of sexual harassment in the workplace and mainstreaming gender in policy. Dr. Gasparyan has been associated with esteemed organizations, including the National Human Rights Commission of India, Institute of UN Studies in India, Committee of State and Legal Affairs, Public Council of Armenia, Diaspora High Commissioner’s Office (Armenia), and other international institutions.

Sulajja Firodia Motwani

Sulajja Firodia Motwani

Sulajja Firodia Motwani is an Entrepreneur and the Founder and CEO of Kinetic Green Energy and Power Solutions Limited, a company specialising in green mobility solutions. She is also the Vice Chairperson of Kinetic Engineering Limited, which is part of the Kinetic Group, a pioneer in the Indian automotive industry. Sulajja is credited with leading Kinetic’s diversification into clean energy vehicles, including electric scooters, three-wheelers, and small electric vehicles for last-mile connectivity.

Sulajja was born into the prominent Firodia family, known for its contributions to India’s industrial growth. She earned a Bachelor’s degree in Commerce from the University of Pune and later pursued an MBA in Finance and Marketing from Carnegie Mellon University in the United States.

Sulajja began her career in the finance sector, working with investment firms in California before joining the Kinetic Group. Upon her return to India, she played a pivotal role in modernizing the company’s strategies. In 2015, she founded Kinetic Green, focusing on sustainable mobility solutions, which has since become a leader in the electric vehicle space in India.

Sulajja has received numerous accolades for her contributions to the industry, including being named among the “Top 25 Businesswomen of India” by publications such as Business Today and India Today. She has also been widely recognized for her efforts in promoting environmental sustainability through green technologies. She is also invited to speak at various prestigious forums and plays leadership roles at industry bodies such as FICCI, IFGE, NIF, i create and Invest India. 

Sulajja is a fitness enthusiast and has competed at national-level badminton tournaments. She balances her professional commitments with her personal passion for sports, including scuba diving and skiing, and fitness.

title: Ersilia Vaudo
excerpt: Ersilia Vaudo Ersilia Vaudo Ersilia Vaudo serves as Chief Diversity… Read more
content_html:
Ersilia Vaudo

Ersilia Vaudo

Ersilia Vaudo serves as Chief Diversity Officer and Special Advisor on Strategic Evolution at the European Space Agency (ESA), 

She holds a degree in Astrophysics and an executive certificate from the John F. Kennedy School of Government at Harvard Kennedy School.

Over her 30-year career spanning Paris and the USA, she has undertaken numerous roles, including in strategy, finance, and international relations, also serving as Executive Secretary of the scientific-technological committee for the selection of missions to Mars. From 2002 to 2006, she was the Deputy Head of ESA’s Washington, D.C., office, in charge of relations with US and Canada stakeholders, including NASA. She has also served on the Board of Directors of Women in Aerospace US.

Ersilia Vaudo is the President and co-founder of the “Il Cielo Itinerante” Association, which promotes STEM education by bringing “the sky where it doesn’t reach.” Using telescopes  and experiments carried on a minibus, the initiative engages children in disadvantaged areas through hands-on STEM activities.

She is the Vice President of Eurisy, a non-profit association comprising 30 European space agencies, focused on fostering the relationship between space and society.

As an author, Ersilia published “MIRABILIS. An English version, “The Story of Astrophysics in Five Revolutions,” will be available too. In May 2024, she published “Why to Study Physics Is (NOT) Difficult” for schools with Mondadori.

Her contributions extend to design as the co-creator of the “Lune d’acqua” lamp, produced and distributed by Artemide. Ersilia Vaudo also curated the XXIII International Exhibition at the Milan Triennale, “Unknown Unknowns: An Introduction to Mysteries,” held from July 2022 to January 2023.

In 2020, she was part of the Italian government’s Task Force “Women for a New Renaissance”, advising on measures for enhancing the participation of girls and women in research and STEM fields. The proposals were later integrated into Italy’s first National Strategy on Gender Equality.

Ersilia Vaudo was also appointed by President Emmanuel Macron as co-chair of the “Talents and Diversity” table within the Scale-Up Europe initiative, presenting recommendations to the French President in June 2021.

In 2022, she was awarded the title of Commander of the Order of the “Stella d’Italia” by the President of the Italian Republic.

title: Rome, Italy Meetings, along with Annual WEF, 20-23 November 2024.
excerpt: Women United, World United: Together We Can G100 Rome… Read more
content_html:
Women United, World United: Together We Can

G100 Rome Italy Meetings, along with Annual WEF, 20-23 November 2024

 
The G100 meetings were held in conjunction with the Women Economic Forum (WEF) Italy, to empower women in business, foster leadership, and promote collaboration among women leaders from various sectors. The event brought together influential leaders from across the world to share experiences, discuss challenges, and explore opportunities.
 
The panels and meetings celebrated the power of women’s leadership in driving change across economic, social, and cultural landscapes. Over three impactful days, the event brought together over 300 participants and eminent speakers from around the world to share insights and create actionable pathways for progress.
 
The WEF Italy 2023 was held at Luiss Guido Carli University in Rome. The conference opened with inspiring addresses by distinguished speakers, including H.E. Laura Mattarella, First Lady of Italy, and Yulia Svyrydenko, First Deputy Prime Minister of Ukraine, who emphasised the critical role of women in shaping global policies and economic strategies. The sessions covered a diverse range of topics such as sustainable development, digital transformation, and women’s role in building economic resilience.
 
The participants engaged in meaningful conversations, focusing on unity, collective action, and sisterhood to bridge gender gaps and pave the way for inclusive growth. Workshops and interactive sessions created a collaborative platform to exchange best practices and inspire women leaders to take bold steps toward transformation. 
 
Luigi Gubitosi, President of Luiss University, highlighted the institution’s commitment to fostering a culture of leadership and innovation. Paola Severino, President of the Luiss School of Law, lauded the forum for creating a space for actionable dialogue. Piero Colonna, Vice President of Fondazione Roma, expressed pride in supporting such a transformative event. Monica Lucarelli, Councilor for Security Policies, Productive Activities, and Equal Opportunities for the Municipality of Rome, emphasized Rome’s role as a hub for gender equality initiatives. Marilena Citelli Francese, President of WEF Italy, celebrated the forum’s role in advancing women’s contributions to society and the economy. 
 
Prominent leaders discussed the evolving role of women in shaping economies and societies. Chiara Corazza, G20 Empower Representative to France, chaired a pivotal session on the same featuring panelists like Paola Angeletti (Chief Sustainability Officer, Intesa San Paolo) and Fabienne Arata (Country Manager, LinkedIn France). Discussions revolved around breaking barriers and fostering sustainability. 
 
The panel on Climate focussed on actionable steps for climate justice, bringing together experts like Monica de Virgiliis (Chairwoman, Snam) and H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, Former Minister and UNESCO chair holder for Water, Women and Decision-making, who highlighted the critical intersection of gender, policy, and environmental advocacy.
 
Another session explored advancements in health and wellbeing, with insights from Antonella Santuccione Chada (CEO, Women’s Brain Foundation) and Anna Maria Colao (Endocrinology Expert, Federico II University). A special lecture by Vittorio Sebastiano from Stanford Medicine captivated attendees with groundbreaking research on aging.
Sessions on AI, and Space further explored themes shaping our future. The technological transformation was addressed in a session led by Barbara Caputo, Full Professor at Politecnico di Torino. Key speakers, including Floriana Ferrara (IBM) and Giusella Finocchiaro (Alma Mater Studiorum), emphasised leveraging AI for societal good while addressing cybersecurity challenges. Space for Life Leaders in space exploration, including Simonetta Cheli (Director of Earth Observation Programmes, ESA) and Milena Lerario (CEO, e-GEOS), discussed the potential of space technologies to address global challenges.
 
The event “Preparing for the Future: How Education Can Support an Inclusive and Sustainable Democracy” featured a diverse panel of experts. Ersilia Vaudo, an astrophysicist at the European Space Agency, Emma McCoy from the London School of Economics, and Livia De Giovanni from Luiss University discussed the role of education in fostering inclusivity and sustainability. Other notable participants included Staffan De Mistura,( UN, Under-Secretary-General), Chiara Sbarigia(Cinecittà), Patrizia Torchia(La7), and Chiara Moenter (Co-Founder, SDG 18). The discussion centered on how education can help build a more democratic and sustainable future.
 
Strategies for resilient food systems were examined in a session chaired by Sharon Cittone, with contributions from innovators like Simona Caselli (President, Granlatte Coop) and Gladys Morales (IFAD).
 
The forum featured unique cultural experiences, including a private visit to the Vatican Museums and a reception honouring women athletes, emphasising the strength and triumph of women in sports.
 
The final day concluded with an exclusive visit to the Knights of Malta headquarters, leaving attendees inspired and united in their mission to advance gender equity and innovation. 
 
The event united voices from diverse backgrounds, creating a roadmap for a fairer, more sustainable, and inclusive world where women lead as agents of change.
 
A meeting with Hon’ble Ambassador of Mexico in Italy was also organised by the Mexican delegation led by Patricia Gonzalez. 
 
Special thanks to G100 Global Chairs at the event including Annabella Nassetti, Sharon Cittone, Mar Introini, Patricia Gonzalez, H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, Datin Hartini Osman, Diah Yusuf. 
 
Gratitude to Marilena Citelli, and the entire organising team of Musadoc, including Donata and Maria Luisa. The impeccable organisation was testimony to the power of togetherness. Together We Can.

Lamia Hanafi

Lamia Hanafi 

Lamia Hanafi is a Founder & CEO of Nest Accelerator, a visionary leader in global innovation, startup ecosystems, and transcontinental entrepreneurship. An internationally acclaimed entrepreneur and innovation strategist, she is celebrated for bridging startup ecosystems across Europe, Africa, and the Middle East. She has built a remarkable career empowering visionary entrepreneurs, scaling high-impact startups, and advising governments and corporations on innovation-driven growth.

As the driving force behind Nest Accelerator, the first transcontinental innovation hub dedicated to connecting and positioning emerging markets on the global startup map, Lamia is committed to fostering impactful collaborations that place emerging economies at the forefront of global innovation. In her role as Global Chair – Startup Ecosystem & Innovation at the Women Economic Forum (G100), she leads worldwide initiatives advancing female leadership in technology and entrepreneurship.

Previously, as Head of Innovation & Entrepreneurship at Université Mohammed VI Polytechnique (UM6P) France, Lamia conceived and launched NextAfrica — the first transcontinental accelerator program at Station F, the world’s largest startup campus — positioning African innovation on the global stage. Her strategic vision and international network played a pioneering role in establishing the first African university with a global presence at Station F, creating unprecedented opportunities for African startups in Europe.

Since 2016, Lamia has been a leading advocate for mobilizing African and diaspora startup founders, working closely with global institutions to leverage innovation and entrepreneurship as catalysts for sustainable development. Recognized among France’s Top 100 Startups, she co-founded an internationally awarded proptech startup in 2015. Her leadership and influence have been featured in Forbes, Voice of America, MoroccoWorldNews, Bilan.ch, Challenges, ArabLeaders, among others. She has delivered keynote talks at major global forums across Europe, Africa, and the Middle East, inspiring policymakers, investors, and entrepreneurs to embrace innovation as a driver of inclusive growth.

In 2016, Lamia was selected from thousands of entrepreneurs worldwide to join the Global Entrepreneurship Summit at Stanford University, hosted by President Barack Obama, where she was mentored by the Director of Innovation of the White House — an experience that deepened her strategic vision for transcontinental entrepreneurship. In 2025, she was named among Europe’s 40 Under 40 Business Leaders by the Business Elite Awards, honoring her exceptional contribution to global innovation.

A true architect of entrepreneurial education, Lamia has designed and delivered transformative bootcamps and startup programs at leading universities and institutions, equipping thousands of young leaders to launch impactful ventures. Internationally awarded for her achievements in innovation and entrepreneurship, she continues to mentor and advise startups worldwide, building strategic bridges between ecosystems and positioning emerging markets as powerhouses of the global startup economy.

content_html:
Uniting Voices for a Violence-Free Future: G100 Paris Colloquium on Women’s Rights and Advocacy

Paris–French Senate Meetings, 25 November 2024 

On 25 November 2024, International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and Girls, 50 leaders at the G100 network gathered in Paris at an event organised by the G100 wing of Government & Ministerial Advocacy, led by Patricia Elias, in association with Every Woman Treaty. 

G100 Global Chairs from across different wings and from across the world, joined in support, including from Europe, Asia and Africa. The participants included senators, high-ranking officials, former ministers and civil society leaders who shared their insights and inputs on how to strengthen societies globally through treaties and instruments toward eliminating the epidemic of violence against women. 

On the occasion, the discussion centered on further strengthening the CEDAW (Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), through a complementary protocol aimed at bridging the gaps in CEDAW, especially regards compliance and implementation. Other measures were also shared by all for better protection of women’s fundamental rights, especially as the contextual realities such culture and needs are different from to region, and must be taken into account for customising solutions. 

Discussions also focussed on providing universal access to education and health, as these basic rights still remain inaccessible to millions of women and girls worldwide. 

More importantly, organisations such as ours can enable the engagement of top decision-makers, in order to take cognisance of such issues affecting women, so that policymakers and public figures can address these realities and integrate them into their policies for inclusive solutions.

The colloquium was a rich learning experience and exchange with inspiring women leaders from G100, a global network committed to real change. Together, we laid the groundwork for concrete and sustainable actions.

content_html:
Fostering Connections, Empowering ASEAN Exchange

G100 Vietnam Meetings, Ho Chi Minh & Phu Quoc, 29 november, 3 december 2024

We recently had the privilege of visiting Vietnam with a group of Indian business leaders in honour of Dr. Bina Modi, a renowned businesswoman and iconic female leader. Dr. Modi graciously hosted us additionally for a G100 Meet & Greet breakfast at the Park Hyatt Saigon, where we invited women leaders from various walks of life. 

The meet & greet event was attended by around 15 women leaders on November 30th, followed by additional meetings on December 1st and 2nd. We were also joined by Datin Hartini Osman from Malaysia, who leads as G100 Global Chair for the wing of Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication. She shared about the upcoming Women Economic Forum for the ASEAN region in June 2025, and invited women leaders to join in order to strengthen cooperation among ASEAN countries. 

The gathering brought together a diverse group of accomplished women from various fields. Participants included Ms. Nguyen Le Anh, CEO of Life Appreciate Inc.; Ms. Naomi Nga Doan, CEO of MindsVibe Inc.; Ms. Nga, Director of Ben Tre Coop; PhD candidate Nguyen Thi Lan from PetroVietnam University; and several entrepreneurs and business leaders, including Ms. Trieu Thi Huong Thuy, Ms. Joyce Phan, Ms. Jancy Tram Nguyen, Ms. Mi Nguyen, and Ms. Koyama Thao, Founder of Eldoraku Inc. 

During our stay, we also visited the Phu Quo Island, a newly developed island space with extensive infrastructure. We were impressed by Vietnam’s efforts to welcome the world through this unique destination. We explored possibilities for future retreats here with our G100 Retreats, Recreation, and Restoration wing.

We extend our gratitude to Dr. Modi for her warm hospitality and to our new Vietnamese sisters for joining us. This trip marked a wonderful first step in engaging with leaders in Vietnam and learning about the country’s progressive steps towards empowering women in the ASEAN region.

title: Global President
excerpt: G100 Global President A Global President is nominated every year… Read more
content_html:
G100 Global President

A Global President is nominated every year by rotation from among the Global Chairs for a one-year tenure from January 1 to December 31. The Global President retains the portfolio as Global Chair of a wing, while leading as Global President in self-led initiatives. 

The Global President seeks proactive participation from all wings to develop ideas and actions with members worldwide especially in fulfillment of the mandate as shared below. The Global President can further expand the Presidents Advisory Council and also form ad hoc committees comprising leaders from across the G100.

The Global President leverages support from Global Chairs, Country Clubs, the Denim Club, and the Secretariat for planning global outreach and meetings, particularly encouraging annual wing and global summits in coordination with Global Chairs.

The role of Global President includes the following mandate in general, but each incoming Global President can prepare a personal and precise roadmap, selecting spheres of influence that align most with one’s strengths and networks, with strategic synergies and resourcefulness of reach and relationships. 

The Global President leads high-level global meetings and delegations, develops strategic partnerships, and invites influential leaders to the G100, to scale and strengthen our global influence and impact.

The Global President plays a vital role in advancing the group’s ELLEGOSSSE principles on the global stage, specifically for their adoption in policy development across governments worldwide. This is achieved through active participation in intergovernmental fora like the UN, EU, AU, G7, and G20. By engaging with these fora, the Global President helps shape policy agendas, promote international cooperation, and drive progress toward a more equitable and sustainable world.

In addition, the Global President also engages with various collectives such as for parliamentarians, industry, trade, media, think tanks, business, associations, universities, and networks. This multi-faceted approach enables the Global President to foster collaborative relationships, promote knowledge sharing, and drive meaningful change with partners across the board.  

The Global President represents all wings at global events and conferences, signing agreements on behalf of the group. The Global President is the voice of harmony, guided by principles of neutrality, centrality, sorority, and humanity, and adhering to a non-political, non-religious, and non-dogmatic code of conduct.

The Global President works closely in coordination with the Founder on all matters, and relies on the Secretariat for coordination of all Wings, including for Wing Roadmaps, Chair Tenures and Mandates.

The G100 Leadership & Wealth Creation Summit, held on January 12-13, 2025, was an inspiring and transformative event that brought together prominent female leaders to explore topics related to leadership, business growth, and wealth creation. The summit created a space for women to share their experiences, insights, and strategies for success, all while fostering empowerment, connection, and collaboration.
 
The event kicked off with an Opening Session that introduced the vision and mission of G100 from Tove Lovisa Bergkvist, Global Chair of G100 Female CEOs & Wealth Creation Wing, together with Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of G100 and Bodil Valero, President of G100. This distinguished group set a powerful tone for the days ahead, emphasizing the importance of women’s leadership in business and wealth creation. The panel discussion, centered on “Empowering Women to Lead and Succeed,” featured leaders from diverse sectors, who shared their journeys, answered key questions, and discussed how women can be empowered to thrive in leadership roles.

content_html:
Auspices

The five sister platforms – ALL, WEF, G100, SHEconomy, and WICCI – operate under mutual auspices, with ALL serving as the primary platform established in 2011. Like five fingers of the same hand, they work together in solidarity, addressing various aspects of empowerment and bridging gaps to foster a more inclusive and equitable world. To summarise, the five sister platforms are focussed as follows: 

ALL Ladies League (ALL), a global sisterhood platform that embodies the spirit of She-for-She support and Shakti Bandhan, uniting women as “sisters beyond borders.” Women Economic Forum (WEF), a conference platform that amplifies women’s visibility, voice, recognition, and global networking, empowering women to pursue “business beyond borders.” Women’s Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (WICCI), an industry and business chamber driving women empowerment, through actions and advocacy for “policies beyond borders.” G100, a global platform for joint action, accelerating actions for “gender equality beyond borders.” SHEconomy, an e-commerce platform and app that promotes women-owned businesses, strengthening “commerce beyond borders.”

Together, the family of platforms bridge the gaps on various fronts with purpose, partnership and positive spirit. All platforms together ensure women’s advancement in all walks of life with an integrated vision and inclusive values. With a powerful network reaching a million women worldwide, these empowering ecosystems are among the largest global communities of women. Supported by The Denim Club of He for She champions, all platforms cultivate communities in a spirit of All for All. 

Membership to the platforms is free and by invitation only. The platforms are non-political, non-religious, non-dogmatic. They are driven by Core Values of Positivity, Code of Conduct of No Negativity, with the tenets of Support, Sisterhood and Solidarity as the primary organising principles, resting on a vision of the world as One Family.

H.E. Dr. Epsy Campbell Barr is the Former Vice President of Costa Rica. She is the first woman of African descent to be vice president in Costa Rica and in Latin America. Formerly, she was also Foreign Minister of Costa Rica. She has been a member of the Costa Rican National Assembly. Excellency Campbell has been active in Afro-Caribbean affairs since entering politics. In 1996, she founded the Women’s Forum for Central American Integration, which she coordinated until 2001. Concurrently, she also coordinated the Network of Afro-Caribbean and Afro-Latin American Women. Excellency Campbell has published books and articles on democracy and inclusion, political and economic participation of women, people of African descent, sexism, and racism, among other topics. She is an expert in social development issues, political participation of women of African descent, and equality.
