Alexandra Maramenides

Alexandra Maramenides is the Founder of Rêve Agency, a literary and screen agency. A graduate of the University of Cambridge, Alexandra has spent her career at the forefront of the the creative publishing industry, collaborating with leading companies worldwide. She is passionate about global storytelling and building businesses with a powerful purpose.

A commercially driven leader, Alexandra founded Rêve after serving as Managing Director and CEO of publishing houses in the UK and Australia. She brings extensive expertise in leading businesses, specializing in the creation, production, licensing, sales, and distribution of content across various formats and genres. Her strategic vision has fostered successful partnerships and driven the global expansion of renowned publishing brands.

Among her career milestones, Alexandra served as Managing Director of Simon & Schuster UK’s Children’s division, where she championed bestselling authors, illustrators, and debut talents. She also served as Vice Chair of the UK Heads of Houses and held positions on several publishing boards. Earlier, she led businesses within the Bonnier Group, including the launch of Echo Publishing, and worked at leading businesses including Hachette and Phaidon.

A member of YPO (Young Presidents’ Organization), Alexandra served on the Executive Committee for four years, in Melbourne. She is also a Board Director for a not-for-profit association, further extending her commitment to impactful leadership. Alexandra remains deeply dedicated to nurturing creative talent and advancing the future of storytelling.

content_html:
Advancing Global Change: Empowering Women and Fostering Inclusive Leadership

G100 Rijeka, Croatia Meetings, along with women without  PARdon Conference 21–23 November 2024

 
The G100 Rijeka Meetings in Croatia, held from 21–23 November 2024, brought together inspiring leaders and changemakers from across the globe. The event was organized in conjunction with the Women Without PARdon Conference, creating a platform to discuss critical issues, share insights, and foster collaborations.

Highlights of the Event:
Global Participation:
Leaders from diverse sectors participated, including policymakers, entrepreneurs, activists, and visionaries committed to advancing gender equality and societal progress.

Collaborative Discussions:
The sessions focused on pressing global issues such as inclusive leadership, women’s empowerment in governance, economic development, and the role of cross-border cooperation in achieving sustainable progress.

Workshops and Panels:
The conference hosted interactive workshops and panel discussions led by notable G100 chairs, country leaders, and subject-matter experts. Topics included:

The evolution of gender policies in governance.
Strategic planning for building inclusive ecosystems.
Fostering partnerships for sustainable development goals.
Women Without PARdon Sessions:
Special sessions highlighted the achievements and ongoing challenges for women in traditionally male-dominated industries. The conference amplified the importance of breaking barriers through advocacy and collaborative efforts.

Networking and Next Steps:
The meetings served as a networking hub, enabling participants to forge meaningful connections. Key resolutions and roadmaps for future actions were also developed, emphasizing the continued synergy between local and global initiatives.

This landmark gathering reiterated the G100’s commitment to empowering women worldwide while fostering impactful dialogues that pave the way for change.

We extend our gratitude to 
Dr. Gordana Nikolic, G100 Global Chair (Higher Education & Industry Connect Wing), for convening the meetings in synergy and solidarity.

Dr. Maricor M. Malitao

Dr. Maricor M. Malitao

Dr. Maricor M. Malitao is a distinguished leader and accomplished professional, currently serving as the President and Chief Executive Officer of the Standout Group of Companies. Her remarkable passion for excellence is evident in her diverse contributions across scholastic, business, social, and ministry spheres. She is the National President of ARAL (Association for Righteousness Advocacy in Leadership) and the President of the Philippine Haggai Institute Alumni Association (Metro Manila Chapter). Dr. Malitao was also elected as the Vice Chairperson of the Confederation of Asia-Pacific Chamber of Commerce and Industries – Women Entrepreneurs Council (CACCI-WEC) in Japan.

Her leadership extends to the business community, where she holds various influential positions, including President of the Caloocan Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Board Director of the Philippine Association of Service Exporters, Inc. (PASEI). She is also the President of the Tripartite Industrial Peace Council – DOLE – Caloocan and has held leadership roles in multiple civic and professional organizations, such as Assistant Governor of Rotary International District 3810 and President of the Rotary Club of Chinatown-Manila (Dist. 3810).

Dr. Malitao is an accomplished academic, earning a Doctorate in Business Management from the Philippine Women’s University (PWU) and a Master’s degree in Industrial Relations from the University of the Philippines – SOLAIR. She also holds a Master’s in Property Management and Building Administration and an AB in Mass Communication from PWU. Her academic excellence is reflected in her High Pass grade in the Comprehensive Examination for her Master’s in Industrial Relations.

Apart from her academic and professional achievements, Dr. Malitao is deeply involved in community service and ministry. She is the founder and chairwoman of the Lead the Way Foundation and co-founded Koinonia International Ministries and Koinonia International Theological School. She also serves as a broadcaster for the show “Maglingkod sa Panginoon” on DZME 1530 KHZ AM Band, a role she has held since 1995. 

Her entrepreneurial spirit is evident in her membership in the Entrepreneur Society of the Philippines and the Philippines-U.S. Business Council, Inc., among others. Dr. Malitao is also a committed advocate for various social causes, serving as the Chairwoman of the OFW Sandigan Club, Inc. and a board director of the Philippine National Police – Caloocan.

With a strong commitment to leadership, service, and community development, Dr. Maricor M. Malitao continues to make a significant impact in both business and society.

G100 Takes Davos: A Historic First Gathering of Equality Advocates Leading the Intelligent Age

G100 At Davos Week, Davos, Switzerland, 20 – 24 Jan 2025  

Davos Week 2025 marked a historic milestone for the G100 global movement, with nearly 60 participants from diverse nations, including Kazakhstan, Poland, the U.S., Saudi Arabia, Ecuador, Malaysia, Ukraine, and India. This gathering aimed to advance the mission of gender equality, diversity, and shared opportunity. As the first-ever G100 assembly at Davos, the event amplified the voices of nearly 500,000 members committed to systemic transformation.
 
Notable attendees included Vladyslava Magaletska, former Deputy Minister of Food and Agriculture of Ukraine; His Excellency Mr. Luis Gallegos from Ecuador; and Nurhayati Ali Assegaf, President of the Geneva Council for International Affairs and Development (GCIAD). The week offered an unparalleled platform for delegates to share impactful solutions, forge alliances, and advocate for actionable measures to ensure women’s voices are central to shaping the Intelligent Age. Insights from these discussions will culminate in a paper outlining strategies to address systemic barriers and promote inclusivity worldwide.

title: Fadi Georges Comair
excerpt: Fadi Georges Comair Fadi Georges Comair, President, UNESCO-IHP & The… Read more
content_html:
Fadi Georges Comair

Fadi Georges Comair, President, UNESCO-IHP & The Ecomed Academy UNESCO-IHP, Cyprus. Fadi Georges Comair is a professor of applied hydrology, Integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM), and infrastructure at EEWRC (Energy, Environment, Water and Research Centre) of the Cyprus Institute.

Dr. Comair has been the Chairperson of the UNESCO Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP) since 2019. Between 1993 and 2021, he has served as Head Department at the Centre d’Etudes et de Recherches de l’Industrie du Beton (CERIB) in France (1987-1993) and as the President of the Litani River Authority (LRA) and Director General of Water Resources (1993-2021) in Lebanon.

He is the founder of the Water-Energy Environment Research Center (WEERC) at Notre Dame University (NDU). He also contributed to the design and execution of several projects in the field of water management and hydraulic engineering infrastructure.

He acted as the Vice-President of the Euro-Med Water Information System (EMWIS) and the President of the Mediterranean Network of Basin Organizations (MENBO) from 2009 to 2011, developing important activities and partnerships to promote IWRM.

He actively contributed to the water strategy of UfM and also the one of UNESCO IHP –IX, which is entitled” Science for a Water Secure World in a Changing Environment,” for the next decade ( 2022-2029)

Prof. Comair is a water diplomat (DWRE) from the American Academy of Water Resource Engineers (AAWRE) and an international negotiator specialized in Transboundary water in the MENA region. In addition, he initiated the concept of Hydrodiplomcy based on his negotiation experience related to the Jordan River Basin, the Orontus, The Nile, and the Tigres and Euphrates.

He has published around 200 scientific publications, among them authored several books. He is a member of the Academie des Sciences d’Outre-Mer and the Academie de l’Eau in France. He graduated from France, the Ecole Nationale des Ponts et Chaussées(ENPC) and Claude Bernard Lyon I University, with a Ph.D. in Applied Hydraulics and Energy System Engineering.

title: Giorgio Saccoccia
excerpt: Giorgio Saccoccia Giorgio Saccoccia, Senior Advisor to the Director General,… Read more
content_html:
Giorgio Saccoccia 

Giorgio Saccoccia, Senior Advisor to the Director General, European Space Agency, France. Giorgio Saccoccia is the former President of the Italian Space Agency (ASI) and is currently Special Advisor to the Director General of the European Space Agency (ESA), specifically in charge of the management and coordination of the multidisciplinary Basic Activity budget of ESA and other tasks.

Graduated with honours in Pisa (IT) in Aerospace Engineering in 1988, he has cumulated an extensive technical and managerial experience at international level in the space sector, through different positions. He holds as well a Master in Business Administration obtained in Leiden (NL) in 1995. After three years of work in Italy, he joined the European Space Agency (ESA) in 1990 at the European Space Technology Centre (ESTEC) in the Netherlands, covering various functions until April 2019, including being the Head of the Propulsion and Aerothermodynamic Division and the acting Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department, in charge of disciplines such as Propulsion, Aerothermodynamics, Structures, Mechatronics, Life Support, Thermal Control, and managing the ESA Test Centre and several technical laboratories.

Throughout his career, Giorgio Saccoccia has been the promoter and coordinator of a huge portfolio of research and technological development projects that had a significant impact on Europe’s role in various space applications. Possibly the area where his contribution has been essential and internationally recognized is the one of Electric Propulsion, where he had a key role to radically change this technological sector: from an area of pure research to an enabling resource worldwide for new space application to satellites for Telecommunications, Science, EO and, more recently, for advanced Space Transportation and Logistics.

In particular, Giorgio Saccoccia conceived and was then the Project Manager for the development of the Electric Propulsion System of the SMART-1 probe, to date ESA’s only lunar mission.

During his 4 year’s mandate as President of the Italian Space Agency (ASI), from May 2019 to 2023, the Italian resources available for space activities have more than tripled, allowing Italy to strongly strengthen its international positioning in the sector. In particular, he was responsible for the preparation of two highly successful Italian contributions to ESA’s Ministerial conferences in 2019 and 2022. Through a careful reorganization of the Agency, ASI’s staff increased by almost 50 percent, after years of lack of growth. New projects and initiatives have been launched at national level and in bi-multilateral collaboration with other countries. The initiatives launched under Saccoccia’s presidency have pursued various strategic objectives, such as a greater synergy between education, research and industry, a strengthening of the Italian positioning in the world Space Economy and, more generally, the use of Space as a growth accelerator for Europe. Particular attention has been dedicated to initiatives that could significantly boost SMEs and SpaceNewCos.

Particularly attentive to the promotion and advancement of space activities at international level, he has served as member and officer in several Organisations devoted to space.

He is a long-time IAF contributor, advocate, and leading voice, having supported the Federation for about 25 years so far in different functions. He chaired and co-chaired for years the IAF Space Propulsion TC and the Propulsion Symposium at IAC, which became under his coordination one of the top 3 paper contributors. He has been adviser to two IAF Presidents in the IAF Bureau for different subjects. He had a fundamental role in bringing the 75th edition of the IAF International Astronautical Congress in 2024 to Milan (Italy).

He is full Member of the International Academy of Astronautics (IAA) since 2012, Emeritus Member of the French Association of Aeronautics and Space (3AF) since 2017, Associate Fellow of the American Association of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA) since 2006. He also served in the Boards of Directors of the Electric Rocket Propulsion Society (ERPS), the Von Karman Institute for Fluid Dynamics (VKI) and in the technical and Scientific Committee of the Italian Space Agency (ASI) and the Italian Centre for Aerospace Research (CIRA).

He organised and chaired over his career several successful international conferences in the space field.

Mr. Saccoccia has elaborated as author or co-author more than 80 articles published in technical journals and / or presented during major international space conferences.

He dedicates time and enthusiasm to lecturing in the field of space and leadership to Academia and other educational organisations, as support to future generations of space professionals.

As an enthusiastic advocate of Space, in his career he has addressed the challenges, needs, opportunities, decisions, internal dynamics of the space sector and established an extensive network with key stakeholders in the European and International scientific, industrial and institutional contexts. Promotion and support to innovation, diversity, cooperation and growth have been at the heart of his values throughout his career.

For his merits, in 2022 Giorgio Saccoccia was knighted the title of “Commendatore” by the President of the Italian Republic.

Rinawati Prihatiningsih

Rinawati Prihatiningsih is the Co-Partner and Chief Operating Officer of PT Infinitie Berkah Energi, where she drives the company’s mission to provide fuel and energy solutions to diverse industries. She also serves as Principal at CV Hako Mulia Abadi, overseeing property leasing and sales operations. Beyond her business endeavors, Rinawati is deeply committed to women’s empowerment. Since 2019, she has served as Co-Chair of G20 Empower Indonesia, working to advance gender equality and elevate the role of women in business and economic development.  

As Deputy Chair for Manpower, Research, and Development at the Indonesian Business Women’s Association (IWAPI), she leads initiatives in policy development, manpower strategies, and research with a focus on inclusivity. In her capacity as Deputy Head of the Committee for APEC and Economic International Organization at Kadin Indonesia, Rinawati represents Indonesia’s business interests on the global stage, contributing to the shaping of international economic policies and partnerships.  

Rinawati’s expertise and advocacy have made her a sought-after delegate and speaker at international conferences, where she addresses critical global issues such as sustainable development, women’s empowerment, and economic cooperation.  

With a passion for sustainable energy, property management, and fostering international economic collaboration, Rinawati invites like-minded professionals to connect and work towards transformative change.

Advancing Inclusive Innovation and Policy Collaboration for a Sustainable Future

G100 Cross-Wing & Cross-Country Event, Parallel with European Green Party Congress, Dublin, Ireland, 6-7 Dec 2024 & 28 Jan 2025

 
G100 Global Chair Dr. Lizbeth Goodman (CARE Economy, Disability Inclusiveness & Social Innovation Wing) and Bodil Valero (G100 Global President 2025, Global Chair Security & Defence Wing) organized a two-day event in Dublin in parallel with the European Greens Congress in December 2024. This event was conducted in collaboration with SMARTlab at University College Dublin, the Wellcome Trust Reclaim Project, the European Commission, and other partners under the theme:
 
FUTURE GREEN – INCLUSIVE DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION IN THE BIOECONOMY & CLIMATE
 
The timing of the event coincided with the Irish general elections, which posed challenges in securing meetings with government representatives at the originally planned scale. Nevertheless, G100 was provided with a demo booth at the Dublin Convention Centre in the Green Party Congress Exhibition area on December 6. At this booth, we showcased examples of Virtual Reality experiences, educational comics, and organic olfactory scents for Climate Action & the Bioeconomy, including novel VR and Olfactory exhibits created for the Biobeo Project and the VOICE Project, co-funded by the European Commission.

March 2025 marked a significant milestone for G100, as the organization hosted two landmark events dedicated to empowering women leaders, fostering collaboration, and driving economic progress. On March 12, 2025, within the framework of CSW69, G100 facilitated high-level discussions in New York, bringing together esteemed professionals to explore key themes in corporate governance, diversity, and cross-border business partnerships. Shortly after, on March 21, 2025, the G100 USA Business Networking Wing successfully launched its inaugural event, uniting women leaders from various industries to establish strong business networks and mentorship initiatives. These events reaffirmed G100’s mission to create a more inclusive and supportive global business environment for women.
 
The March 12, 2025, meetings in New York, led by Michelle Ferrari (G100 Global Chair, Corporate Boards & Gender Balanced Companies) and Patricia Gonzalez (G100 Global Chair, Human Resources & Talent Development), provided invaluable insights into corporate leadership and the evolving role of women in business. The first session, hosted at PwC, convened over 30 distinguished G100 members, who engaged in thought-provoking discussions on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI). The session emphasized inclusive leadership practices and actionable strategies to foster equitable corporate structures worldwide. Industry leaders exchanged best practices to promote meaningful change, reinforcing the importance of women’s voices in shaping global business policies.

content_html:
G100 Takes Davos: A Historic First Gathering of Equality Advocates Leading the Intelligent Age

G100 At Davos Week, Davos, Switzerland, 20 – 24 Jan 2025 

Davos Week 2025 marked a historic milestone for the G100 global movement, with nearly 60 participants from diverse nations, including Kazakhstan, Poland, the U.S., Saudi Arabia, Ecuador, Malaysia, Ukraine, and India. This gathering aimed to advance the mission of gender equality, diversity, and shared opportunity. As the first-ever G100 assembly at Davos, the event amplified the voices of nearly 500,000 members committed to systemic transformation.
 
Notable attendees included Vladyslava Magaletska, former Deputy Minister of Food and Agriculture of Ukraine; His Excellency Mr. Luis Gallegos from Ecuador; and Nurhayati Ali Assegaf, President of the Geneva Council for International Affairs and Development (GCIAD). The week offered an unparalleled platform for delegates to share impactful solutions, forge alliances, and advocate for actionable measures to ensure women’s voices are central to shaping the Intelligent Age. Insights from these discussions will culminate in a paper outlining strategies to address systemic barriers and promote inclusivity worldwide.
 
The G100 delegation’s presence at Davos represented a significant leap forward in the global conversation on gender parity. Gathering alongside key leaders during the World Economic Forum, G100 members seized the opportunity to participate in decision-making discussions and advocate for women’s critical role in shaping the future. This gathering demonstrated the collective power of a network spanning almost half a million members. Delegates introduced each other’s impactful work, explored cross-sectoral synergies, and shared innovative approaches to building inclusive societies. By fostering dialogue and collaboration, the G100 ensured its mission was not only heard but acted upon during this influential week.
 
Collaboration with the Swiss-Asian Chamber of Commerce
 
A key highlight of the week was G100’s participation in the first-ever meeting of the Swiss-Asian Chamber of Commerce, facilitated by Presidents Mr. Khalil Choudhary and Mr. Roger Leitner. Lucia de Luca, G100 Global Chair for Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation, addressed the Chamber, urging its members to implement inclusive practices within their organizations. She emphasized the need for actionable measures to create more inclusive workplaces and set a future appointment to review progress at the 2026 meeting in Davos.
 
Anila Hussain, CEO & Co-founder of Shenannz, and Liza Seggaya, international human rights lawyer and co-founder of Phenomenal Women Global, presented cooperative projects in Pakistan and Africa, providing tangible examples of inclusiveness and women’s economic participation. This event underscored the G100’s commitment to fostering accountability and measurable impact within the business community.
 
Building a Legacy for the Future
 
Davos Week 2025 was a week of “firsts” for the G100, laying the groundwork for future engagements and long-term impact. The G100 delegation’s debut at Davos showcased the movement’s strength, vision, and unwavering commitment to creating a more inclusive future. These events solidified the G100’s role as a global thought leader in advancing gender equality and corporate transformation.
 
As the G100 prepares to release its paper, the movement continues to build momentum, emphasising collaboration with other global networks to dismantle systemic barriers. Together, the G100 is setting the stage for a future defined by inclusivity, equality, and shared success.
 
Convenor: 
 
The event was convened by Lucia de Luca, G100 Global Chair, Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation. 

We are grateful to the support of Global Chairs based in Switzerland, Anila Hussain (Business Networking) and Dr. Nicoleta Acatrinei (Sustainable Banking & Finance), and Minh Nguyen Cao Nguyet, Vietnam Country Chair (Communication, Advocacy & Mediation) for the organisational support, and all members and sisters who participated from G100 and beyond. Together we strengthen in solidarity and partnership.

Dr. Anita C Powell

Dr. Anita C Powell 

Dr. Anita C Powell is the Founder of the TAPN2U, a movement for Peace and Empowerment. Anita received the prestigious US President’s Lifetime Achievement Award in 2024. She was also honored with a Tribute from the Governor of Michigan for her impactful peace initiatives, culminating in the founding of a Global Peace Day. As the visionary behind the Global TAPN2U Peace Partner Movement, Anita is dedicated to fostering peace and unity worldwide.

Driven by her mission to champion inner and global peace, Anita believes that Inner Personal Enhancement is key to the betterment of self, the world, and humanity. Through coaching, consulting, volunteering, and speaking, especially with outreach to young people, she shares her transformative message of empowerment, self-awareness, and peace.

Through another transformative platform, The Awareness Shift, Anita empowers individuals to elevate energy, self-awareness, and conscious living. The initiative features programs like Universal Pulse Weekly Vibrations, Beyond the Mirror narratives, Self-Awareness Narratives, and The Energy Exchange Podcast, focusing on creating purpose, peace, and possibilities. Her philanthropic efforts include raising funds with Sisters Supporting Sisters for buildOn.org to establish a school in the KonduiB. Community of Burkina Faso, West Africa.

Anita is also a published author, with works like YOU – Your Own Universe, available in English and Albanian (attributed to Prof. Dr. Shpresa Delija – Tirana University), Reflections of an Angel (Four Editions), The Divine Feminine – My Relationship with God (global anthology), and Universal Verses – Words to Inspire Peace & Hope (an ESWP global anthology).

Anita is a proud mom and grandmother, an accomplished Energy Principle Practitioner, and a Metaphysical Coach and Consultant specialising in self-awareness and inner peace. Additionally, Anita serves as a Human Rights Consultant, Michigan Unemployment Appeals Advocate, and Rare Disease Advocate.

An award-winning international spoken word artist, poet and passionate speaker, Anita holds a Doctorate in Metaphysics and a Doctor of Philosophy, Honoris Causa, from Jharkhand Rai University in India.

Wealth Creation Summit: Fostering Collaboration and Strategies for Success

G100 Online Leadership & Wealth Creation Summit, 12-13 January 2025

The G100 Leadership & Wealth Creation Summit, held on January 12-13, 2025, was an inspiring and transformative event that brought together prominent female leaders to explore topics related to leadership, business growth, and wealth creation. The summit created a space for women to share their experiences, insights, and strategies for success, all while fostering empowerment, connection, and collaboration.

The event kicked off with an Opening Session that introduced the vision and mission of G100 from Tove Lovisa Bergkvist, Global Chair of G100 Female CEOs & Wealth Creation Wing, together with Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of G100 and Bodil Valero, President of G100. This distinguished group set a powerful tone for the days ahead, emphasizing the importance of women’s leadership in business and wealth creation. The panel discussion, centered on “Empowering Women to Lead and Succeed,” featured leaders from diverse sectors, who shared their journeys, answered key questions, and discussed how women can be empowered to thrive in leadership roles.

Participants then engaged in a series of breakout sessions, each tailored to different aspects of leadership and business development. These sessions included “Mentoring in Action” with Maria Chishti, and “Innovation & Creativity in Business” with Camilla Kristiansen, which sparked meaningful discussions and provided valuable takeaways for attendees.

The networking session following the breakout discussions allowed participants to connect and exchange ideas, building valuable relationships with other like-minded leaders. The day concluded with a Closing Session, where participants shared their key takeaways and “AHA” moments, reflecting on the knowledge gained and the inspiration drawn from the summit.

On Day 2, The event started with an Opening Session that introduced the vision and mission of G100 from Tove Lovisa Bergkvist, Global Chair of G100 Female CEOs & Wealth Creation Wing together with Yash Ranga, Denim Partner of G100 Female CEOs & Wealth Creation Wing. The summit continued with another series of breakout sessions, including topics such as “Global Networking” with Dana Mufleh, “Public Speaking for Business Growth” with Richa Chandra, “Awakening Your Inner Strength: A 5 Step Journey to Resilience and Empowerment” with Angela Morales, “Strategic Influencing” with Dr. Elizabeth Coffey, and “Wellness Advantage: The Role of Wellness in Women’s Entrepreneurial Journey” with Yunche Wilson.

The panel discussion on Day 2, centered on “Elevating Women with Strategic Success,” brought together influential leaders who shared their expertise on leveraging strategy to propel women into positions of greater leadership and influence. These sessions provided attendees with practical tools to grow their leadership capacity, enhance their business skills, and maintain personal well-being as they pursue their professional goals.

The second day also featured opportunities for further networking and interaction, followed by a final Closing Session where participants again shared reflections, insights, and personal experiences, reinforcing the community created during the event.

The summit’s structure facilitated smooth participation, with breakout rooms allowing for interactive discussions and meaningful engagement. Participants were also encouraged to exchange contact information via a shared Google spreadsheet and join a WhatsApp community group, further solidifying the bonds created during the event.

The G100 Leadership & Wealth Creation Summit was a resounding success, offering women in leadership the tools, support, and network needed to thrive. It showcased the power of women supporting women and highlighted the collective strength that emerges when we come together to share knowledge and empower one another. As participants continue their leadership journeys, the summit’s impact will resonate, sparking ongoing growth, collaboration, and success.

G100 Global Chair Dr. Lizbeth Goodman (CARE Economy, Disability Inclusiveness & Social Innovation Wing) and Bodil Valero (G100 Global President 2025, Global Chair Security & Defence Wing) organized a two-day event in Dublin in parallel with the European Greens Congress in December 2024. This event was conducted in collaboration with SMARTlab at University College Dublin, the Wellcome Trust Reclaim Project, the European Commission, and other partners under the theme:
 
FUTURE GREEN – INCLUSIVE DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION IN THE BIOECONOMY & CLIMATE
 
The timing of the event coincided with the Irish general elections, which posed challenges in securing meetings with government representatives at the originally planned scale. Nevertheless, G100 was provided with a demo booth at the Dublin Convention Centre in the Green Party Congress Exhibition area on December 6. At this booth, we showcased examples of Virtual Reality experiences, educational comics, and organic olfactory scents for Climate Action & the Bioeconomy, including novel VR and Olfactory exhibits created for the Biobeo Project and the VOICE Project, co-funded by the European Commission.
 
The activities were led by G100 Dr. Lizbeth Goodman, G100 Tara O’Neil, Country Chair Canada for Resilient Rural Communities and Senior Advisor to the Care Economy Wing Globally, and Bodil Valero, spearheading collaboration with the European and Global Greens.
 
The event provided an excellent opportunity to engage with Irish politicians, parliamentarians, and Green Party members from across Europe, as well as leadership figures from the European Green Party.
 
We also organized a G100 Multi-Wing Meet and Greet over tea at the Spencer Hotel, near the Dublin Convention Centre. The discussions focused on our collaborative approach, potential joint initiatives, and the necessity of expanding cross-wing activities.
 
On December 7, Dr. Lizbeth Goodman conducted a participatory workshop alongside G100 members Dr. Colin Keogh (Care Economy Wing Denim Partner) and Dr. Tara O’Neil at University College Dublin’s International Village. Participants engaged deeply in futures thinking with a real-world impact, and another workshop for G100 is planned in the near future.
 
Follow-Up Meeting on January 28: Strengthening Collaboration
 
The group reconvened in Dublin on January 28, where they presented G100 and the ELLEGOSSSE framework to the board of the African European Parliamentarians Initiative.
 
The ELLEGOSSSE framework stands for Education, Legislation, Leadership, Empowerment, Governance, Ownership, Security, Sustainability, Solidarity, and Equality. It serves as a comprehensive roadmap for gender equality and empowerment through 100 strategic recommendations, divided into 10 recommendations under each of the 10 focus areas.
 
During this follow-up session, the G100 group also had the opportunity to meet with former Labour Minister Brendan Howlin. Additionally, the group broadened its outreach, engaging more individuals interested in learning about G100, thus expanding awareness and strengthening support for the mission.

excerpt: G100 Secretariat G100 is a public charitable trust registered in… Read more
content_html:
G100 Secretariat

G100 is a public charitable trust registered in India. Membership is free, albeit by invitation only. The G100 Secretariat serves as the central coordinating body for the workings of the G100. The Secretariat is funded by the Founder and her foundations. The Secretariat works closely with the Founder and Global President on all matters. The Secretariat is led by a Director General, who is in-charge of overseeing operations across all wings, particularly the following actions: 

Wings Coordination and Support:

  • Acts as the primary point of contact for all G100 activities, ensuring communication and collaboration among Global Chairs, Country Chairs, State Chairs, Advisory Councils, Country Clubs. 
  • acilitates the development of high-level global meetings, and features them on website and socials. 

Wings Leadership and Governance:

  • Oversees the nomination, appointment, and transition of chairs across all levels, Viz. Global, Country, State, City, and for advisory and other members. 
  • Manages the formalization, review, and termination of roles, as well as wing mergers or closures.
  • Ensures compliance with the G100 policies. 
  • Addresses any disputes and disruptions, upholding the code of conduct. 
  • Guides workings on the founding principles of sisterhood and distributed leadership. Sisterhood gives us the glue of solidarity to work with multiple levels of leadership across cultures and continents, weaving a resilient framework of community through voluntary service, leadership and initiatives. Distributed leadership ensures that we all thrive with shared duties and multiplied outcomes. 
  • Safeguards the spirit of commitment, dedication, integrity as a sine qua non at the network, where everyone cares to connect, communicate and contribute, in a spirit of responsibility, responsiveness and raising the bar. 

Wings Strategic Vision and Roadmap:

  • Provides the overarching vision for each wing, while receiving roadmaps from respective chairs on their strategies to address both quantitative and qualitative goals, around the main mandate of each chair creating an engaged community of 100 members. 
  • Ensures follow-through with all chairs for their strategic steps in pursuance of their roadmaps comprising goals and outcomes.

Wings Awards and Recognition:

  • Coordinates the conferral of G100 Awards by the Global Chairs. 
  • Provides awards guidelines, awards templates, and facilitates the process. 

Wings Presence on Website and Branding: 

  • Seeks regular updates from all chairs. 
  • Updates the G100 website with latest wing information. Any chair not featured on the G100 website is not deemed a chair. 
  • Supports with wing logos, social media banners, e-stationery, formal letters and other branding resources to support outreach.

Wings Collaboration and Synergy: 

  • Facilitates collaboration among wings, promoting synergy through peer sharing and exchange. 
  • Connects country clubs, led collectively by the country chairs across wings in a given country, in the empowering presence of the resident global chair.
  • Connects wings with prospective new members and potential partners to explore synergies. 

Wings Personnel Management:

  • Manages in consultation with the founder all the roles regards invitations, withdrawals of invitations, tenure terminations, resignations, or recusals, including change of non-performing chairs and appointing new ones.

G100 Riyadh Meetings, Along with Women Economic Forum (WEF) – GCC, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, 16-18 April 2025

The G100 Riyadh Meetings, held alongside the Women Economic Forum (WEF) – GCC from April 16–18, brought together a powerful coalition of global leaders and entrepreneurs committed to advancing women’s economic empowerment. It was a transformative experience, offering eye-opening insights into Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 and the country’s bold reforms. 
 
From government policies to entrepreneurial opportunities, it became clear that the Kingdom is making significant strides in empowering women through education, employment, engagement, and leadership. It is notable that the female labor force participation has reached 35.3%, already exceeding the Vision 2030 target. Even more impressive, 45% of SMEs are led by women, and 40% of total startups are women-owned – figures that outpace those in many European countries. 
 
Saudi women are now taking on decision-making roles in both government institutions and the private sector, actively contributing to the nation’s development and economic transformation, leading as change-makers in a future-focussed nation eager to connect, collaborate, invest, and grow.

title: G100 Maha Kumbh – India Women’s Summit & Retreat, 7-9 February 2025.
excerpt: Maha Shakti Kumbh 2025: Awakening the Shakti Within with Courage,… Read more
content_html:
Maha Shakti Kumbh 2025: Awakening the Shakti Within with Courage, Confidence & Confluence.

G100 Maha Kumbh – India Women’s Summit & Retreat, 7-9 February 2025

The Maha Shakti Kumbh India Women’s Summit & Retreat, held in the sacred embrace of the Maha Kumbh 2025 in Prayagraj, was a profound gathering of spiritual and social transformation.
 
The Summit itself took place in Parmarth Niketan Ashram’s Kumbh Camp, which was truly inspiring in its commitment to being eco-friendly—an example to emulate in taking care of both people and the planet.
The summit centered on the powerful themes of Shakti (Power), Samannata (Equality), and Samriddhi (Prosperity), bringing together over 100 participants and women leaders from diverse backgrounds, including public life, business, education, and wellness, who gathered in spiritual fervour to amplify the voice and agency of women in shaping a more just and inclusive world where all can thrive. 
 
Set against the sacred backdrop of the Triveni Sangam, the confluence of the holy rivers Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati, the summit facilitated deep dialogues, spiritual practices, and collective action aimed at strengthening both the self and society. Summit participants also experienced holy dips at the Triveni Sangam (confluence of the three rivers), engaged in yoga, meditation, and devotional practices such as havan (holy fire ritual) and kirtan (collective singing), drawing strength from the timeless spiritual fervour of the Maha Kumbh, a hallmark event in India’s ancient and abiding spiritual legacy. This mammoth spiritual event and human saga of devotion is also recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage. Held every 12 years, it attracts an estimated 500 million visitors.
 
The event was inaugurated by esteemed dignitaries and eminent personalities, including: 
• Dr. Sadhvi Bhagwati Saraswati, Spiritual Leader and President of the Divine Shakti Foundation. 
• Shri Arjun Munda, Former Union Minister and Ex-Chief Minister of Jharkhand. 
• Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder, G100
• Priyanka Chaturvedi, MP, Rajya Sabha
• Aditi Singh, MLA and Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly
• Ira Chaturvedi, Yoga Acharya and Wellness Expert
• Parul Sharma Jesudasan, Group President of Reliance Group (ADA), among others 
• Vinay Rai, Founder, Zero Hunger Mission 
 
Pujya Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati highlighted the privilege of participating in the Kumbh Mela, emphasizing that, “Women’s empowerment is not about making women powerful; women are inherently powerful. It’s about recognizing and acknowledging that strength within.” Shri Arjun Munda underscored the importance of preserving the energy that sustains life and the unique wisdom that Indian culture offers in maintaining the balance of life. He spoke of the deep connection between nature and the tribal community, describing how their energy and wisdom are a vital part of India’s strength. Vinay Rai remarked, “Prayagraj can become a super destination for spiritual healing and upliftment year-round and not just during Kumbh, as it now has fabulous infrastructure.” Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai elaborated, “The celebration of Maha Shakti Kumbh is a profound tribute to the Nari Shakti, the feminine power that embodies the sacred principles of nature and nurture. Just as the rivers at Triveni Sangam symbolize care, cleansing, power, purification, love, and life, may we honor the divine feminine within and around us.”
 
A symbolic tree-planting ceremony was held, reinforcing the deep connection between Mother Nature and the Divine Feminine, emphasizing that nurturing the environment goes hand in hand with empowering women in society. The Ganga Aarti Pledge brought together eminent women leaders—including cultural icons, entrepreneurs, and social reformers—who reaffirmed their commitment to advancing gender transformation and empowerment.
A significant highlight of the event was the launch of the book Shakti Sutras: 108 Sutras for Peace and Prosperity by Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai and Vinay Rai. This book serves as a guiding light for those seeking transformation through ancient wisdom and modern insights.
The Maha Shakti Kumbh India Women’s Summit & Retreat was not just a moment of reflection but a spark for long-lasting impact. Plans are underway for follow-up gatherings and collaborative initiatives to ensure these conversations lead to meaningful change.

We extend our heartfelt gratitude to our partners—Parmarth Niketan, GIWA, and WICCI—for their unwavering support in making this vision a reality. Together, we are not just celebrating women’s power but awakening a collective force of courage, confidence, and consciousness that will transform our world for generations to come.

Convenor

Sadhvi Bhagwati Saraswati 

G100 Global Chair, Healing Circles Wing

excerpt: Redefining Global Security: Inclusive Strategies for a Safer Future G100… Read more
content_html:
Redefining Global Security: Inclusive Strategies for a Safer Future

G100 at Munich Security Conference, Bavaria, Germany, 14 -16 Feb 2025

The 61st Munich Security Conference (MSC) marked a pivotal moment in global diplomacy and security, reflecting a stark and urgent reality. This year, the discussions were not just about military conflicts but also about the new and evolving threats to democracy, cybersecurity, and global stability. The G100 Delegation was honored to be part of this transformative dialogue, bringing diverse perspectives to the table and advocating for inclusive security strategies.
The G100 Delegation, which I had the pleasure to coordinate, was composed of professionals from diverse backgrounds who actively engaged in discussions and side events, ensuring that gender, civil society, and youth perspectives were represented in the debate. At a time when security concerns extend beyond traditional military conflicts, our presence highlighted the necessity of inclusive and forward-thinking security policies.
A blatant aspect of MSC 2025 was the underrepresentation of women, young professionals, civil society organizations, and academia in security dialogues. Security is no longer just a matter of “peace or war”—it now encompasses cyber threats, disinformation, and AI-driven attacks. The G100 Delegation advocated for a broader and more inclusive approach to security, one that recognizes the evolving nature of conflict and prioritizes protecting vulnerable populations from emerging threats.
New Battlefields: Cybersecurity and Disinformation
Today’s conflicts are no longer confined to physical battlegrounds. Cybercriminals, often acting as proxies for larger state or non-state actors, weaponize data and information to undermine democracies. Personal health data, financial records, and even critical infrastructure systems are now targets of cyber warfare. These threats raise urgent questions: Are public institutions equipped to combat these evolving dangers? Do we have the expertise to address cybersecurity challenges at the governmental level? How can private-sector collaboration strengthen national and international security?
Public-Private Cooperation: A Necessity, Not a Choice
One of the key discussions at MSC 2025 revolved around the collaboration between the military and private sector in intelligence and data-sharing. With private companies operating most of the world’s logistics, transport, and communication systems, their role in national security is more critical than ever. The Foreign Policy Emerging Threats Forum and the “Catch Me If You Can: Cyber Edition” discussion at Amerikahaus explored whether such cooperation is feasible and how it can be implemented effectively.
Lieutenant General Michael Vetter, Director General and Chief Information Officer at the German Federal Ministry of Defense, emphasized that military-private sector cooperation is not just an option—it is a necessity. The reliance on private companies for critical infrastructure, particularly in sectors like connected vehicles and telecommunications, underscores the need for robust cybersecurity measures and collaborative strategies.
Challenges to Global Democracy
With 68 democracies now outnumbered by 74 autocracies worldwide (Bertelsmann Report), MSC 2025 highlighted an urgent shift in the global order. As Dr. Nathalie Tocci, Director of Istituto Affari Internazionali, pointed out, the world is no longer facing a simple division between democratic and autocratic regimes. Instead, hybrid “autocratic democracies” are challenging the rule of law and redefining governance norms.
The protests on the streets of Munich during the conference also reflected this tension. While some groups demonstrated against NATO and the arms industry, others rallied in support of Ukraine, demanding continued military and financial aid for Kyiv. These events underscored the complexity of modern security challenges and the need for unified international responses.
A Call for Action
The G100 Delegation’s participation in MSC 2025 reinforced our commitment to fostering inclusive, innovative, and cooperative solutions to global security challenges. We extend our gratitude to Priscilla Schelp for facilitating our engagement and to Amerikahaus for hosting critical discussions on cybersecurity and emerging threats.
As we move forward, the G100 remains dedicated to ensuring that security policies reflect the diverse realities of today’s world. The future of global security depends on collaboration, adaptability, and inclusive leadership—values that the G100 proudly champions.
A special thank you to Priscilla Schelp for making the presence of the G100 Delegation possible and to Amerikahaus for welcoming us!
 
Convenor: 
Lucia de Luca
Global Chair 
G100 Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation Wing

content_html:
Guillermo Reina

Guillermo Reina is the Executive Director of CTAUN (The Committee on Teaching About the United Nations) since 2017. 

Guillermo’s contributions to education have been widely recognized, including the prestigious Excellent Teaching Education Award from the United Nations, New York City Headquarters, in 2028. His dedication to international education and global engagement continues to shape his work in and out of the classroom. A Spanish Language Teacher at Somerset County Vocational and Technical High School since 2015, he was honored as Teacher of the Year for the 2022/2023 academic year. 

An accomplished educator, executive coach, and organizational leader, Guillermo has a strong background in industrial engineering and business administration. Holding dual citizenship from Colombia and the United States, he has built a distinguished career in education, coaching, and international engagement. He earned an associate degree in Industrial Technology and a Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering in Colombia before completing a Bachelor of Arts in Business and an MBA from Fairleigh Dickinson University in the United States.

He holds multiple professional certifications, including a Career and Technical Education (CTE) Teacher of Engineering Technology, Spanish Language, English as a Second Language, and Bilingual Bicultural Education, all granted by the Department of Education of New Jersey. He also teaches ESL at Raritan Valley Community College and Union County College, helping students develop language skills for academic and professional success. Additionally, he is a certified Executive and Organizational Coach from New York University and an ISO 9000 Quality Manager, certified by ICONTEC Colombia and FUNIBER Spain.

Beyond his professional commitments, Guillermo enjoys landscape and nature photography and traveling to diverse destinations, including Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Bermuda, Greece, Italy, France, Portugal, and Iceland. A firm believer in the power of kindness and positive influence, he draws inspiration from the words of Maya Angelou and Leo Buscaglia. A proud member of a large Hispanic family, he resides in Mendham, New Jersey, with his wife and beloved pets—Mike, a dog; Murray, a cat; and Bogart, a Senegal parrot.

Dr. Savita Sengar

Dr. Savita Sengar

Dr. Savita Sengar, Chancellor of Jharkhand Rai University (JRU), India, is a distinguished academician, an accomplished academic administrator, and an architect by education.

Dr. Sengar is dedicated to bridging the gap between education and community development. She actively works to make skill-based learning accessible to students across Jharkhand and neighboring states, ensuring they are equipped with industry-relevant knowledge. 

As a thought leader in the education sector, Dr. Savita holds several other leadership positions of eminence and influence. She is a member of the Board of Management of a Central University in Lucknow, nominated by the Hon’ble President of India. Additionally, she serves on the Board of Governors of the Board of Practical Training Eastern Region, Ministry of Education, Government of India, and is a member of the Governing Council of the Association of Indian Universities.  

Dr. Sengar’s exceptional leadership and unwavering dedication to education have earned her numerous prestigious awards and accolades. She was recognized as the Outstanding Leader of the Year (2017) by the Centre for Education Growth and Research (CEGR) for her remarkable contributions to academia. In 2022, she was honored among the Women of the Decade at the Women Economic Forum (WEF) for her impactful leadership in education. Her contributions to education have also been recognized through prestigious awards such as the Guru Shiksha Samman (2016) and *Guru Shiksha Samman (2015), both awarded by Dainik Bhaskar for her outstanding work in the field.

Under Dr. Sengar’s visionary leadership, earlier as Vice Chancellor of Jharkhand Rai University, the institution has flourished as a center of excellence, innovation, and industry collaboration.

A visionary leader in the fields of education and sustainable development, she is a passionate advocate for inclusive, skill-based education and is deeply committed to ensuring “education for all.” With a special focus on girl child education and the empowerment of students from underserved backgrounds, she works tirelessly to ensure inclusive access to quality learning opportunities.

content_html:
Advancing Global Solidarity for Gender Equality: Strengthening the Power to Overcome

G100 India Meetings, Delhi & Ranchi, India 26 Feb – 2 Mar 2025

 
In Delhi, on February 26, H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, Former Minister of Cote D’Ivoire, and G100 Global Chair for First Ladies Outreach met with the Hon’ble Smriti Irani, Former Minister of Women and Child Development. They discussed approaches to bridging the gender gaps, and continuation of their collaboration, especially at the upcoming UN CSW events. The day concluded with G100 Awards and gala dinner hosted by the Ambassador of Côte d’Ivoire, H.E. Mr. Eric Camille N’Dry. The event was attended by diplomats, dignitaries, and influential women leaders.

On March 3, H.E. Euphrasie led three key meetings in New Delhi with: 
  • Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Delegation, for exploring partnership opportunities.
  • Shamika Rai, Special Advisor to the Prime Minister of India, for collaborations on gender-related initiatives.
  • Country Director at the World Bank Headquarters, centering on gender promotion.

In Ranchi, meetings were held on February 27 and 28. A Global Leaders Lunch was hosted by Jharkand Rai University at the Radisson, welcoming Dr. Epsy Campbell, former Vice President of Costa Rica and G100 Global Chair for the wing of International Affairs, along Ms. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, and Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder, G100 Club of Global Women Leaders. 

The event saw participation from prominent women leaders, including politicians, social workers, and entrepreneurs. They shared their thoughts and experiences, highlighting the importance of women’s empowerment, entrepreneurship, and social change. Smt. Meera Munda, a prominent figure in Jharkhand politics and supporter of tribal welfare, women’s empowerment, and sustainable evolution, and Dr. Neera Yadav, ex-education minister, Government of Jharkhand, were also present to advocate for equity and encourage women’s participation and leadership in all walks of life. 

Many recognised leaders also attended the program, including Ragini Singh, MLA from the Jharia constituency; Purnima Mahato, a renowned Indian archery coach and former archer; Aruna Tirkey, Founder and Managing Director of Ajam Emba Private Limited, a pioneering initiative committed to reviving and mainstreaming Jharkhand’s rich indigenous food culture; Usha Jalan, National Vice President, Ekal Abhiyan; Dr. Mini Sharan, Director of Sharan Path Lab; Sarita Pandey, Chairperson & Director of Bhimbirsa Immense, who also serves as the Chairperson of the Women’s Wing at PHDCCI, Ranchi, and Laghu Udyog Bharti; Sangeeta Sharma, Gold medalist in Air Pistol Shooting at the state level; and Manita Gupta, an entrepreneur who owns a retail garment business with the objective of empowering underserved rural women and strengthening their financial condition. 

Key discussion topics included promoting tribal women’s economic empowerment, increasing women’s participation in business and market-based systems, and supporting health, sports, and indigenous art, culture, and products. The leaders’ insights emphasised that women worldwide are committed to shaping their future in a way that drives societal progress as well, placing women’s leadership and women-led development at the heart of inclusive economic growth. A key takeaway was also the incredible importance of having support and solidarity among women, toward preventing burnout and avoiding overwhelm, empowering one’s energy and endurance. 

Addressing the gathering, H.E. Dr. Epsy Campbell said that women across the world are connected through their challenges and therefore, need to find solutions collectively. Echoing the same, and giving a clarion call to action, H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, gave a stirring slogan: “The Time is right, The Time is Now,” which was received with much enthusiasm by all present. Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai elaborated that the G100 platform brings together women leaders from across the world in all walks of life, toward promoting global solidarity for gender equality. She added that women have immense innate power, and indeed, when women come together to help and support one another, all can tap into their greater inner strength to overcome challenges and rise above. 

Later, Ms. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao called upon Shri Hemant Soren, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Jharkhand, to discuss ongoing women’s empowerment initiatives and their amplification through global networks.

On February 28, 2025, the G100 women delegates attended the 5th Convocation Ceremony of Jharkhand Rai University, where three G100 Global Chairs were awarded Honorary Doctorates (Honoris Causa) for their excellence in their respective fields. H.E. Dr. Epsy Campbell, in her acceptance remarks, congratulated the graduates and stated, “I’m here because of my journey with people who believe in possibilities to build together a better world. Between us, women and men, with equal rights, we need to build a new world, working without borders, by being a global tribe.” H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, in her acceptance speech, appreciated Jharkhand Rai University’s efforts to ensure quality education for all in the state. Sulajja Firodia Motwani, Vice-Chairperson of Kinetic Engineering Limited, in her acceptance remarks, expressed her passion for working towards green energy, training and employing women in the energy sector, and creating a safer, greener world for future generations. After the convocation, the dignitaries enjoyed a traditional Indian Thali Lunch. The international guests also then spent a day in Rajasthan at the picturesque Six Senses Fort Barwara, immersing themselves in India’s vibrant culture and warm hospitality.

Overall, the meetings emphasised the need for sustained efforts to promote gender equality and empowerment, and for women leaders to continue working together to drive positive change. The various G100 meetings worldwide continue to enable these objectives through high-level meetings with policymakers and decision-makers, along with partnerships with a range of institutions, toward finding solutions collaboratively to address common challenges, and promote a more inclusive and equitable society.

We are most grateful to Dr. Savita Sengar, former Vice Chancellor, and now Chancellor of Jharkhand Rai University, as also G100 Global Chair for the wing of Universities & Thought Leadership for her utmost support, gracious care and unwavering leadership. We are also deeply thankful to the entire team at the university for their impeccable organisation and stellar spirit of service. Truly, together we can. 

Convenor: 
Dr. Savita Sengar
Chancellor, Jharkhand Rai University, Ranchi, India
G100 Global Chair Universities & Thought Leadership Wing

Fostering Growth in Gabon: G100 Summit Spurs Business Opportunities and Educational Advancement

G100 The Business Networking Summit, Gabon, 25-28 February 2025

The G100 Business Networking Summit took place in Libreville, Gabon, from February 25 to 28, 2025. This innovative event, organized with the support of Come Pro Consulting, a Gabonese firm specializing in training, support, and consulting, aimed to enhance the business climate in Gabon. The summit brought together professionals from various sectors, including real estate, associations, networking specialists, business intermediaries, trade finance experts, entrepreneurs, opportunity seekers, and project leaders. Unlike traditional conferences, this summit emphasized practical engagements over panel discussions or exhibitions, focusing on personalized appointments for each participant.
 
Key Highlights:
  • Opening Ceremony: The event commenced with an opening ceremony that, despite initial modest attendance due to its novel concept, set the stage for the subsequent activities.
  • B2B, B2G, B2C Meetings: Structured sessions facilitated direct interactions among businesses, government entities, and consumers, fostering meaningful connections and collaborations.
  • Company Visits: Participants had the opportunity to visit various companies, gaining first-hand insights into local business operations and potential partnerships.
Notable Outcomes:
  • Educational Opportunities: A Paris-based firm offered the “Conquérants & Leaders AFRIK” program to four high school students from disadvantaged backgrounds (two girls and two boys), aiming to cultivate curiosity, ambition, determination, authenticity, project design, and action among these students.
  • Scholarships: Five scholarships were awarded to recent high school graduates from underprivileged backgrounds for studies at Jharkhand Rai University in India.
  • Digital Literacy Initiatives: Plans were initiated to teach young girls from disadvantaged backgrounds coding, computer science, and robotics through a virtual campus, introducing them to basic energy concepts and environmental impacts.
  • STEM Engagement: Discussions began on organizing The Game Changer Awards in person, an event where teams of young girls work on STEM projects, similar to initiatives in Australia, with potential sponsorship from the Australian government.
  • Satellite Program: The Mission Shakthisat program aims to select 108 young girls aged 14 to 18 in Gabon, coaching them to build satellites, with opportunities for a few to launch their satellites from the Indian space station, supported by various space agencies and the Indian government.
  • Art Exhibitions: Contracts were established for Gabonese artworks to be exhibited in galleries across India, the United Arab Emirates, and Singapore.
  • Business Partnerships: Several partnerships and collaboration contracts were signed between Gabonese companies and international entities, enhancing the local business landscape.
The summit received support from the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Gabon, the General Directorate of Crafts, and the National Chamber of Crafts of Gabon. Gratitude was extended to all international entities that provided these opportunities to the Gabonese people and to all participants who contributed to the event’s success.

G100 Gabon Country Chair Business Networking Wing

content_html:
Finding Balance: Quest for Emotional and Economic Wellbeing for Wealth & Values

G100 Hong Kong Meetings, 7-9 March 2025  

Our recent exploratory trip to Hong Kong was a transformative experience, offering valuable insights and new learnings. It was led by G100 Founder, Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, who attended a private event with noted leaders from India and leveraged this occasion to connect with local networks in Hong Kong.
 
The meet-and-greet session, held in honor of International Women’s Month, was a valuable listening and learning experience, where we gained important insights into the societal issues affecting Hong Kong and impacting women and girls, such as:
 
  • Intense Pressure to Excel: Women, girls, and children in general face unrelenting demands to succeed professionally, financially, and academically. These pressures are exacerbated by a declining economy and rising living costs, leading to complex and chronic stressors.
  • Rising Mental Health Concerns: Young women and students struggle with mounting social anxiety, pessimism, and stifling academic expectations. These factors have led to a troubling surge in childhood depression and teen suicides.
  • Vulnerability to Cybersecurity Threats: Women and girls across generations face growing digital threats, from financial scams to predatory online relationships, compromising their safety and trust.
These discussions sparked the consideration of potential solutions, such as integrating different communities to address these common issues. We aim to collaborate with local women’s organizations and charities, develop greater global solidarity—particularly in upcoming meetings for the ASEAN region—to determine new directions to tackle root causes and create lasting change through partnerships and collaborative actions.
 
We are most grateful to Dr. Minu Bakshi for her invitation to Hong Kong. We extend our utmost gratitude to Malti Dialdas for her support and introductions. We were delighted to meet Shirley Whing Chow, who led G100 activities in Hong Kong in 2023. We also thank Karishma Samtani for her soulful care.

content_html:
Women at the Heart of Progress – Inclusive Development Driving Change

G100 International Women’s Day Conference, Portugal, 13 March 2025 

Women are not just part of change – they ARE the change. This conference emerged from a group of women in the G100 wing of Communication, Advocacy & Mediation, who came together to courageously address topics that may be unpopular but are necessary to engage with for inclusive growth. With this spirit, prominent figures from various sectors were invited to discuss and deliberate on a manifesto with concrete inputs. It was most inspiring to see all united in their determination to turn words into action.

The conference theme, “Women at the Heart of Progress: Development, Economy, and Sustainability,” emerged from our faith in the power of women to build a better future together by deconstructing taboos, identifying obstacles, and mapping a forward path. After all, progress requires questioning the status quo and taking collaborative action to achieve meaningful change.

In Portugal, as in many parts of the world, strategic decision-making still lacks a balance of perspectives, with women’s voices often underrepresented.
Thematic panels at the conference covered subjects such as economic transformation, sustainability, education, and public policies. All participants agreed that a unified commitment is urgently needed to promote real change, ensuring that talent, qualifications, and merit are genuinely recognized, regardless of gender.

We are convinced that a country that values diverse perspectives is better prepared for the future. Research has consistently shown that women are already leading businesses with responsibility, resilience, and forward-thinking vision. The female perspective brings more responsible, ethical, and resilient management models, driving organizational and societal transformation. Women-led companies foster faster and more sustainable economic growth, supported by compelling statistics. Achieving gender equality in the labor market and corporate leadership leads to increased economic growth, innovation, and profitability. Companies with diverse leadership tend to be more adaptable and resilient. While the number of female entrepreneurs is growing, accessing funding and support networks remains a significant challenge.

The female presence is crucial for the economy’s competitiveness and modernization. It’s essential to emphasize that women are not just participants but catalysts for economic transformation. Ensuring fair opportunities for women is not only a matter of equity but also a strategic necessity for sustainable development. In this regard, there’s no turning back—companies need more women in leadership roles, and they will only benefit from it. As we move forward, it’s vital to include both female and male leaders in our journey to bridge gaps and create an inclusive path to a future where everyone can thrive.
Sustainability is no longer optional; it has become essential for businesses to remain competitive. Technological innovation and digitalization are crucial for ensuring sustainable development and integrating responsible practices across all areas of business and public policy. Notably, female leadership has played a key role in implementing management models that uphold Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles, embrace the circular economy, and prioritize social responsibility.

In education, it’s essential that both boys and girls grow up understanding that equality is not a threat but rather an advantage for everyone. Investing in female empowerment directly benefits the progress and innovation of society as a whole. Education empowers women, reduces inequalities, and increases political and economic participation, ultimately creating a more equitable society.

However, structural barriers continue to limit women’s access to traditionally male-dominated fields such as Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM). To foster more diverse, creative, and productive teams, we need to encourage more girls and women to pursue these areas. This highlights the importance of female leadership programs, soft skills training, and policies supporting career advancement within organizations. To achieve meaningful change, schools and educational institutions must also challenge stereotypes from an early age, empowering girls and boys to explore all areas of knowledge without gender-based restrictions.

Through public policies and global alliances for equality, we can explore how governments, businesses, civil society organizations, and academic institutions can collaborate to reduce inequalities, create opportunities for women, and ensure a more equitable future. Achieving gender equality requires collective effort; international partnerships are crucial for sharing best practices and effective solutions. The UN, European Commission, OECD, and World Bank play a vital role in setting global goals and providing policy recommendations. Additionally, European funds support companies implementing diversity and inclusion policies, while also facilitating data collection and periodic reports to assess policy impact.

It is important to note that despite existing legislation ensuring equal pay, equitable parental leave, combating gender harassment and violence, and greater female representation in politics and business, strict enforcement and further action are still required to ensure these policies are not merely symbolic but translate into real practice.

Challenges persist, and continuous commitment from governments, businesses, and civil society is necessary. Change only occurs with political will, concrete measures, and cooperation between nations, businesses, and citizens. Building a fairer, more equal future is a collective task. Portugal will only be truly competitive and innovative if women have the same opportunities as men in politics, the economy, science, technology, and other sectors.

Talent and intelligence have no gender, but unfortunately, opportunities still do. However, conferences and platforms like ours help create spaces for opportunities, foster partnerships, and empower solution-driven initiatives. Together, we can bridge the gap and drive meaningful change.

Convenor:
Linda Pereira
G100 Global Chair, Communication, Advocacy & Mediation

Judith Batchelar OBE

Judith Batchelar OBE is a Biochemist, Board Director, Trustee of The Royal Botanic Gardens Kew, Ambassador for the Woodland Trust and Farm Africa, Member of the Natural Environment Research Council, UK. 

She is an influential leader in the food and drink industry with over thirty-five years of experience encompassing the diverse sectors of manufacturing, retail, and policy. Judith is Honorary President of the British Nutrition Foundation, Non-Executive Director of the Environment Agency, and Chair of the Rugby Players Association. 

She was formerly Director of Brand at Sainsbury’s, with responsibilities for product and policy development, food safety packaging, as well as corporate responsibility and public affairs. 

Judith holds an Honorary Doctorate in Agriculture from Harper Adams University and is a Fellow of the Institute of Food Science and Technology and the Royal Society of Arts and Manufacturers.

Judith was awarded an OBE in 2015 for services to Farming and the Food Industry and is a Commissioner on the Food, Farming and Countryside Commission.

content_html:
Milestone March: Advancing Women’s Leadership & Global Business Collaboration

G100 at UN CSW, New York, USA, 12 March & 21 March 2025 

March 2025 marked a significant milestone for G100, as the organization hosted two landmark events dedicated to empowering women leaders, fostering collaboration, and driving economic progress. On March 12, 2025, within the framework of CSW69, G100 facilitated high-level discussions in New York, bringing together esteemed professionals to explore key themes in corporate governance, diversity, and cross-border business partnerships. Shortly after, on March 21, 2025, the G100 USA Business Networking Wing successfully launched its inaugural event, uniting women leaders from various industries to establish strong business networks and mentorship initiatives. These events reaffirmed G100’s mission to create a more inclusive and supportive global business environment for women.
 
The March 12, 2025, meetings in New York, led by Michelle Ferrari (G100 Global Chair, Corporate Boards & Gender Balanced Companies) and Patricia Gonzalez (G100 Global Chair, Human Resources & Talent Development), provided invaluable insights into corporate leadership and the evolving role of women in business. The first session, hosted at PwC, convened over 30 distinguished G100 members, who engaged in thought-provoking discussions on Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI). The session emphasized inclusive leadership practices and actionable strategies to foster equitable corporate structures worldwide. Industry leaders exchanged best practices to promote meaningful change, reinforcing the importance of women’s voices in shaping global business policies.
 
Beyond business discussions, participants also enjoyed an enriching cultural and leadership experience through an exclusive guided visit to Tiffany & Co. This visit provided an in-depth look at the brand’s heritage, craftsmanship, and leadership in the luxury sector, sparking engaging conversations on branding, innovation, and the growing influence of women in the luxury business industry. The event further solidified G100’s commitment to empowering women across diverse sectors.
 
A major highlight of the New York engagements was the Pre-WEF Iberoamérica and G100 gathering, featuring a compelling discussion with the President of the Business Council—one of the most influential women in Mexico. The conversation centered on global economic trends, U.S.-Mexico trade relations, and the role of cross-border collaborations in fostering sustainable growth. This dialogue reinforced the importance of international partnerships in building a more inclusive and prosperous business landscape.

On March 21, 2025, the G100 USA Business Networking Wing hosted its inaugural event, bringing together a distinguished group of women leaders from various industries. The event served as a dynamic platform for knowledge-sharing, collaboration, and business networking, setting the stage for future initiatives aimed at elevating women in leadership. A key highlight of the event was the inspirational keynote addresses delivered by influential women, including H.E. Ann Linde, Former Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Kingdom of Sweden; Hon. Carmen Vasquez and Hon. Kathy J. King, New York Supreme Court Justices; Perla Tamez, Founder of Latina Empire & President of the Napoleon Hill Institute (Spanish Division); and Maria Belen Muñoz Barajas, Mexico’s first Indigenous Congresswoman from the State of Nayarit. These speakers shared powerful insights into leadership, economic empowerment, and the role of women in global business, inspiring attendees to drive change within their respective fields.
 
A significant moment during the event was the official introduction of the G100 USA Business Networking Wing State Chairs, who will lead efforts to expand the organization’s reach and impact across the country. The appointed State Chairs—Beatrice de Salles (California), Deborah Crowley (Michigan), Springa Zhao (Florida), and Denise Mejia Guerrero (Nevada)—will play a crucial role in fostering local business collaborations, mentorship programs, and leadership initiatives.
 
The event also featured engaging networking sessions, enabling participants to explore cross-sector partnerships, mentorship opportunities, and strategic initiatives to further economic empowerment for women. The discussions reinforced the critical need for inclusive and innovative approaches to entrepreneurship, corporate leadership, and business growth.
 
The success of these March 2025 engagements marks the beginning of a new era in women’s leadership, strengthening global connections and opening new opportunities for collaboration. G100 remains steadfast in its mission to empower, mentor, and support women in business, ensuring that they have access to the resources and networks needed to thrive in today’s competitive global economy.

excerpt: Bernard Swanepoel Bernard Swanepoel is a highly respected Non-Executive Director… Read more
content_html:
Bernard Swanepoel

Bernard Swanepoel is a highly respected Non-Executive Director at Implats, Zimplats, Manganese Metal Company (MMC), and THINKspiration, with over 40 years of experience in the mining industry, more than 25 of which have been spent in senior and executive leadership roles. A qualified mining engineer with a BSc in Mining Engineering from the University of Pretoria (Tuks), Bernard also holds a B.Com (Hons) in Financial Management from UNISA and a Mine Manager Certificate of Competency. He matriculated at Hoërskool Bergsig in Rustenburg. In 2008, he co-founded To The Point Growth Specialists with Clinton Halsey, a boutique consulting and investment firm.

Bernard has an extensive board portfolio, having served 11 years on the board of Sanlam and 15 years on the board of African Rainbow Minerals. He is currently a Non-Executive Director on the boards of Impala Platinum (Implats), Zimplats, and the African Exploration Mining and Finance Corporation (AEMFC). He is also the Chairman of Manganese Metal Company. A respected leader in business advocacy, Bernard is the past President of the AHI and was the inaugural Chair of the Small Business Institute (SBI), a national business chamber.

Through To The Point Growth Specialists, Bernard co-owns Resources for Africa Investment Conferences, which hosts some of the mining industry’s leading conferences, including the Joburg Indaba, Junior Indaba, London Indaba, Coal & Energy Transition Day, and the PGMs Industry Day—all of which he chairs. Alongside his wife Tracey, he also leads THINKspiration, a consulting venture focused on strategy alignment, culture change, and leadership development. Bernard recently registered as a member of the Institute of Directors. Beyond the boardroom, he is deeply connected to the land, owning and operating a cattle farm in Limpopo and co-owning a macadamia farm in Mpumalanga. Bernard combines deep industry expertise with a passion for business, leadership, and sustainable development.
