Denim Club Dialogues: Uniting Global Leaders for Gender-Balanced Leadership and Transformative Change

G100 The Denim Club Dialogues, Six Senses Fort Barwara, Rajasthan, India, 23–26 May 2025

The G100 Denim Club Dialogues brought together global leaders, Denim Partners, and changemakers at the iconic Six Senses Fort Barwara, India, for an inspiring three-day exchange on fostering gender-balanced leadership, inclusive excellence, and transformative change across industries.
 
It all began with a vision: to bring together some of the world’s most inspiring leaders in a space where authentic conversations could take place — conversations that inspire action, foster collaboration, and drive us closer to a world of gender-balanced leadership and transformative change.
 
Driven by this purpose, and organized with dedication by Michelle Ferrari and Patricia Gonzalez, under the inspiration, support, and vision of Dr. Harbeen Arora and Dr. Vinay Rai, the Denim Club Dialogues at Six Senses Fort Barwara became a remarkable gathering of changemakers from around the world.
 
The anticipation was high as the event approached. It offered an extraordinary opportunity to connect, collaborate, and advance progress with global leaders, colleagues, and Denim Allies, all united by a shared purpose.
 
Supported by the G100 Wings of Change, the forum brought together two key initiatives: Corporate Boards & Gender Balanced Companies and Human Resources & Talent Development. Alongside the unwavering commitment of the Denim Partners, these initiatives are building pathways to foster diversity, equity, and leadership opportunities for women across sectors and borders.
 
The majestic Fort Barwara provided an inspiring backdrop for deep reflection, cross-sector collaboration, and the co-creation of strategies for a more inclusive future.
 
The gathering began with a welcome cocktail, with an agenda thoughtfully curated by Michelle and Patricia, setting the tone for meaningful dialogue, connection, and celebration.
 
A vibrant group of leaders participated, including CEOs, cultural icons, senior officials, and changemakers, among them:
Rosario Marín (former U.S. Treasurer), Larry Rubin (President, American Society of Mexico and Denim HR Partner), Carla Estrada (renowned international producer), Valentina Alazraki (international journalist), Julio Di Bella (CEO, Gran Bajío), Rosalind Wilson (President Latin America, GATX), Angélica Ruiz (President Latin America, BP, and President of BritCham), Silvia Dávila (President, Danone), Blanca Estela Pérez (HR leader entrepreneur and G100), Concepción Valadez (UN Public Information Representative and G100), Mauricio Schwartzmann (Country Manager Mexico, MasterCard), Ana Paula Jiménez (CEO, PwC Mexico), Maria Teresa Arnal (Global Board Advisor and former CEO, Google Mexico), Valerie Aguirre (Executive Chief, WEF Iberoamérica), Luis Fernando Guareschi (former CEO, Cargill Mexico), Ana Luisa Mondragón (CEO, Morna Consulting Group), Sebastián Casanova (Ford Mexico Post-Sale Director), Irene Espinosa (former Deputy Governor, Mexico Central Bank and Mexico General Treasury), Begoña Vizcaíno (Leader Deals Iberoamérica, PwC and one of the 100 most influential Latinas worldwide), John Ryan (CEO, Healthy Place to Work), Ma. Eugenia Sidaoui (owner of Fians Capital), Olga Zueva (entrepreneur, wellbeing leader), among many others.
 
A highlight of the evening was the presentation of recognitions by the Rai Foundation and G100. These acknowledgments created a powerful atmosphere of light, inspiration, and renewed commitment, celebrating leadership and advancing meaningful, lasting change.
 
Adding a special dimension to the event was the presence of mothers and daughters — a beautiful reflection of the multigenerational spirit of this journey, where learning, leadership, and legacy are shared across generations.
 
Through the leadership of Michelle and Patricia, supported by Valerie Aguirre, and an agenda designed to inspire and mobilize, the Denim Club Dialogues became an extraordinary platform where hearts, minds, and generations connected in purpose.
 
This experience reaffirmed the collective commitment to shape a future where C-suite leadership, gender balance, and inclusive excellence are the global standard. The Denim Club Dialogues showcased the power of collaboration, passion, and vision, all in service of building a more equitable and inclusive world.
 
Convenor: 
Patricia Gonzalez, G100 Global Chair, Human Resources & Talent Development Wing
Michelle Ferrari, G100 Global Chair, Corporate Boards & Gender Balanced Companies Wing

content_html:
H.E. Dominique Hasler

H.E. Dominique Hasler, Former Minister of Foreign Affairs, Education, and Sports of the Principality of Liechtenstein, is a distinguished political leader recognized for her dynamic and globally engaged policy leadership on behalf of one of the world’s smallest sovereign nations.

Her commitment to inclusive policymaking, innovation, and principled diplomacy has been evident throughout her political career. She entered government in 2017 when she was appointed Minister of the Interior, Education, and Environment, following her nomination by the Patriotic Union (Vaterländische Union). In this capacity, she was responsible for national security, Liechtenstein’s environmental policy, and the strategic management of the entire national education system. She also played a critical role in crisis management and communication during the pandemic, ensuring continuity in public services and facilitating a rapid transition to digital learning across the country.

Building on these achievements, Hasler assumed the expanded role of Minister of Foreign Affairs, Education, and Sports in 2021—a position she held until April 10, 2025.

Through her international engagement, Dominique Hasler upheld a steadfast commitment to the rule of law and the protection of human rights, consistently advocating for inclusive dialogue, constructive problem-solving, and the strengthening of multilateralism. She notably led the Veto Initiative at the United Nations—an internationally acclaimed diplomatic breakthrough designed to increase transparency and accountability in the use of veto power within the UN Security Council. The initiative mandates that any veto cast by a permanent member automatically triggers a meeting of the UN General Assembly, allowing the international community to openly debate the issue and ensuring that the veto no longer remains the final word.

As a strong advocate for human rights, good governance, and international justice, Hasler consistently emphasized the strategic role of small states in international diplomacy. With her deep systemic expertise in education, fostering international solidarity through humanitarian aid and sustainable development cooperation remains particularly close to her heart.

Her work also underscores the importance of gender equality, the role of women in peace and security processes, and inclusive leadership. As Foreign Minister, she actively fostered a global network of women foreign ministers to promote cooperation on joint initiatives and to strengthen solidarity with women and girls in crisis situations, who are often disproportionately affected by conflict, displacement, and the erosion of fundamental rights.

In her role as Foreign Minister, Dominique Hasler was also responsible for shaping Liechtenstein’s foreign economic policy, with a particular focus on its engagement within the European Economic Area (EEA), the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and the World Trade Organization (WTO). She led key negotiations on international treaties and agreements aimed at diversifying and expanding Liechtenstein’s global economic partnerships.

A hallmark of her leadership was Liechtenstein’s Presidency of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe, which she chaired from November 2023 to May 2024. As Chairperson of the Committee of Ministers—the Council of Europe’s main decision-making body, representing 46 member states—she led pivotal initiatives to uphold democracy, human rights, and the rule of law. During her chairpersonship, the Council adopted the landmark Artificial Intelligence Framework Convention, reinforcing Europe’s commitment to the ethical and human-rights-based development of AI. Additionally, under her leadership, the Register of Damages for Ukraine was formally implemented and operationalized. She also co-initiated the innovative “Book of Europe” project, bringing together reflections from European heads of government to foster dialogue on the future of the continent.

Before entering politics, Hasler held leadership and board-management positions in the education, health, and palliative care sectors, gaining expertise in strategic governance and organizational development.

Her academic journey reflects a continuous commitment to education and leadership. After completing secondary school at the Cantonal School in Sargans, Switzerland, she earned her teaching diploma in 2000. She went on to obtain a Master of Arts in Special Needs Education from the Intercantonal University of Special Needs Education in Zurich (2003–2006). She later enhanced her leadership profile by earning a Certificate in Organizational Development and Coaching, and ultimately completed her second Master’s degree—an Executive MBA in Entrepreneurial Management—at the University of Liechtenstein.

content_html:
Women Leaders Beyond Borders: Shaping the Future of the ASEAN Sheconomy

G100 ASEAN Roundtables at Women Economic Forum (WEF) ASEAN, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, 19–21 June 2025

The G100 ASEAN Roundtables in collaboration with The Women Economic Forum (WEF) ASEAN 2025, held from 19–21 June 2025 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, brought together over 614 influential women leaders, policymakers, entrepreneurs, academics, and changemakers from 33 countries.
 
Themed “Women Leaders Beyond Borders: Shaping the Future of the ASEAN SHEconomy,” this prestigious event served as a vital platform for advancing cross-border collaboration, innovative leadership, and sustainable economic development driven by women across ASEAN and globally.
 
The forum provided space for bold conversations, meaningful networking, and actionable initiatives aimed at shaping a future where women lead economic transformation and foster inclusive growth.
 
Held at Dewan Perdana MITI, the event showcased impactful strategies, success stories, and inclusive models highlighting the strength and potential of women-led development in the ASEAN region and beyond.
 
Opening Ceremony & Inauguration
The forum commenced with inspiring inauguration addresses by eminent leaders.
 
YABhg. Dato’ Seri Dr. Wan Azizah Dr. Wan Ismail, spouse of the Prime Minister of Malaysia, graced the forum as Guest of Honour and officially launched the opening ceremony.
 
YB. Senator Tengku Datuk Seri Utama Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz, Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI), represented by his Deputy, YB. Tuan Liew Chin Tong, delivered the keynote address. He expressed confidence that the deliberations and outcomes of the G100 ASEAN Roundtables in collaboration with WEF ASEAN 2025 would catalyse lasting change. He emphasised that the discussions would yield actionable strategies to foster inclusive leadership, accelerate efforts to close the gender gap, and ensure women are at the forefront of ASEAN’s economic transformation.
 
YBhg. Datin Dr. (h.c) Hartini Osman, President of WEF ASEAN 2025, delivered a powerful and inspiring speech on behalf of the organising committee, Yayasan Bina Kesejahteraan. She celebrated women’s transformative role in driving global economic growth and underscored the significance of cross-border collaboration, leadership, and innovation.
 
Key Highlights
Throughout the event, several distinguished Ministers and Senior Civil Servants addressed the audience, sharing their insights and vision for an inclusive and resilient Sheconomy.
 
YB. Datuk Seri Dr. Noraini Ahmad, Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development, addressed the plenary session and the closing ceremony, reinforcing the importance of women’s leadership at all levels of society.
 
YBhg. Dato’ Sri Suriani Dato’ Ahmad, Secretary-General of the Ministry of Health, delivered valuable insights during the plenary session, emphasising the intersection between women’s leadership and public health.
 
YBhg. Dato’ Sri TPr Dr. Maimunah Mohd Sharif, Mayor of Kuala Lumpur, inspired attendees during the plenary session by highlighting the role of inclusive urban governance in fostering women’s empowerment.
 
YBhg. Datuk Bahria Mohd Tamil, Deputy Secretary-General (Investment & Management) at MITI, connected with participants during the Networking Evening Tea session, highlighting Malaysia’s commitment to inclusive economic development.
 
Other notable speakers included YBrs. Dr. Sugumari S Shanmugam, who shared her expertise in a parallel session, and YB Puan Anfaal Shaari, who participated in an engaging fireside chat session.
 
The 27 resolutions of the Women Economic Forum ASEAN 2025 are organized across four key dimensions. Dimension 1 focuses on Inner Power, emphasizing the need to empower women through leadership, education, and innovation, enabling them to unlock their full potential. Dimension 2 centers on Inclusion, advocating for equitable and sustainable economic development by ensuring that women have equal access to opportunities and resources. Dimension 3 highlights Integration, promoting cultural, digital, and policy alignment to drive the growth of the Sheconomy through collaboration and systemic support. Dimension 4 addresses Innovation, aiming to strengthen global connectivity, visibility, and accessibility for women in the post-normal era by harnessing technology and forward-thinking strategies.
 
Founders & Global Leaders
The forum featured the active participation of Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of WEF and G100, alongside a distinguished group of G100 Global Chairs.
 
The G100 Global Chairs, Presidents Advisory Members, Global Advisory Members, and Country Chairs present included H.E. Dominique Hasler, Presidents Advisory Member, Dr. Meenakshi Arora Dabral, Global Alliances & Alumni Networks, Dr. Coco Wong, Leadership & Entrepreneurial Education, Farzanah Chowdhury, Healthcare, Wellness, Insurance & Risk, Dr. Diah Yusuf, Business Accelerator, Dr. Sirikul Nui Laukaikul, Brand Creation & Marketing, Vanessa Florence Roux, Coaching & Training, Dr. Milan LaBrey, Volunteerism & Values, Mireille Toulekima, Engineering & Energy, Dr. Maricor M. Malitao, Business Chambers & Partnerships, H.E. Dr. Epsy Campbell Barr, International Affairs, Caroline Sack Kendem, Rural Development, Migration & Refugees Resettlement, Agnes Tshibaka Mpemba, Global Advisory, Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication, Marie Paule Niat, Global Advisory, Agriculture, Agritech, Agritourism, Agribusiness, Marie France Kouakou, Côte d’Ivoire, Country Chair First Ladies Outreach, Bory You, Cambodia Country Chair, Leadership & Entrepreneurial Education, Zenda Ng, Malaysia Country Chair, CARE Economy, Disability Inclusiveness & Social Innovation, Rosemarie Rafael, Philippines Country Chair, Business Accelerator, Sylvie IKOO, France Country Chair, Design & Lifestyle.
 
These influential leaders emphasised the critical role of women in shaping global policies, advancing sustainable development, leading digital transformation, and strengthening economic resilience across borders.
 
Book & Product Launches
The forum also witnessed the launch of significant publications and entrepreneurial ventures:
 
ABLE Visionary Leaders Vol.1, authored by Dr. Sarifa Alonto Younes, was launched to inspire future generations of women leaders.
 
The Ca-Ching Skincare and Wellness Brand, founded by Dr. Coco Wong, was introduced, promoting wellness led by women entrepreneurs.
 
The Malaysia Women Entrepreneur Chamber of Commerce, spearheaded by Datin Dr. Norli Hj Alias and Avagrace Law, MWECC Collaboration was officially launched to support and empower women entrepreneurs.
 
MOU Signing
MOU Signing Ceremony
A key Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the G100 Wing of Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication, under the leadership of Datin Hartini Osman, G100 Global Chair, and the following strategic partners:
 
African Women Entrepreneurship Program (AWEP)
VR Universe
 
This agreement will facilitate women’s leadership training programmes and entrepreneurial development across West and Central Africa, ASEAN, and specifically the Philippines. Initiatives will commence in Ghana, Cameroon, Gabon, Congo DRC, Ivory Coast, and select ASEAN nations, supporting inclusive economic growth and women-led enterprises.
 
Wawasanita and Malaysia Women Entrepreneur Chamber of Commerce (MWECC), represented by Datin Norly Hj Alias and Avagrace Law
With
Philippines Muslim Women Council, represented by Bai Norhata Alonto, President
Women’s Business Council Philippines, represented by Rhoda Castro Caliwara, President
 
Cultural Immersion & Shared Experiences
A hallmark of the G100 ASEAN Roundtables in collaboration with WEF ASEAN 2025 was the celebration of Malaysia’s multicultural heritage and inclusive spirit.
 
The Gala Dinner was a memorable evening filled with music, traditional performances, and culinary delights, showcasing unity in diversity. An awards session in four segments recognised 97 awardees at the:
 
Inaugural session
Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai Keynote Address
Networking Tea
Gala Dinner
 
Participants also experienced a heartfelt visit to the Yayasan Basmi Kemiskinan orphanage homes Asrama Kasih ybk in Serendah followed by a private tour to PNB 118 Second Tallest building in the World.
 
The forum concluded with a scenic Hop-On Hop-Off Night Tour of Kuala Lumpur, fostering cross-cultural connections and shared experiences.
 
Conclusion & Call to Action
The G100 ASEAN Roundtables in collaboration with The Women Economic Forum (WEF) ASEAN 2025 underscored a powerful collective vision to build an inclusive, innovative, and sustainable Sheconomy.
 
The event reaffirmed our shared responsibility to dismantle systemic barriers and elevate women not only as beneficiaries but as architects of global economic and societal transformation.
 
We call upon governments, the private sector, academia, and civil society to take bold, coordinated action to advance women’s leadership, economic participation, and influence across ASEAN and globally.
 
The 100 Days Connect & Collaborate Roundtable will also mark the launch of the YBCARE web app, which will serve as the central platform for communication among all Global Chairs. The app will feature the 35-year journey of YBK, along with links to their upcoming programs and community initiatives.
 
We have successfully engaged with 77 Global Chairs and 23 ASEAN leaders, along with the Secretariat of WEF, YBK, and the YBCARE team, in preparation for this important launch and the launch of the web app www.YBCAREmalaysia.com, featuring the 100 Days Meet and YBK Eradicating Poverty Ecosystem shared with the world.
 
Convenor:
Datin Hartini Binti Osman, G100 Global Chair, Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication Wing

Dr. Maja Stevkova Shterieva

Dr. Maja Stevkova Shterieva

Dr. Maja Stevkova Shterieva is the President of the Macedonian Banking Association and Chief Financial Officer at Komercijalna Banka, the largest bank in Skopje, North Macedonia. Born in 1970 in Skopje, she is a dedicated economist with a strong academic and professional background in finance.

She earned her Ph.D. in Economic Sciences in 2012 from the University “St. Cyril and Methodius” in Skopje, with a focus on “Operational Risk and Corporate Governance.” In 2000, she completed her Master’s degree in Monetary Economics from the same university, concentrating on “Asset and Liability Management in Banking.” Her international training includes a Risk Management Program completed in the United States in 2000, organized by the University of Wisconsin and Georgetown University. Most recently, she participated in the Executive Program on Corporate Management organized by AOTS in Tokyo.

Maja Stevkova Shterieva currently serves on the Board of Directors of Komercijalna Banka and represents North Macedonia in the European Banking Federation’s Associate Members Group as President of the Macedonian Banking Association.

She is a strong advocate for women’s rights, equality, and social responsibility. Since 2009, as President of the Coordination Group for Corporate Social Responsibility at Komercijalna Banka, she has led numerous initiatives supporting women, especially victims of domestic violence. These include financing the Center for Victims of Family Violence in Skopje, supporting the publication of the “Manual for the Treatment of Women Victims of Family Violence,” and backing the project “Economic Strengthening of Women in Rural Areas and Victims of Family Abuse.”

Beyond her executive responsibilities, she is actively involved in governance and education. She is a Member of the Supervisory Board of “KB Prvo,” a pension fund company, former President of the Board of the Academy of Banking and IT Foundation, and a former Board Member of the Chamber of Commerce of the Republic of Macedonia.

Committed to the development of younger generations, Maja Stevkova Shterieva also serves as a lecturer in “Entrepreneurial Finance” at the Faculty of Economics, University American College, Skopje. She has previously lectured on “Managing Risk” at Staffordshire University’s Faculty of Business and Law in collaboration with New York University in Skopje.

Khosi Sibisi

Khosi Sibisi   

Khosi Sibisi is the Founding Member and Chairperson of Women in Mining Business (WiMBIZ, SA), an organization dedicated to advancing women’s participation and leadership in the mining sector. Her contributions to the industry were recognized when she was named among the Top 100 Global Inspirational Women in Mining by Women in Mining UK in 2018.

A seasoned businesswoman, social entrepreneur, public speaker, mentor, and coach, Khosi has built a distinguished career in corporate leadership, sustainability, and governance. She serves as a Non-Executive Director of HCI Coal and Ori Professionals and is the Chairperson of Gole VOP Trades, a company specializing in trading and bulk commodities, investing in strategic assets, and providing logistic solutions. Leveraging her extensive experience in strategic decision-making and business growth, she continues to drive impactful change in multiple industries.

She is the Founder of KS Management Consultants, a firm specializing in Sustainability Reporting aligned to International Standards, including TCFD, GRI, SASB, and others. The firm assists companies in aligning their Sustainability Reporting with ESG Principles and the UN Sustainable Development Goals Vision 2030.

Khosi’s career in mining began at Harmony Gold, where she held the position of Group Corporate Affairs. She later became the Founder and CEO of Khusela Women Investments, a 100% women-owned coal mining company that successfully established operating mines in the Mpumalanga Coalfields.

Her expertise extends across executive and non-executive roles in South Africa’s blue-chip companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange. She is passionate about driving business success and is open to exploring new non-executive director opportunities, where she can contribute her leadership and industry insights.

Khosi holds a BA in Social Science from City College of New York, a Certificate in Purchasing and Supply Management from The Eli Broad Graduate School of Management, Michigan State University, USA, and a Certificate in ESG Sustainability Reporting and Regulation Implementation from Illinois University, USA. She is also a Wits Business School alumna, having completed short courses in Leadership Development, Finance for Non-Financial Managers, and Corporate Governance (King I, II & III).

content_html:
Empowering Connections, Catalysing Change

G100 Aix-en-Provence France Meetings, Alongside les Rencontres Economiques, 3-5 July 2025

On our way to Aix-en-Provence for the 25th edition of the Rencontres Économiques, we had the pleasure of visiting L’Epopée, a vibrant coworking space in Marseille, France, offering flexible workspace solutions to entrepreneurs, startups, and businesses – creating empowering ecosystems where individuals can grow, innovate, and thrive with the power of inspiration and community. 
 
Led by co-founder Laurent Choukroun, a social entrepreneur with a background in innovation and social business from HEC Paris, L’Epopée has become a hub for entrepreneurship, education, and social innovation.
 
Over lunch, we discussed our shared drivers of commitment, impact, and international cooperation, while exploring parallels between India and France in economics, culture, and diplomacy. This sparked plans for a trip to India in August to further conversations and build tangible connections between L’Épopée’s ecosystem and purpose-driven stakeholders in India.  
 
Thereafter, we visited Tangram, Marseille, another beautiful site and space for meetings and conferences. We had the honor to meet Véronique Albertini-Saadé, Présidente of CMA Media, and Tanya Saadé Zeenny, Managing Director of the CMA CGM Group and President of the CMA CGM Foundation, toward organising the Global Leadership by Women Summit on September 18 at the Palais du Pharo in Marseille, in the leadership of Chiara Corazza, also on the G100 Presidents Advisory Council.
 
G100 Founder Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai was invited to join the Advisory Council of the Global Leadership by Women Summit. The Advisory Council comprises prominent leaders and professionals from various fields, including Véronique Saadé (President of CMA Media), Tanya Saadé Zeenny (President of the CMA CGM Foundation), H.E. Elisabeth Moreno (Former French Minister of Gender Equality, Diversity, and Equal Opportunities and Chairwoman of Ring Capital), and Mathilde Lemoine (Group Chief Economist at Edmond de Rothschild). The council also features media professionals like Apolline de Malherbe (Journalist and host on RMC BFM) and eminent international representatives like Chiara Corazza (Representative of France for the private sector G20 EMPOWER).
 
We then proceeded to attend the 25th edition of Les Rencontres Économiques d’Aix-en-Provence, held from July 3 to 5, 2025, at Parc Jourdan, bringing together leaders from politics, business, and academia to discuss pressing issues and shape the future of Europe. This edition featured around 400 speakers, including prominent politicians, economists, business leaders, and intellectuals. The conference covered various topics, such as economic policy and Eurozone coordination, sustainable growth and climate governance, digital transformation and innovation, and global challenges and cooperation.
 
The Rencontres Économiques in Aix-en-Provence provided a valuable opportunity to meet and engage with prominent personalities, including French Minister for Gender Equality, H.E. Madame Aurore Bergé, fostering meaningful connections and discussions. 
 
We also met eminent leader María Elena Agüero, the Secretary General of Club de Madrid, and extended our support from the G100. Club de Madrid is a prestigious organization comprising 127 former leaders from different countries who have held high-ranking government positions, toward promoting democratic values globally, as also bringing together global leaders to share experiences and expertise.
 
We also met up with sisters in our network attending the event, notably Global Chair for Humanity, Technology & Innovation, Dominique Delporte-Vermeiren, and Carmen M. Nzamba (France Country Chair, Global Networking Wing).

Meetings led by: Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder, G100, along with Vinay Rai, Founder, Denim Club

Born in Pakistan and settled in Switzerland, Anila flourished both as an educator and fashion consultant, carving her niche in the European fashion scene. Driven by purpose and passion, Anila is a natural at networking, embodying an ease in connecting with people, engaging and empowering communities with purpose and passion. A tireless advocate of gender equality, Anila is dedicated to supporting underserved women, striving to create sustainable livelihoods through ardent entrepreneurial and educational endeavors. Anila’s journey is a blend of creativity, business acumen, community building, civic engagement, and a profound commitment to societal progress. With deep roots in the East, Anila understands the challenges faced by women at the cusp of tradition and modernity. She leverages her education and experience in the West to help bridge cultural gaps and enrich cross-cultural exchange, which is vital for people across the world to come together in peace and harmony, and to work and build together in solidarity and prosperity for all. A dreamer and doer, her journey is a testament to the power of self-belief and dedication to delivery.

G100 Kazakhstan Meetings, 5-6 Sept 2025 

 
In early autumn, the first International Forum of Kazakhs of the World “KZ Empowering Women” was held in Astana. Organized by the public foundations “Arial” and “Moldir Umit” in collaboration with G100, the event coincided with the Day of Languages of the People of Kazakhstan and Family Day, under the theme “A Million Likes – Women Who Did a Million Deeds.”

The forum gathered Kazakh women from around the world who have achieved success in various fields. They shared their inspiring life stories, discussed women’s empowerment, gender equality, and anti-violence initiatives, and explored ways to strengthen cooperation and networking among active women.

The main speaker was Datin Dr. (H.C) Hartini Osman from Malaysia — Presidenta Global de Filantropía G100 BPE, Presidenta del Foro Económico de Mujeres WEF ASEAN 2025 C YBCARE. She is also the President & Group Managing Director of Prihatin Group of Companies, Chairman of YBCARE (Foundation), President of WEF ASEAN 2025, Global Chair G100 Philanthropy, Business and Poverty Eradication, and President of the ASEAN–India Business Council of the Women’s Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (WICCI).

She introduced G100 to the Kazakh women and delivered a strong speech about the empowerment of women all around the world.

Distinguished guests included Orazkul Asangazi, Dr. Reshide Yuksel, Kyrmyzy Saparkyzy, Asylgul Abish, and Kuralai Eshmuratova. The event also featured cultural performances by the Korkyt ethno-ensemble, fashion shows by Kerbez Models and AsianCharmModels, and a traditional-themed defile by designer Raushan Anuarbekova.

excerpt: Dr. Michael Short Michael Short is a Associate Professor of… Read more
content_html:
Dr. Michael Short

Michael Short is a Associate Professor of Nuclear Science and Engineering, joined the faculty at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in July 2013. He brings more than 15 years of research experience in nuclear materials, microstructural characterization, and alloy development. His work integrates large-scale experiments, micro- and nanoscale characterization techniques, and multiphysics modeling and simulation to solve complex problems in nuclear science and engineering.

Professor Short holds dual Bachelor of Science degrees in Nuclear Science and Engineering and in Materials Science and Engineering, both awarded by MIT in 2005. He continued his graduate studies at MIT, earning an M.S. in Materials Science and Engineering in 2010, and a Ph.D. in Nuclear Science and Engineering later that same year.

His research primarily focuses on three key areas. The first is the development of non-contact, non-destructive techniques to measure irradiated material properties, particularly using Transient Grating Spectroscopy (TGS). Second, his group works on preventing the deposition of deleterious phases, such as CRUD (Chalk River Unidentified Deposits), which form as fouling layers in nuclear reactors and other energy systems. Third, he is advancing the quantification of radiation damage through stored energy fingerprints—a novel approach that earned him the prestigious National Science Foundation (NSF) CAREER Award in 2016.

Professor Short’s dedication to teaching and mentoring has been widely recognized. He received the MIT Bose Award for Excellence in Teaching in 2022 and was named a MacVicar Faculty Fellow in 2021, one of MIT’s highest honors for undergraduate teaching. He was previously honored with the Junior Bose Award for Excellence in Teaching in 2017, the Earll S. Murman Award for Excellence in Undergraduate Advising in 2016, and the Ruth and Joel Spira Award for Excellence in Mentoring and Advising in the same year.

His research and communication excellence have also earned international recognition. He received Best Poster at the 1st Annual MIT NSE Research Expo in 2010, Best Nuclear Energy Presentation at the 2nd Tokyo Tech MERCES Forum in Okinawa, Japan, in 2009, and Best Graduate Paper at the Bodycote 2009 Paper Prize Competition in Cologne, Germany.

Women at the Forefront: Driving Sustainability, Economic Inclusion, and Peace 

G100 Vienna Meetings, United Nations, 12 Sept 2025

At the heart of one of the world’s most influential institutions, the United Nations headquarters in Vienna, the G100 marked a significant milestone with its international conference titled “The Role of Women for a Sustainable and Peaceful Future.” Held on 12 September at the Vienna International Centre and in cooperation with UNIDO, the event served as a beacon of thought leadership, global collaboration, and visionary dialogue. Exactly 100 change-makers gathered in person, with many more joining via live stream from across the world.
 
With deep pride and a firm belief in the movement’s impact, the G100 community came together to highlight the transformative role of women across four key pillars: Sustainability, Circular Economy, Finance, and Peace. These are not abstract ideals; they are today’s most pressing challenges, and women are leading the response.
 
The conference opened with keynote speeches by Gunther Beger, Managing Director at UNIDO; Bodil Valero, President of G100 2025; and Irena Radovic, Governor of the Central Bank of Montenegro and G100 Global Chair for Financial Inclusion, who addressed the audience via a powerful video message setting the stage for a platform of global relevance.

Caroline Sack Kendem

Caroline Sack Kendem

Caroline Sack Kendem is the co-founder and President of AWEP Cameroon (The African Women Entrepreneurship Program for Cameroon ). She is also the chairperson for AWEP Central Africa and a representative of all the French speaking AWEP branches (total of 19 branches). Caroline is a woman committed to the fight against the economic and social exclusion of African women for almost 13 years now. Her activism and commitment radiate in Africa.

In 2012, when she launched AWEP Cameroon, she was a pioneer in the fight for better access for women in the business world. AWEP activities are aimed at female entrepreneurship, coaching, leadership, mentoring as well as the empowerment of young girls and women. In 2017, AWEP Cameroon received a 85 000 USD grant from the US Department of State for the implementation of an empowerment project for women and young girls in the northern regions of Cameroon which faced at that time terrorism. Caroline was the lead coordinator of that 2-year project which involved the training and capacity building of 500 grassroots young girls and women. She also coordinated the building of sheepfolds and collaborated with local veterinarians to train those group of women on first aids to be given to animals. Thereafter, it was about providing the marketing skills and at last connecting them to local markets. The second part of the project was to create and raise awareness among those women’s groups, by inviting moderate imams, traditional leaders/elders, women leaders and survivors of domestic violence and former/disengaged terrorists. Caroline took the risk of going to these regions when nobody wanted to go there to reach out to these women and raise awareness on the absolute necessity of counter-terrorism and promote peace.

In 2022, because of tremendous difficulties on access to finance, Caroline along with 6 other Cameroonian women leaders decided to invest and launch the very first impact funds of the sub region called SAVE (Support to African and Vulnerable Entrepreneurs). Her goals were to finance projects for young girls and displaced women and girls all across Africa. Two major companies decided to partner with her on that initiative: Advans which is the world leader in microfinance and E4IMpact/JFN center which is the leader in incubation for entrepreneurship. Caroline is the one who initiated of all these programs and set them up. Caroline was recognized as a leader and equipped textile entrepreneur by the Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton during her closing remarks at the Agoa Forum that was held in Zambia in June 2010.

For the past 4 years now, Caroline is mobilized for greater access for young girls to STEM (Sciences Technology, Engineer and Mathematics) and she founded the WATI (Woman Association for Technological innovation). In recognition of her contributions and activities, she was elected in December 2022 as the Vice President of FAAEI (Forum of African Associations on Economic Intelligence), a pan African organization that aims to promote scientific knowledge relating to strategic economic intelligence and technological innovation

Caroline sits as a board member of the SYNDUSTRICAM, the pioneer of industrial unionism in Cameroon, which serve as interlocutor of the industrial sector vis-à-vis government and other business groups. She is as well Executive Member of the ECCAS High Business Council. She is also the Godmother of the WONDER program of AfDB (African Development bank) for Cameroon which is an Accelerator program implemented in Cameroon and dedicated for existing female owned company

Caroline holds an MBA from the University of Scranton, in Pennsylvania (1992). She has 12 years’ experience working as in international consultant for international organizations/ institutions such as the Minister of Economy of Cameroon, ITC (ITC is the joint agency of the World Trade Organization and the United Nations) , AGOA Comity of the Prime Minister Office, Ministry of industry. She is lecturer across Africa for all topics related to gender issues. A dear Soul Sister who is committed to recovery, resilience and reintegration of all with dignity and humanity. The empowered and eminent group of #G100 is stronger with your presence and leadership.

excerpt: Connecting ChangeMakers, Catalyzing Change: Mobilizing Momentum for Mission Million G100… Read more
content_html:
Connecting ChangeMakers, Catalyzing Change: Mobilizing Momentum for Mission Million

G100 paris Meetings, France, 26 July 2025

On July 26th, we held a successful gathering and networking luncheon in Paris, featuring esteemed guests including Elizabeth Moreno, former French Minister, and Gabriela Ramos, Mexico’s official candidate for Director-General of UNESCO.
 
The event coincided with Afro-descendant Women’s Day on July 25th, aligning with Excellency Elisabeth Moreno’s ADWIN initiative. We also expressed our support for Gabriela Ramos’ candidacy, welcoming the prospect of another strong female leader at the helm of UNESCO.
 
Over 30 distinguished guests attended, including global chairs, country chairs, and prospective new members, specially invited by Global Chairs Vanessa Florence Roux, who now heads the wing of Coaching & Training, and Lamia Hanafi, who has taken the lead at the Start Up Ecosystems wing.
 
The lunch highlighted crucial insights, including the need for women to unite globally and work towards a shared vision to bridge gaps. The key points emphasised the importance of collective action, highlighting that the time is now to support women from all backgrounds in finding visibility, voice, and influence to drive peace and progress. Furthermore, progress is not guaranteed, and regression can occur without continued perseverance and support. Additionally, including men from diverse walks of life, such as the G100 Denim Club, is essential for fostering solidarity and accelerating progress on this journey.
 
We were also pleased to welcome Benjamin Brockt, Public Relations Director at the Paris Peace Forum Permanent Secretariat, who invited us to curate a session alongside the forum, which we were delighted to follow up on. We have been present at the forum earlier in Paris, when our Global Chair for World Peace, Nobel Peace Laureate H.E. Ouided Bouchamaoui, was a speaker.
 
After the luncheon, we went for meetings at MEDEF (Mouvement des Entreprises de France), France’s largest business federation. MEDEF represents entrepreneurs and businesses nationwide, advocating for economic growth, competitiveness, and job creation. Their “Women of MEDEF” initiative, launched in 2019, promotes diversity and female leadership, uniting women leaders and members.
 
At MEDEF, we met with Dominique Carlac’h, Vice-President and Spokesperson, MEDEF. Dominique is a renowned businesswoman and former professional athlete, holding various leadership roles in MEDEF and beyond.
 
Together with Lamia Hanafi, G100 Global Chair, Start Up Ecosystems wing, and Inès Baudienville at MEDEF International, who facilitated the meeting, we explored possibilities for a partnership for our Women Economic Forum conference and a CEOs summit and retreat. Collaborating with MEDEF would provide an excellent opportunity for women leaders across our communities to share ideas and insights, empowering women’s entrepreneurship, leadership, and economic vibrancy, as envisaged by the SHEconomy.
 
Indeed, partnerships with various like-minded communities, networks, and organisations is key to mobilising momentum for our Mission Million—uniting a million women in solidarity, toward leading the change we seek.
 
As we move forward, we look forward to turning these outcomes into reality and remain committed to fostering empowering collaborations in all aspects of life. By working together, we believe we can create a more peaceful, progressive, and prosperous world for everyone.
 
Convenor: Secretariat
Meetings led by: Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder, G100 and Vinay Rai, Founder, The G100 Denim Club

Alison Eddy

Alison Eddy

Alison Eddy is the Partner Ambassador for Inclusion and former London Managing Partner at Irwin Mitchell, a multi-disciplinary law firm with 23 offices across the UK.

She is recognised as a leading medical negligence lawyer, specialising in representing women and babies who have suffered life-changing injuries due to obstetric negligence. Throughout her career, she has been a passionate advocate for safe, compassionate healthcare for women and is committed to raising awareness of inequalities in healthcare, particularly within maternity services.

As a leader, she has championed diversity, inclusion, and social mobility. Under her leadership, Irwin Mitchell became the only top 50 UK law firm where over 50% of the partners are women (currently 58%). She has widely shared the journey of how this achievement was made possible. She also co-leads The Female Voice, a platform designed to connect, empower, and inspire women across professional networks. She firmly believes that intentional small steps lead to meaningful, lasting impact.

Alison supports two healthcare-focused charities. She serves as a Board Trustee for Group B Strep Support and as a Business Ambassador for Meningitis Now. In recognition of her contributions to gender equality and inclusive leadership, she has received multiple awards, including the Legal 500 ESG Lifetime Achievement Award – Women in Law (2024) and the Modern Law Awards Diversity & Inclusion Award (2025).

G100 Global Denim Club

G100 is also supported by The Denim Club : Group of G100 He-for-She Champions globally, comprising leaders and luminaries from the business, corporate and political domains, each leading a sector of influence and having their companies and institutions in support of gender parity and equality. They will advocate for gender equity and balance, mitigate barriers to women’s leadership, commit to women’s greater C-suite representation, and fuel funding for female founders.

Why ‘Denim’ ? Because it’s symbolic of our common ground. While men may be from Mars and women from Venus; and while girls may grow with pink and boys with blue, denim belongs to all of us equally as a place of comfort for cool and candid conversations. The sturdy denim stands for the solid dialogue between genders and the strength of solidarity that we aspire for. Together we can co-create a better, balanced world for All.

The G100 Global Chair along with the G100 Global Denim Club Partner develop together for their G100 Wing policy recommendations to governments and multilateral institutions worldwide. The far-reaching impact will energise a million women by 2022, and 5 million by 2030.

Together, in joint collaboration and co-creation, we are committed to join our forces and strengths for a better world toward defining, designing and determining a new future for ourselves with equity, equal opportunity, inclusion and economic empowerment of women, and of all, through the inclusive agency of women, supported by men champions.

Membership to G100 and Denim Club is free and by invitation only. The endeavours are non-political, non-religious and non-dogmatic.

We are co-creating a bold and beautiful model of working together in shared vision and aligned actions with gender respect, balance and parity. Our stellar example of solidarity is a shining testimony to the power of women and men walking together in purpose and mutual empowerment for the greater good of a more sustainable, balanced, progressive and peaceful world for all.

Sign - up

Jean Todt

Jean Todt was formerly Peugeot Talbot Sport’s Director and then Scuderia Ferrari Formula 1 team principal, before being appointed Chief Executive Officer of Ferrari from 2004 to 2008.

In October 2009, he was elected President of the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), and he was re-elected in 2013 and 2017.Under his leadership, Peugeot won 4 World Rally Championship titles (drivers and manufacturers), won the Paris-Dakar Rally 4 times, and twice won the Le Mans 24 Hours. During his time in charge, Ferrari won 14 Formula One World Championship titles (drivers and manufacturers).

It is also under his leadership that Michael Schumacher won five consecutive World Drivers’ Championships, from 2000 to 2004, and obtained 72 of his 91 victories.In 2015, Todt was appointed by the Secretary-General of the United Nations as its Special Envoy for Road Safety.

View More

Dr. Colin keogh

Dr. Colin Keogh, Founder – Sapien Innovation/TeamOSV/Rapid Foundation, Research Engineer – University College Dublin, Ireland. Dr. Colin Keogh is an award-winning innovative Engineer, with successful background in innovative technologies in the Engineering, Business and Innovation sectors.

He is an active innovation consultant, supporting the innovation and commercialisation of both commercial and EU funded research projects as an expert advisor, mentor and consultant. He has led ground-breaking research in the Energy, SDG’s, Additive Manufacturing and Innovation fields at multiple global universities, with a focus on technology forecasting, enhanced innovation methodologies, additive manufacturing, applied impact and integrating advanced technologies into social, environmental, philanthropic and entrepreneurial activities.

 
View More

Alyn Ware

Alyn Ware is a New Zealand peace educator and campaigner in the areas of peace, non-violence, nuclear abolition, international law, women’s rights, children’s rights and the environment.

He is an advocate for the use of legal and political mechanisms to resolve conflicts and prevent war. He was part of the government advisory team that integrated peace education into the New Zealand school curriculum, and he co-established a number of programs to implement peace education in schools, including Our Planet in Every Classroom, Cool Schools Peer Mediation, Mobile Peace Van, Schools Peace Week and the UN Decade of Nonviolence Schools Outreach Program.

Internationally, Mr Ware worked for the World Federalist Movement to help establish an International Criminal Court. He has served as Vice-President of International Peace Bureau, a Nobel Peace Laureate organisation working for peace, war prevention and disarmament for development.

View More

Eric Parrado

Eric Parrado Herrera is the Chief Economist and General Manager of the Research Department of the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) since March 2019.

Before joining the IDB, he was a professor of economics and finance at the ESE Business School of the Universidad de los Andes in Santiago, Chile. Mr. Parrado is a visiting professor at Oxford University and ETHzürich, and a member of the World Economic Forum’s Global Future Council on Frontier Risks.

From 2014 to 2018 he was the Superintendent of Banks and Financial Institutions in Chile, where he promoted reforms such as the modernization of banking legislation and the creation of new instruments for financial inclusion. Between 2011 and 2014, he was advisor to the Financial Committee that counsels the Ministry of Finance on the investment policy of Chile’s sovereign wealth funds and professor at the Adolfo Ibáñez University. 

View More

Edmond Hajrizi

Dr. Edmond Hajrizi is an academic, entrepreneur, and expert in the fields of management, information technology, and engineering. As the Founder, President, and CEO of the University for Business and Technology (UBT), he has led the institution since 2001, driving its growth and establishing it as a premier higher education institution in the region. His strategic vision has been pivotal in developing and executing plans that align with the university’s mission, ensuring long-term sustainability and excellence.
 
Dr. Hajrizi holds a Doctorate Degree in System Management from the Vienna University of Technology, where he also served as a Lecturer and Research Project Manager. His academic credentials are complemented by a Post Doc from City University London, a Postgraduate Degree in Advanced Automation Technology, and a Graduate Degree in Engineering from the University of Prishtina. His educational background is enriched by various certifications in quality management, business excellence, and project management from esteemed institutions like the City University London and the European Organization for Quality.

ulrik vestergaard knudsen

Ulrik Vestergaard Knudsen, OECD, Deputy Secretary-General and OECD, Gender and Diversity Champion, France. Ulrik Vestergaard Knudsen is an economist with more than 25 years of experience in international cooperation. He has served as Permanent Secretary of State/CEO of the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, as Chief Foreign Policy Advisor to the Danish Prime Minister, and as Ambassador to the OECD. 

During his five years as CEO, he spearheaded a change-management process, brought the Ministry of Foreign Affairs successfully through a period of budgetary constraints, and defined the strategic direction for the organisation in increasingly complex and unpredictable times. Prior to this, he served as Sherpa and Chief Diplomatic Advisor to two Danish Prime Ministers on Security Policy and on EU and Foreign Affairs in the Prime Minister’s Office. 

Mr. Knudsen served as Ambassador to the OECD and UNESCO in Paris (2008-09). In 2019 he was appointed Deputy Secretary-General of the OECD, covering a wide-ranging portfolio.

View More

Rainer Hahn

Rainer Hahn, Secretary General at Global United FC and Founder of Initiative Sports Responsibility in Germany.
 
Rainer Hahn has held various leadership positions, including director, business manager, and site manager, across multiple industries such as publishing, service agencies, event management, sponsorship, and corporate social responsibility. As the founder of Initiative Sports Responsibility, he focuses on promoting responsibility and sustainability in sports.
 
Currently, Rainer serves as the COO/Secretary General for Global United FC, the world’s largest international charity football organization dedicated to addressing climate and environmental issues through social projects.

Peter Lamers

Peter Lamers, President of the Executive Board, Scholengroep Spinoza, Netherlands. Peter was born and raised in the city of Rotterdam. He studied political science at the Erasmus University.

He is a highly experienced politician and CEO in education and government in which he has worked for over 30 years. For eight years he was the spokesman for the Minister of Finance of the Netherlands. Peter is very knowledgeable in strategic and corporate communication and he is a great networker. He was the head of the communication department of a special program of the ministry of Youth & Welfare called: Operation Young.

He started his political career as member of the council of Feyenoord-Rotterdam, then he was councilor of the province of South Holland. In 2012 the municipality of the city of Rotterdam nominated Peter to be Alderman for Youth & Education. In this position he made a significant impact. He successfully improved the policy on care and support for the youth and qualified education in Rotterdam.

James Michael Lafferty

James Michael Lafferty is the CEO and Member of Board of Directors Fine Hygienic Holding, UAE. He is not only a successful CEO– He is an Olympic Coach. An award-winning journalist. A college professor. A competitive athlete. A philanthropist, husband, father of 6, and a grandfather of 3. James started his career with humble roots, as a youth track and field coach. 

Hired by Procter and Gamble in his native Cincinnati, Ohio, James was recruited from the ranks of fitness instructor to enter P&G’s esteemed “Brand Management” program. After superb business and organizational results on the US business, James was transferred into an international career that took him to North Africa, Central and Eastern Europe, The Middle East, Western Europe, Africa and Asia. 

With a marketing and general management career that spans over 30 years, James Michael Lafferty is among the leading global experts on business-building, marketing and branding particularly in emerging markets. He has had a long and successful career building businesses and organizations across five continents for some of the world’s leading fast-moving consumer goods companies, including CEO roles within Procter and Gamble, Coca-Cola, and British American Tobacco.

Prof. Richard D’Aveni

Prof. Richard D’Aveni, The Bakala Professor of Strategy, Tuck School of Business, Dartmouth College, USA. D’Aveni is one of the foremost experts in the world on competition between corporations, militaries, governments, alliances & capitalist systems.

He is currently focusing his research on Technological Competition caused by 3D Printing. He has published numerous articles, books, blogs and columns on additive manufacturing. His work on additive manufacturing won the 2016 Thinkers50 Strategy Award, and nominated for the 2019 Thinkers50 Breakthrough Idea Award.

He authored numerous articles on competitive strategy in academic journals, HBR, FT of London, WSJ, Washington Post, and MIT/Sloan Management Review, as well as the global best selling book Hypercompetition, which is available in 14 languages. Since the 1990s, his writings are credited with creating a new paradigm in strategy using temporary advantages, principles of rapid & aggressive maneuvering and disruption rather than on defensive barriers & power over buyers/suppliers.

Pavan Bhatia

Pavan Bhatia is the Founder and CEO of GenWE Inc. and Co-Founder of CareerGPS. With over 25 years of experience at PepsiCo in senior global Human Resources roles, Pavan transitioned to entrepreneurship in 2020 to pursue his passion for developing future leaders. He launched GenWE in March 2020 with a mission to nurture global young leaders by equipping teenagers with essential leadership skills through a unique pairing model that connects youths from diverse backgrounds.

In 2022, he co-founded CareerGPS, a startup focused on transforming career development. CareerGPS simplifies, automates, and enhances career pathways for individuals while helping organizations identify high-potential talent and strengthen succession planning processes.

Dr. Porramate Chumyim

Dr. Porramate Chumyim, Founder/Director of NSTDA Acceleration, Venture Builder, Advisory Board of SB (Sustainable Brands), Thailand. Manages the national platform of the leading government innovation ecosystem providers, Thailand FoodInnopolis, under National Science Technology and Development Agency INSTDA).

He is a former national innovation policy maker at National Science Technology and Innovation Policy Office (STI office). Expert in Innovation system, business model innovation design and experience driven scalable process and has leadership and advisory roles in several additional organizations, innovative businesses and Tech start-ups.

He has additional deep experience in design thinking, product and service development, innovation strategy and diversification of business model portfolios. Wide experience with local entrepreneurs across the country. Driven by making an impact, he is a part of creating an innovation ecosystem in Thailand where he has strong purpose to drive not only the economic but also culture of inclusion and sustainable environment.

Kulmeet Bawa

Kulmeet Bawa, President & Managing Director, SAP Indian subcontinent. Kulmeet has been helping businesses in their digital transformation journey and is passionate about delivering exceptional experiences by leveraging a strong partner ecosystem and a great talent pool.

He is a technology veteran and an established business leader with more than 25 years of experience. Prior to joining @SAP, he led the India & South Asia market for Adobe and helped drive excellence in customer experience.

Kulmeet has also had an illustrious career in the Indian Army where he served in the Armoured Corps for 12 years before moving into the corporate world.

Niels Christian Nielsen

Niels Christian Nielsen is a proven leader of knowledge-based companies. Most of his career has evolved in professional services companies.

Today he serves as Board Director. He is or has been director of 40 companies; in 15 of them Chairman. He brings global perspective; strategy acumen combining discipline and innovation; leadership development and succession, and experience in M&A activities, where his total career record includes more than 100 transactions. Many of the companies have had exceptional growth trajectories.

Previously he was CEO of Catenas, a global roll-up of services companies. During the 1990s he was part of the team that created the DTI, and from 1994 he was part of the Executive Board that took DTI through a turn-around and made it a prime technology consulting company.

NCN has initiated a number of big strategic projects, involving multiple participants and public-private collaboration. He designed the Danish Network Cooperation program, subsequently adapted in a number of other countries, often with NCN as strategic advisor.

Ludovic Emanuely

Ludovic Emanuely is a seasoned international facilitator and strategic advisor, widely recognized for his work across Africa, Europe, and Asia. He currently serves as President of Croissance PEACE (Croissance Partagée Entre Afrique, Chine, Europe), an initiative dedicated to fostering shared economic growth across continents. He is also the President of the NGO Maître-Nageur Sauveteur Sans Frontières and CEO of Ludo l’Inventeur, a creative venture focused on developing non-digital educational board games.

Ludovic is married, a father of two, and a proud grandfather of six. With multicultural roots, he holds a deep belief in equity, opportunity, and global cooperation. His guiding motto is: “Shared prosperity? It’s only a matter of will and fairness.”

Miguel Reynolds Brandao

Miguel Reynolds Brandao, Founder & CEO CORKBRICK EUROPE, Expert, European Commission, President & CEO, Global Business Brokers, Managing Director, RAZÃO FINAL CONSULTING, Portugal. A Stanford alumni, always learning, curious and independent by nature, he graduated in engineering and management.

He is a serial entrepreneur who started his first venture in his early twenties. Since 1994, he has been strategic management advisor for several institutions in Portugal, Brazil and USA. Author of books and articles in strategic management systems, entrepreneurship, business brokering and teleworking, his last book, published in May 2015, is “The Sustainable Organisation – a paradigm for a fairer society”.

He is currently developing an objective, transparent and accessible criteria to support sustainable, impact, investment worldwide, where criteria includes the gender parity factors.

Bernard Swanepoel

Bernard Swanepoel is a highly respected Non-Executive Director at Implats, Zimplats, Manganese Metal Company (MMC), and THINKspiration, with over 40 years of experience in the mining industry, more than 25 of which have been spent in senior and executive leadership roles. A qualified mining engineer with a BSc in Mining Engineering from the University of Pretoria (Tuks), Bernard also holds a B.Com (Hons) in Financial Management from UNISA and a Mine Manager Certificate of Competency. He matriculated at Hoërskool Bergsig in Rustenburg. In 2008, he co-founded To The Point Growth Specialists with Clinton Halsey, a boutique consulting and investment firm.

He is currently a Non-Executive Director on the boards of Impala Platinum (Implats), Zimplats, and the African Exploration Mining and Finance Corporation (AEMFC). He is also the Chairman of Manganese Metal Company. After a successful multinational career, he has devoted time, energy & resources to public service with humanitarian & educational organizations which benefit communities locally and around the world. This includes a commitment to empower others, especially women, to accomplish ambitious goals. 

Firoz has had considerable experience in strategy development and large-scale change management, and continues to assist others to achieve transformational change and improve lives. 

He is an active Rotarian, lives by its ethos of service above self, and has served as District Governor and Rotary Foundation advocate. 

Firoz grew up in East Africa (Zanzibar & Kenya) and his travels as well as interest

H.E. President Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi is also the current Chairperson of the African Union, from Feb 2021 to Feb 2022. Prior to being elected President of the DRC in its first ever peaceful hand over of power, he was a top executive of the UDPS (Union for Social Democracy and Social Progress), a party led by his late father, Etienne Tshisekedi, who passed away in February 2017. 

In 2011, he was elected as Member of the National Assembly representing the constituency of Kananga in the Kasai Occidental province. Having refused to sit in the National Assembly in protest of the electoral fraud, he was later on deprived of his parliamentary mandate in 2013. Following the death of his father, he was elected national president of the UDPS at an extraordinary party Congress in March 2018.

In the same month, he was chosen by his fellow opposition leaders to lead the “Rassemblement”, on broad opposition electoral platform for the presidential election.

Jyrki Koskelo, Member Of The Supervisory Board, Gulf Marine Services PLC (UK), Senior Advisor, Chairman, Invest Solar Africa Pty (Botswana), Senior Advisor, Sofala Partners (UK), Member of the Supervisory Board, FIBank (Bulgaria), Member of the Board of Directors, Expobank CZ a.s. (Prague, Czech Republic), Austria. Jyrki Koskelo, an Emerging Market specialist, Senior Advisor and Member of Supervisory Boards, focused on ESG compatible development and growth through technology and innovative financial solutions. Jyrki Koskelo joined IFC ( International Finance Corporation, the private sector arm of the World Bank Group) in 1987 as a junior Investment officer and departed the organization as a Vice President responsible for Global Investment Operations in 2011. During the course of his career at IFC, the organization grew from less than $1 bn in investments globally to around $20 billion; a trend which highlights the role of private sector in driving the economic development in emerging markets. Jyrki sponsored IFC’s first Gender focused, highly successful investment programs to facilitate equal opportunities for women in emerging markets, multi billion dollar global trade programs

Gennandrea Mancone

Gennandrea Mancone, Visionary Entrepreneur Chairman, Arborea Living Switzerland.

Gennandrea Mancone is an Italian entrepreneur whose career has always been inspired by innovation in several fields, from textile to real estate markets. Right after his Master’s Degree in International Law he got involved in managing companies such as his family business that specialised in the production and transformation of textile material that served companies producing the most exclusive bed linens.


In 2006 he conceived ‘Arborea Living’, an ambitious project that aims at building a new neighborhood in Monza, a city in the outskirts of Milan.
That represented a remarkable switch: from running a production factory to imagining the construction of a small city. 

A complex project that requested a multidisciplinary evaluation starting with its feasibility from a financial and environmental point of view including all

Murat Bayizit, Managing Director of Tioga Foods Ltd, UK.

 Industry, he also has Academic background in Agricultural Economy and International Trading. 

He is proud to be V.President of Assembly in Bursa Chamber of Commerce and Industry to inspire entrepreneurs to see that foreign trading is the essential part of business and the future is Sustainable Food and Agriculture.

 Last but not least, he is the founder President of Turkish Frozen Food Association and the leader of Bursa Frozen Food Cluster.

Guillermo Diaz, Jr, Chairman, Hispanic Technology Executive Council (HITEC), USA.

Guillermo Diaz Jr. is a transformative global business leader and champion of inclusion and diversity. He now serves as the Chairman of the Hispanic Technology Council (HITEC), the premier global executive leadership organization of senior business and technology executives who have and are building outstanding careers in technology.

Diaz has most recently served as the CEO of Kloudspot, Inc., an innovative predictive AI and IOT analytics platform provider. He currently serves on the Board of Directors of Blue Shield of California.

Prior to these roles, he was a transformational innovator across Cisco Systems and broadly in the industry where he developed a strong track record for accelerating culture through people, process, and technology. Guillermo

Matteo Colangeli

Matteo Colangeli, Regional Director, Western Balkans at European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Serbia. As of May 2021, Matteo Colangeli has been appointed to the role of Regional Director for Western

 Balkans at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), based in Serbia. In his 16 years at EBRD, Matteo held a number of country management and banking positions in HQ, Ukraine, Bulgaria and Albania.

The EBRD has invested close to €14.2 billion in the Western Balkans to date, supporting the private sector, financial institutions, as well as energy and infrastructure projects. The Bank is working towards building green, inclusive, and digitalized economies in the region.

H.E. Prof. John Chrysoulakis is a distinguished academic and public management executive with an extensive international career in governance, education, and diplomacy. He is widely recognized for his leadership in public administration, international cooperation, and global philanthropic initiatives.

He holds a PhD in Engineering from Aristotle University and a Master of Science degree from the University of Minnesota. Throughout his academic career, he has taught at six universities in Greece and abroad and has authored more than 300 scientific publications. His academic and research contributions have significantly influenced public administration, technology development, and international collaboration.

Antonio Saraiva, President of CIP – The Portuguese Confederation of Business and Vice President of Business, Europe, Portugal. CIP represents over 160 thousand companies and Business Europe represents over 75 million companies all over Europe.

He has also dedicated over 30 years to associativism at the highest level and is known as a builder of bridges. Respected by politicians, the business community and the social sector he is constantly focused in the media and

Alfonso Vegara

Alfonso Vegara has a PhD in City and Regional Planning and degrees in Architecture, Economics, and Sociology. He was President of ISOCARP, the International Society of City and Regional Planners, which has members in over 70 countries. He is a Fellow and Trustee of the Eisenhower Fellowships, and since 2005, he is Honorary Consul General of Singapore in Madrid.

Alfonso Vegara has been lecturing Urbanism at the Escuela Técnica Superior de Arquitectura de Madrid, Universidad de Navarra, and Universidad CEU San Pablo. He was also a visiting scholar at the School of Design of the University of Pennsylvania and Advisor of ETH Zurich Polytechnic.

Meshack Kinyua Ndiritu

Meshack Kinyua Ndiritu, Alumnus of The Lindau Nobel Laureates Programme in Physics, Specialist in Space Systems, Space Applications Training expert with African Union Space Programme, African Union Commission, Ethiopia. 

Meshack is the Space Applications Training Officer at the African Union Commission. He oversees the institutional and human capacity development of the Global Monitoring for the Environment and Security in Africa (GMES & Africa) .which is a continental project in Earth Observation with a network of over 120 National and Regional institutions. Meshack’s emphasis has been on the integration of ICT with Earth Observation in areas like virtualization and cloud computing. GMES & Africa has redefined the delivery of Earth

 Observation services in the continent. Meshack is further acknowledged for his significant contribution to defining the African Outer Space Programme, and the subsequent establishment of the African Space Agency. He is passionate to see Emerging Nations play key roles in the Space 4.0, particularly in the cis-Lunar Economy. He is a graduate and a specialist in Space Systems in which he is contributing in global bodies of expertise. Educated in economics with degrees from universities in the UK and Italy, Milatović’s career spans both international finance and national governance. Before entering politics, he held a notable position at the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), where he worked on initiatives to bolster economic growth in emerging markets.
 
In Montenegro, Milatović gained recognition as Minister of Economic Development in 2020, championing policies aimed at reducing poverty, increasing wages, and promoting transparency. He co-founded the Europe Now Movement, a political platform committed to structural economic reforms and advancing EU membership for Montenegro. Elected President in 2023, Milatović continues to advocate for policies that improve living standards, reduce unemployment, and position Montenegro as a competitive economy within the European landscape.

His passion is about mining into the deeper layers of human creativity, thoughts and words to discover the causative elements of Human Evolution. This inherent capability has helped him to inspire and evolve tens of thousands of creative minds through various communication designs in last 30 years of his creative career . His residential workshops named TALENT WAKE-SHOPS and the film school named NEO FILM SCHOOL are highly successful and sustainable creative educational models established in 2010.

H.E Datuk Noureddine Ayed

H.E Datuk Noureddine Ayed, Chairman and Executive Director of the EAG Group of Companies, Tunisia. Which have offices in about 30 countries over the world/globally. He has over 4 decades of expertise in all facets of the industry with verifiable track record for the successful completion of multi-million-dollar projects through coordinating trades, developing partnerships and building positive rapports with engineers, local authorities and clients while maintaining costs. He also competent in contract negotiations, document preparation and site management.

He has assisted in obtaining within half a day all authorizations requested by the Defense Ministry, Ministry of Interior, Ministry of Transportation and Airport Authority to have the Malaysian C130 military plane land on the commercial airport of Tunis Carthage and had received all diplomatic delegations from the Malaysian Government and his courageous deeds and dedication continue until this day in order to uphold the dignity of men and women for the service of the Malaysian people.

Jeffrey S. Petty

Jeffrey S. Petty is a professor of entrepreneurship in the Faculty of Business and Economics at the University of Lausanne, Switzerland. He is the Director of the Department of Strategy, Globalization and Society, the Academic Director of the HEC UNIL Executive MBA programme, and the Co-founder and Academic Director of the UNIL HUB Entrepreneurship and Innovation. Jeffrey has an MBA in international management and a doctorate in management and his primary research interests include entrepreneurship and new venture financing, with a focus on equity crowdfunding, venture capital decision making, and venture debt. He has taught courses on corporate strategy, entrepreneurial finance, entrepreneurship, knowledge management, sustainable innovation, and technology and innovation management. Over the past twenty-five years Jeffrey has also worked with entrepreneurial organizations, ranging from start-ups and non-profit ventures to multi-national corporations, and has participated in all phases of the firm lifecycle, from concept development and initial fund raising to initial public offerings and acquisitions.

Dr. M. Muinul Hafiz

Dr. M. Muinul Hafiz, Chairman of Hearing Care Center Ltd, Global & Public Healthcare Expert, Bangladesh. With over 40 years of diversified experience in the healthcare sector along with a mission of helping those without means, Dr. M. Muinul Hafiz has contributed to the betterment of the people. He is considered an expert otorhinolaryngologist and is a UN enlisted ENT surgeon of global renown. Dr. Hafiz, with assistance from NGOs, has performed complicated surgeries free of charge in rural areas for underprivileged people who cannot afford to visit referral hospitals. For the last 12 years he has worked with hearing health to raise awareness and prevention advice for deafness, noise pollution and ear infection in children in rural areas. As an OPC consultant he regularly hosts an ENT camp in rural areas with a high poverty rate which focuses on helping underprivileged women and children. He is regularly featured on television talk shows to discuss ENT health related problems with the wider public. He regularly attends national and internal conferences, panel discussions and symposiums where he shares his knowledge with a global audience. Dr. Hafiz is the Chairperson of ENT Care Center and Hearing Care Center along with being the Chief Consultant (ENT) at Bangladesh Specialized Hospital.

Prof. Dr. René Schmidpeter

Prof. Dr. René Schmidpeter, Professor, Research University and Speaker, Germany. Professor René Schmidpeter is professor for Sustainable Management research professor at BFH in Bern, Switzerland and scientific researcher at Parmenides Foundation in Munich, Germany. He is guest professor/lecturer in USA, India, Australia, England and China. He is series editor for Springer’s CSR, Sustainability, Ethics and Governance books, editor of the Encyclopedia of Sustainable Management (ESM) as well as editor of the Dictionary of Corporate Social Responsibility (DCSR). His research and teaching activities focus on Sustainable Business Transformation, international perspectives on Sustainability, Social Innovation and Sustainable Entrepreneurship with special focus on the relationship between business and society.

He brings more than 15 years of research experience in nuclear materials, microstructural characterization, and alloy development. His work integrates large-scale experiments, micro- and nanoscale characterization techniques, and multiphysics modeling and simulation to solve complex problems in nuclear science and engineering.

Professor Short holds dual Bachelor of Science degrees in Nuclear Science and Engineering and in Materials Science and Engineering, both awarded by MIT in 2005. He continued his graduate studies at MIT, earning an M.S. in Materials Science and Engineering in 2010, and a Ph.D. in Nuclear Science and Engineering later that same year.

Actively participating in and influencing numerous operational details, he leverage a dual perspective to navigate both the intricate workings of day-to-day operations and the broader strategic vision of an organization. Emphasizing strong operational excellence, he is recognized as a growth expert in the field. He has strong expertise in leading fisheries company based on ESG for domestic and global market.

Dato’ James S.W Foo, Chairman & New Profits, Framework Creator, Authority Institute, Malaysia. In addition to his entrepreneurial endeavors, he has been entrusted with consulting and advisory roles for numerous prominent corporations, NGOs, and SMEs. Since then, he has worked in various state, international, and public organizations. He also hosts the T-Junction Podcast, a weekly show dedicated to entrepreneurship and business leadership.
