content_html:
Presence as Power: Lessons from the Paris Peace Forum

G100 Paris Peace Forum Meetings, France — 29–30 October 2025

 
 
In October 2025, the G100 Delegation was led at the Paris Peace Forum by Lucia de Luca, G100 Global Chair of Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation, at a gathering that felt more urgent than ever. In a world where conflicts are multiplying and violence is on the rise, the Paris Peace Forum 2025 wasn’t just another conference—it was a call to action. The honour of leading the G100 Delegation as Global Chair of Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation carried a deep sense of responsibility.
 
The Delegation arrived in Paris from different regions of the world to listen and to act. “It became clear that real change doesn’t happen behind screens; it happens in the rooms where decisions are made, where ideas clash, and where partnerships take shape,” said Lucia de Luca, commenting on the gathering.
Too often, there is an assumption that progress can be achieved through virtual engagement alone. 
 
The Forum served as a reminder that impact requires presence. It is about rebuilding connections, engaging in face-to-face discussions, and leaving with more than just business cards—it is about leaving with actionable next steps. The energy in those rooms was palpable: leaders from governments, civil society, and tech weren’t just talking; they were negotiating, challenging, and committing to solutions.
 
At the meeting, members discussed various topics, including the validity of the United Nations’ model. The question wasn’t whether the United Nations is still relevant, but how it can adapt. The consensus was clear: the veto system must evolve, financing models need overhaul, and collective action is non-negotiable. For the UN to remain effective, it must reflect today’s global realities—not those of 80 years ago. It is time for a Madame Secretary, a new kind of leadership that embraces complexity.
 
The call for more women in leadership wasn’t just about representation—it was about capability. As Michelle Bachelet pointed out, leadership in crisis demands systemic thinking, prevention, and the humility to admit that no single group has all the answers. The world doesn’t need more bravado; it needs leaders who can navigate chaos with wisdom and collaboration.
 
President John Dramani Mahama’s words resonated deeply: “80 years after the UN, Africa is still not at the table.” This isn’t just Africa’s fight—it is a reminder that global governance must be inclusive. Whether it’s health, finance, or tech, no region should be left out of the conversation.
The debate on AI governance was stark: liberal democracies must lead, or risk playing by someone else’s rules. Many speakers highlighted critical gaps in the current geopolitical landscape against the influence—or distortion—of AI. If Europe wants to shape AI’s future, it must move beyond internal divisions and propose bold solutions.
 
The discussions on AI were a wake-up call. Trust and safety can’t be an afterthought—they require investment, accountability, and open-source innovation. Listening to Jacinda Ardern, former Prime Minister of New Zealand, reinforced how her post-Christchurch actions proved that progress is a choice, not an accident. The message was clear: AI’s future must be shaped by all stakeholders—tech, governments, and civil society—together.
 
Special appreciation goes to the members of the delegation who demonstrated once again how impactful a group of determined leaders can be. Gratitude is extended to Patricia Elias, Nigara Mirdad, Raphael von Aulock, and Lucia de Luca for their commitment and leadership throughout the Forum.
 
Show Up – Real change happens where decisions are made.
Speak Up – If you have a seat at the table, use your voice.
Follow Up – Ideas without action are just words.
 
The Paris Peace Forum wasn’t just about listening—it was about owning the responsibility to act. As the world navigates an era of AI, geopolitical shifts, and climate crises, the choice becomes clear: Will society be a spectator, or will it be the force rewriting the rules? The answer begins with showing up—and then doing the work.
 
Convenors:
Lucia de Luca, G100 Global Chair, Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation Wing
Patricia Elias, G100 Global Chair, Government & Ministerial Advocacy Wing

content_html:
Shaping a New Era of Women’s Leadership in the Mediterranean

G100 Mediterranean Meetings, Alongside WEF, 30 October – 1 November 2025 

 
Three glorious days at the end of October 2025 shaped the G100 gathering alongside the WEF Mediterranean Meeting in Palermo. This landmark assembly brought together women leaders, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, and visionaries from across the Mediterranean and beyond. It was a moment where global aspirations met local cultural richness, showcasing how collective leadership, when rooted in shared values and mutual respect, can create profound and lasting impact. The collaboration between G100 and WEF Italy set the tone for a gathering that was not only celebratory but deeply forward-looking.

The city offered a symbolic and inspiring venue, as the Mediterranean Sea has shaped our past and continues to be the cradle of a shared future, where women fully lead, contribute, and transform. Palermo’s unique position—as a crossroads of civilizations, histories, and cultures—served as a reminder of the continuous exchange of ideas and resilience that define the region. Its ancient streets, vibrant communities, and storied landscapes framed a setting where discussions on leadership, peace, sustainability, and innovation felt especially meaningful. The Mediterranean spirit of connection, diversity, and strength resonated throughout the event.

This unique event was organized under the presidency of @Marilena Citelli Francese and under the aegis of Laura Mattarella, First Lady of Italy and President of the Honorary Committee of @Women Economic Forum Italia. Their leadership and patronage added prestige and credibility, reinforcing the importance of elevating women’s voices at national and international levels. Their commitment to promoting women-led development, intergenerational exchange, and collaborative progress helped shape the event’s visionary direction. Their presence also highlighted Italy’s deep dedication to gender equality and inclusive transformation.

The gathering provided opportunities for innovation, collaboration, and cultural exchange, connecting women leaders across borders to shape a more inclusive future. Participants engaged in high-level conversations, interactive workshops, and strategy-driven sessions that bridged diverse sectors—technology, diplomacy, sustainability, education, peacebuilding, and entrepreneurship. These encounters facilitated new alliances, strengthened existing networks, and inspired participants to imagine and design impactful initiatives. The environment was enriched by storytelling, shared wisdom, and a profound sense of sisterhood that transcended geographical boundaries.

The themes discussed reflected the breadth and depth of the challenges and opportunities shaping our world today. Pioneering Women celebrated those who are breaking barriers and redefining leadership. Climate Justice emphasized the urgent need for sustainable, community-driven environmental solutions. Feeding the Future addressed innovation in food systems, agriculture, and resilience. Healthcare Without Borders underscored the pursuit of accessible, equitable health systems. Algorithms and Truth opened critical conversations on digital ethics, misinformation, and AI governance. Space highlighted the importance of technological exploration and its role in future global cooperation. Peace and Security reinforced the central role of women in conflict prevention and nation-building. Educating for the Future focused on reimagining learning to prepare new generations for a rapidly evolving world.

Together, these themes created a tapestry of shared purpose and collective responsibility. They highlighted how women’s leadership is essential in addressing complex global issues and advancing sustainable development. Throughout the event, the energy was one of optimism and determination, as speakers and participants articulated visions of societies rooted in fairness, opportunity, and peace. The dialogues underscored that the Mediterranean region, long a meeting point of cultures and ideas, can once again lead the way in fostering human-centered transformation.

The G100 Mediterranean Meeting, together with WEF Italy, ultimately reaffirmed the power of unity, collaboration, and women-led change. It strengthened cross-border relationships, inspired impactful initiatives, and amplified the voices of women committed to shaping a better and more equitable future. As the Mediterranean continues to serve as a symbolic cradle of shared heritage, this gathering stood as a powerful reminder that women’s leadership—bold, compassionate, and visionary—is key to building a future where all can thrive.

Convenor:
Marilena Citelli Francese, G100 Global Advisory Council, Education, Employment & Scholarships Wing

G100 Peru Meetings, 15 October 2025 

World Food Day 2025 revealed the strength of a movement advancing across continents but driven by one shared purpose: the mission to end hunger through ethics, coordinated action, and global women’s leadership. In a world where millions still go to sleep without eating and where vast quantities of food continue to be lost, the G100 Zero Hunger Mission demonstrated that transformation becomes possible when communities, institutions, and ideas truly connect.
 
The commemoration began on October 15th in Piura, Peru, where the city became the first in the world to officially launch the G100’s global Zero Hunger activities. Under the leadership of Katty Vegas, Peru Country Chair of the G100 Zero Hunger Mission and Founder of CETURGH Peru, local authorities, academic institutions, social organizations, and the community gathered to reflect on the role of territories in the fight against food insecurity. Piura—a region rich in agricultural heritage yet facing persistent challenges—was transformed into a space of dialogue, commitment, and political will.

title: Kenya Meetings with High Tea, 4 October 2025
excerpt: Uniting Voices, Inspiring Change: A Women’s Leadership Gathering G100 Kenya… Read more
content_html:
Uniting Voices, Inspiring Change: A Women’s Leadership Gathering

G100 Kenya Meetings with High Tea, 4 October 2025

 
The G100 Kenya High Tea brought together 35 women, including Advisory Members, Country Chairs, Regional Chairs, and County Chairs across diverse sectors such as Agriculture, Global Networking, Poverty Eradication, Security & Defence, Coaching & Training, Renewable Energy, Financial Empowerment, Anti-GBV, Global Trade, and Business Acceleration. The gathering served as a dynamic platform for connection, inspiration, and the strengthening of collective purpose.
 
The meeting opened with a powerful message from Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of G100 and the ALL Ladies League. She reminded participants that “G100 is not just a network, it is a collective force of women’s voices, wisdom, and action. We are here to rise together, to connect across sectors and geographies, and to build an inclusive and sustainable future for all.”
 
Following this, the Global Chair of G100 Coaching & Training welcomed all participants and acknowledged Kenya’s strong engagement within the G100 movement. She emphasized the vital role of collaboration across the different wings as a key driver of collective impact and long-term success.
 
Ms. Vanessa Florence Roux, the Global Chair of the Coaching & Training Wing, then presented two flagship initiatives that will be developed in Kenya. The first is the Leadership Coaching Program for Women, created in partnership with the Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication Wing, to mentor women leaders and entrepreneurs by strengthening their capacity, resilience, and multiplier effect within their communities. The second initiative is the Hunger Relief Project at the Kakuma Refugee Camp, designed to embody G100’s humanitarian and sustainable development mission by providing nutrition, empowerment, and skills development for refugee women to help restore dignity and hope.
 
During the roundtable titled “Our Vision for Kenya,” participants engaged in a rich and dynamic discussion, sharing their reflections and aspirations focused on fighting poverty and inequality, advancing financial inclusion, enhancing education and youth training with a special emphasis on breast cancer awareness during October, strengthening security, defense, and peacebuilding, promoting innovation in renewable energy and climate responsibility, eradicating gender-based violence and sexual harassment, and empowering the next generation through sports, leadership, and networking. Many powerful insights emerged from the conversation, including statements such as “Collaboration is the new currency,” “Dignity starts with cash – our mission is to put money into women’s pockets,” “Each woman needs an ID – identity is empowerment,” “Legacy is better than titles – it is what we leave behind,” “We influence without making noise,” “Every woman is born with purpose,” and “Think about yourself as a brand – you always have something to offer.”
 
The session concluded with a guided meditation led by the Global Chair for Coaching & Training, focusing on harmony and collaboration across the wings. Participants were invited to embody presence, unity, and collective action. The meeting then transitioned into an elegant High Tea that encouraged informal dialogue, deeper personal connections, and the exploration of future collaborations.
 
The gathering was marked by strong participation from leaders representing diverse sectors, inspiring exchanges of vision, the introduction of impactful projects aligned with the G100 mission, and a renewed commitment to unity, solidarity, and meaningful action. The energy in the room demonstrated a shared dedication to advancing women’s empowerment and shaping a prosperous future for Kenya.
 
As the event drew to a close, participants collectively agreed on the need to develop a national roadmap for Kenya under the guiding theme “Fighting Economic Violence.” Planned follow-up actions include raising awareness to enable 100,000 women to obtain a national ID as part of the “Identity for All Women” initiative, and the development of Financial Inclusion Action Plans by each wing to empower women through improved access to finance, entrepreneurship opportunities, and sustainable livelihoods.
 
The G100 Kenya High Tea served as a transformative moment of connection and inspiration, offering a powerful springboard for bold initiatives that will uplift women, strengthen communities, and contribute to Kenya’s journey toward inclusive prosperity.
 
Convenor:
Vanessa Florence Roux
G100 Global Chair, Coaching & Training Wing

Expanding Women’s Leadership: Strengthening Networks in China.

G100 Shenzhen, China, Meetings, 29–30 September 2025

 

We are delighted to share the successful outcome of the G100 Shenzhen, China, Meeting, initiated by the G100 Business Accelerator Wings and hosted in collaboration with the Shenzhen City Women Entrepreneurship Promotion Association (SWS).
 
This meeting marks a significant first milestone in bringing the G100 network to China, expanding our global movement of women leaders, entrepreneurs, and change makers into one of the world’s most dynamic business ecosystems.
 
During this inspiring gathering, Ms. Zhang Huifen, Chairperson of SWS, was officially appointed and inaugurated as the G100 Business Accelerator China Country Chair by Diah Yusuf, Ph.D., G100 Global Chair for Business Accelerator.
 
The meeting was attended by passionate Shenzhen, China, women entrepreneurs, who showed great enthusiasm to connect globally through the G100 platform, opening doors for collaboration, innovation, and empowerment across borders.
 
As part of the visit, the delegation also toured Shenzhen SIPIMO Technology Group, a leading Chinese hair care treatment company founded by SWS member Ms. Zhu, showcasing the excellence of women-led innovation in China.
 
Another milestone achieved during this visit was the signing of an MOU between SWS and Indonesia Prima, marking a new chapter of partnership between Indonesia and China to strengthen cooperation in trading, entrepreneurship, and women’s economic development.
 
Together, we are building bridges of collaboration and advancing women’s leadership for a more inclusive and sustainable global economy.
 
Convenor:
Diah Yusuf
G100 Global Chair, Business Accelerator Wing

content_html:
Advancing Women’s Participation, Representation & Rights: A Multilateral Policy Dialogue.

G100 Multilateral Dialogue Webinar on Women’s Participation, 17 November 2025 

The Multilateral Dialogue on Women’s Participation, Representation & Rights brought together EU policymakers, civil society leaders, regional experts, and stakeholders from international organizations to examine the growing regression in gender equality and to strengthen collective action. The discussion highlighted rising global challenges, reviewed the EU’s policy responses, and emphasized strategies to promote women’s participation across governance, economic development, and peace and security spheres.
 
A shared concern emerged regarding renewed sexist narratives, persistent gender stereotypes, and increasing political backlash worldwide. In response, the European Commission reaffirmed its commitment to advancing women’s rights and introduced the Roadmap for Women’s Rights—a comprehensive, long-term policy framework endorsed by EU Member States and institutions. The roadmap outlines eight core principles addressing violence prevention, women’s health, education, political participation, economic empowerment, labor market inequities, digital inclusion, and the mainstreaming of gender considerations across all EU policies.
 
Gender equality was strongly framed as both a moral imperative and an economic necessity. Estimates indicate that closing gender gaps could add up to €3 trillion to Europe’s economy by 2050, underscoring the economic cost of inaction. Participants emphasized that empowering women strengthens democratic resilience, institutional trust, peace, and societal cohesion.

A shared concern emerged regarding renewed sexist narratives, persistent gender stereotypes, and increasing political backlash worldwide. In response, the European Commission reaffirmed its commitment to advancing women’s rights and introduced the Roadmap for Women’s Rights—a comprehensive, long-term policy framework endorsed by EU Member States and institutions. The roadmap outlines eight core principles addressing violence prevention, women’s health, education, political participation, economic empowerment, labor market inequities, digital inclusion, and the mainstreaming of gender considerations across all EU policies.
 
Gender equality was strongly framed as both a moral imperative and an economic necessity. Estimates indicate that closing gender gaps could add up to €3 trillion to Europe’s economy by 2050, underscoring the economic cost of inaction. Participants emphasized that empowering women strengthens democratic resilience, institutional trust, peace, and societal cohesion.
 
The dialogue also underscored enduring structural inequalities, such as gender pay and pension gaps, time poverty resulting from unequal care burdens, and heightened risks of poverty for older women. Addressing these barriers requires targeted policy interventions and systemic change.
 
Priority areas under the Women, Peace & Security (WPS) agenda included protecting women in conflict zones, increasing women’s representation in security and defense decision-making, and improving conditions for women in military roles. These measures are essential to ensuring inclusive and effective security policies.
 
The European Commission is developing the European Gender Equality Strategy 2026–2030, grounded in the roadmap’s principles and set for release in March 2026. This strategy will further integrate WPS priorities and invite contributions from civil society and stakeholders.
 
Participants highlighted challenges faced by women in conflict settings, women soldiers balancing multiple roles, rising digital violence, and barriers affecting women and girls with disabilities. The need for coordinated action and stronger policy implementation was emphasized.
 
Regional partners, including the Union for the Mediterranean (UfM), shared new initiatives such as the Regional Network on Climate, Women, Peace & Security. Developed with UNDP Arab States, the initiative aims to integrate gender perspectives into climate and security agendas and deepen cooperation across the Mediterranean region.
 
The meeting concluded by reaffirming the EU’s commitment to gender equality as a foundation for economic strength, democratic stability, and social well-being. Participants agreed on the urgency of countering backlash against gender equality and committed to inclusive policymaking, stronger civil society engagement, and robust multi-stakeholder partnerships. Dr. Harbeen Arora’s proposal to establish the dialogue as an annual event was welcomed as an important mechanism for monitoring progress and strengthening collaborative action.

Dr. Meenakshi Arora Dabral, G100 Global Chair, Global Alliances & Alumni Networks Wing
Cristina Cerioni, G100 Global Advisory Council, Global Alliances & Alumni Networks Wing

Côte d’Ivoire, 21 November 2025

 
 
The Noom Hotel Abidjan Plateau served as the venue on Friday, November 21, for the very first after work of the G100 First Ladies Outreach – Côte d’Ivoire. The gathering was coordinated by the Côte d’Ivoire Country Chair, First Ladies Outreach, Marie-France Kouakou, under the supervision and with the effective presence of H.E. Euphrasie Kouassi Yao, Global Chair of the G100 First Ladies Outreach Wing and holder of the UNESCO Chair “Water, Women and Decision-Making Power.”
 
In her remarks, Mrs. Euphrasie Yao recalled the special place occupied by Côte d’Ivoire within the network:
 
“Côte d’Ivoire has been honored by the G100, which brings together the 100 most influential women in the world. The newly appointed women of G100 Côte d’Ivoire are called upon to commit to equal opportunities between men and women, peace, advocacy, and all that hinders sustainable and inclusive development. Appointed for their dynamism and leadership, these exceptional women will be tasked with covering different regions of the country in order to positively impact communities, including those in the most remote areas. A total of 36 regional coordinators were officially presented during this after work, ready to join G100 initiatives and carry the voice of Ivorian women. The Global President of the G100 also urged these new leaders to strengthen their skills and to implement their actions in a concrete manner, particularly within local communities.”
 
“Côte d’Ivoire has developed a unique approach to gender and development. The women of the Ivorian section of the G100 must be familiar with the programs that have made our country the African Champion with the OECD. Leadership is built in the regions, in the villages. It was through my actions in Diatokro that I obtained the UNESCO Chair, being the only woman in Côte d’Ivoire to hold it,” she recalled.

Natalie Fort

Natalie Fort  

Natalie Fort is a distinguished Ghanaian broadcast journalist, media executive, global communicator, actress, and women’s leadership advocate, with over a decade of experience spanning journalism, media strategy, governance discourse, public affairs, and international convenings. She is widely recognized for her authoritative voice in foreign affairs, development journalism, and leadership communication across Africa and global platforms.

She began her professional journey at the age of 13 as a model and, by 15, represented Ghana at the Miss Princess of the World Pageant in Prague, Czech Republic—marking her early exposure to international platforms. Building on this global foundation, she later established The Fort Group, a diversified lifestyle, media, business facilitation, and humanitarian organization. The Group comprises Fort Media Consultancy (FMC), a media consultancy and advisory firm; Fort Art Gallery; the Natalie Fort Coaching & Mentorship Program; and The Fort Foundation, which focuses primarily on supporting the underprivileged, particularly through access to healthcare.

Natalie is a Senior Broadcast Journalist, News Anchor, and Foreign Affairs Correspondent. She began her broadcasting career with the TV3 Network of Media General, where, within less than a year, she rose to become one of the network’s lead news anchors, anchoring the flagship prime-time bulletin News 360. During her tenure, she worked on the International & General News Desk and hosted Women’s Take on 3FM (92.7), a program examining women’s influence on governance and public leadership in Ghana.

She currently serves as Senior Broadcast Journalist and Foreign Affairs Correspondent with GHOne TV and Starr FM, subsidiaries of EIB Network, Africa’s fastest-growing media group. She is also the host and executive face of the award-winning The Natalie Fort Show, which was named TV Development Show of the Year (2023) by the Radio and Television Personality (RTP) Awards for its contribution to development discourse, thought leadership, and impactful television programming. She has been a key anchor in the coverage of three general elections in Ghana, earning the trust of senior political leaders, policymakers, diplomats, and private-sector executives.

Her international reporting portfolio includes coverage of high-level global and continental forums such as the Doha Forum 2025 in Doha, Qatar, and the 47th Ordinary Session of the African Union, reinforcing her standing as a credible and respected voice in foreign affairs and governance journalism.

Beyond broadcasting, Natalie is an accomplished media strategist, communications advisor, and brand influencer. She is the Owner and Principal Consultant of Fort Media Consultancy (FMC) and has served as a brand influencer for leading organizations including Caveman Watches, Pepsodent Toothpaste, and All Smile Dental, among others. She also serves as a Partner and Advisory Board Member of the World Sustainability Organization and as Special Advisor to the Executive Chairman of the Sixteenth Council on Democracy, Human Rights and Rule of Law.

In February 2024, she hosted the Women Economic Forum in Lagos, Nigeria, convening women leaders, policymakers, and business executives to advance critical conversations on women’s economic empowerment and leadership across Africa.

Natalie is also an actress, having starred in House of Klu, a number-one rated Akwaaba Magic and Showmax series, expanding her influence across Africa’s media and creative industries. As a producer, she has led impactful documentary projects including Where Is Ghana Airways Today?, which examined the absence of a national carrier in Ghana, and Unkept, a documentary highlighting Ghana’s poor maintenance culture and the deterioration of public infrastructure.

She currently serves as the G100 Global Chair for Media, Arts & Communication, having previously held the role of Ghana Country Chair for the same wing. She is also the Ghana Ambassador for the GOTNI Leadership Centre, Africa’s leading leadership institute, and a recipient of the Executive Leadership Honour, presented at the GOTNI Leadership Centre CEO’s Leadership Roundtable 002. In addition, she is a Global Recognition Awards 2025 honouree, recognized for her role as an Ambassador for the Global Entrepreneurship Festival 2025.

Her leadership and impact have been recognized through numerous accolades, including Emerging Television Personality of the Year, Excellent Personality Merit Award, Gold Star Order of the Companion of Honour, Gold Star Order of Excellence, and the Distinctive Service to Humanity Medal. She is a member of the Ghana Feminine Hall of Fame, Patron of the Ghana Philanthropy Forum, and a leading advocate for women’s empowerment and ethical leadership.

Natalie is currently pursuing a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Media Leadership with the University of Cumbria (UK). At the core of her work is a deep commitment to empowering women and young people across Africa—shaping narratives that influence policy, inspire leadership, and drive inclusive development—embodying her philosophy of raising a generation of “Women Who Work.”

The exhibition highlighted how creativity can serve as a bridge across cultures and a catalyst for understanding in an increasingly complex global landscape.
 
Over the two-day exhibition, visitors experienced a rich and diverse collection of artworks spanning multiple disciplines and artistic expressions. Each piece reflected personal narratives and collective realities, offering perspectives on identity, coexistence, social justice, and the evolving role of art in shaping global consciousness. Lucia Fernandes Stanislas is a social innovation strategist, entrepreneur, and ecosystem builder with over 20 years of experience fostering inclusive development across Angola, the United States, and the Global South. She is the founder of Mwika Social Innovation Hub and Impactify, a Silicon Valley–accelerated SaaS platform that empowers mission-driven organizations to measure and scale their impact.

Through her proprietary Impact Thinking™ methodology, she equips changemakers with the tools to design, measure, and communicate sustainable impact. Her pioneering approach has positioned her as a trusted voice in advancing entrepreneurship, innovation, and cross-border collaboration.

Recognized among the 100 Most Influential Women in Angola, she is celebrated as part of the nation’s Golden Generation and has been honored by the First Lady of Angola. These distinctions highlight her commitment to driving systemic change and her influence in shaping inclusive growth across regions.

Beyond her entrepreneurial ventures, she serves as Regional Ambassador for Lusophone Africa at WEDO and has contributed her expertise through corporate board roles. Her leadership continues to inspire networks of innovators, leaders, and organizations dedicated to creating sustainable impact.

She completed her formal education in Atlanta, Georgia, where she specialized in Computer Information Systems, Organizational Communication, and Philosophical Studies. Her multidisciplinary background informs her holistic approach to innovation and development.

Women at the Forefront of Global Diplomacy and International Trade

G100 Singapore Diplomatic Meetings 2026, 30 January 2026

 
Singapore hosted the G100 Diplomatic Meetings 2026, a high-level diplomatic and economic dialogue that also marked the official launch of the WICCI Singapore–India Business Council. The meetings strengthened India–Singapore cooperation while advancing women-led leadership across diplomacy, trade, and innovation.
 
The meetings brought together ambassadors, high commissioners, senior diplomats, policymakers, global women leaders, and business representatives, positioning women at the centre of cross-border collaboration and inclusive economic growth.
 
The event was hosted by Dr. Meenakshi Arora Dabral, Global Chair – G100 Global Alliances & Alumni Network and President of the WICCI Singapore–India Business Council. Tanishq Singapore was the Purpose Sponsor Partner for the meetings.
 
The programme was conceptualised by The Mandala Global.
 
Speaking on the purpose of the platform, Dr. Dabral stated that it was created to move beyond dialogue and deliver outcomes, including market access, mentorship, policy engagement, and cross-border partnerships for women-led enterprises.
 
The G100 Diplomatic Meetings 2026 witnessed the esteemed presence of Her Excellency Ms. Puja Tillu, Deputy High Commissioner of India to Singapore; Her Excellency Ms. Francesca Umayuli, Ambassador of Nigeria to Singapore; Her Excellency Ms. Jessica Lopez, Ambassador of Venezuela to Singapore; His Excellency Mr. Tadeusz Chomicki, Ambassador of Poland to Singapore; His Excellency Mr. Senarath Dissanayake, High Commissioner of Sri Lanka to Singapore; and Her Excellency Ms. Madiepetsane Charlotte Lobe, High Commissioner of South Africa to Singapore. The Ambassador of Chile was unable to attend due to prior commitments.
 
A key highlight of the programme was the keynote address by Her Excellency Ms. Puja Tillu, who spoke on India’s commitment to inclusive growth and the evolving role of women in diplomacy and international trade.
 
The meetings also featured presidential and global addresses by Datin Dr. Hartini Osman, G100 President for 2026.
 
The platform is founded on the vision of Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of G100 and the Women Economic Forum, a globally respected leader in women’s empowerment and inclusive economic development. She conceptualised G100 as a global, action-oriented network of women leaders across sectors, regions, and policy domains, and her work continues to influence global dialogue on gender parity, ethical leadership, and collaborative growth.
The panel discussions and fireside chats featured distinguished speakers and thought leaders including Becky Low; Yan Ping, CEO of the Singapore Council of Women’s Organisations; Dr. Dragana Vujovic Djermanovic; Judit Pach; Fi Dinh; Gunridh Sila; Yingying Li; and Alexandra Vidyuk. Discussions centred on closing the funding gap for women-led enterprises, women and artificial intelligence, future-ready economies, and the role of diplomacy in enabling inclusive and sustainable growth.
 
The meetings also recognised exceptional leadership and global contribution. Her Excellency Ms. Charlotte Lobe was honoured with the Women of the Decade Award, while Dato’ Dr. Laila Rani received the Women of Excellence Award.
 
The G100 Diplomatic Meetings 2026 were supported by Tanishq as the Purpose Partner, aligned with a shared vision of women’s empowerment, leadership, and long-term social impact.
 
The WICCI Singapore–India Business Council has been established to support women entrepreneurs and MSMEs, facilitate bilateral trade and investment, enable mentorship, policy advocacy, and market access, and strengthen India–Singapore economic collaboration through women-led leadership.
Through the Sheconomy Launchpad, homegrown Singapore brands Mandala Spices, Elanearth, Nara, and House of Gulal received the opportunity to showcase their collections.
 
The G100 Diplomatic Meetings 2026 and the launch of the WICCI Singapore–India Business Council reaffirm Singapore’s role as a global hub for diplomacy, innovation, and inclusive economic dialogue, while placing women leaders at the forefront of shaping future global economies.
 
The event was executed by Tatva Productions, founded by Natasha Singh

Dr. Meenakshi Arora Dabral

charlene doak-gebaure

Charlene Doak-Gebauer

Charlene Doak-Gebauer is the Founder and Chair of the federal Canadian charity Internet Sense First, as well as the AICET Council (Anti-Internet Child Exploitation Team). She is an internationally recognized expert in child protection, specializing in proactive strategies for safeguarding children in the digital world. Through her leadership, advocacy, and research, she has become a prominent global voice in online child and family safety.

She is the author of two influential books on digital child protection. Her first book, Digital Sexual Victims: True Cases, earned her a nomination for an international award by the Delta Kappa Gamma Society of Educators. Her most recent publication, The Internet: Are Children In Charge?, further explores the challenges of digital exposure and responsibility. Both books are distributed through more than 40,000 channels worldwide, extending her reach to educators, policymakers, parents, and child-protection professionals globally.

The core objective of Charlene’s organizations is to educate the public on her Theory of Digital Supervision, a proactive framework designed to prevent online child exploitation before harm occurs. In addition to education and advocacy, Internet Sense First provides funding for therapy to support victims of internet-based child exploitation, ensuring both prevention and healing remain central to its mission.

Charlene is a global speaker and keynote presenter, frequently invited to address audiences at Crime Stoppers events, schools, teacher conferences, corporate forums, and international conferences. She has delivered presentations across Canada (including Parliament Hill), the United States, Iceland, Europe, and India, and has been featured on numerous radio and television programs for her expertise in digital child safety.

An award-winning Producer and Director, Charlene recently produced the documentary Vulnerable Innocence, which has received multiple international awards. The documentary is grounded in her Theory of Digital Supervision and powerfully highlights the urgent need for proactive, systemic approaches to online child protection.

Charlene is educated at four distinguished institutions: the University of New Brunswick, the University of Western Ontario, the University of Toronto, and the University of California, Santa Barbara. Her academic background supports a holistic, multidisciplinary approach, which she applies consistently in her research, advocacy, and public engagement.

Her commitment to this cause is deeply personal. Charlene’s family was affected by child pornography crimes on two separate occasions, involving two different family members in two different cities. One family member was only four years old when exploited by neighbors who created inappropriate images and videos. That same family member later lived life with remarkable individuality, only to be tragically killed by a drunk driver at the age of twenty-two. These experiences shaped Charlene’s lifelong dedication to child protection.

She founded Internet Sense First in memory of her family member and in solidarity with victims worldwide. A devoted Soul Sister to survivors and a tireless advocate for safer societies for children, Charlene continues to champion the establishment of strong, global standards for childcare and digital protection policies, working relentlessly to ensure a safer future for children everywhere.

Neaz Adnan is the Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Your House Social Enterprise INC, Canada, a creative social enterprise dedicated to empowering children and youth through education, arts, culture, and community-driven initiatives. She has been leading the organization since its inception in December 2019, shaping its vision and strategic direction with purpose and impact.

She holds a Master’s degree from the University of Windsor, Ontario, Canada, and is a seasoned business professional with diverse cross-sector experience. Her academic foundation, combined with practical leadership exposure, enables her to navigate both corporate and social enterprise ecosystems effectively.

Neaz brings over seven years of experience in the food, beverage, and five-star hotel industry, where she developed strong operational, service excellence, and people-management capabilities. This corporate background has significantly influenced her leadership style, emphasizing quality, efficiency, and stakeholder satisfaction.

In addition, she has 18 years of experience in community development, working closely with diverse communities to design and deliver inclusive programs that foster growth, engagement, and social cohesion. She also has two years of experience in strategic partnerships within the nonprofit sector in North America, where she served as a Regional Head, strengthening collaborations and expanding organizational reach.

As Co-Founder & CEO, Neaz leads Your House Social Enterprise INC by developing high-quality business strategies and execution plans aligned with both short-term and long-term objectives. She actively motivates and mentors her teams, driving employee engagement and nurturing a high-performing managerial culture grounded in purpose, creativity, and accountability.

Your House Social Enterprise INC operates as an integrated platform designed to inspire and uplift young minds through books, shows, festivals, multicultural events, inspirational and educational programs, documentaries, and films—all under one roof. The organization is committed to creating safe, inclusive spaces where children and youth can express themselves, learn, and thrive without limitations.

At the core of Neaz’s leadership philosophy is her vision of a world free from negativity, boundaries, discrimination, and violence. She is deeply passionate about providing a safe and empowering platform for all children and youth, enabling them to soar, dream boldly, and realize their full potential. Through her work, she aspires to bring smiles, happiness, and joy to millions of children and young people across the globe.

content_html:
Advancing Women-Led Global Economic Transformation Through Strategic Collaboration

G100 – Davos Diaries 2026, Switzerland, 18-23 January 2026

 
 
G100 emerged as a leading convener and catalyst for women-led systemic transformation during the Davos engagements, positioning itself at the intersection of global policy, finance, diplomacy, and impact-driven collaboration. Through a series of high-level meetings, strategic dialogues, and curated convenings, G100 advanced its mission to connect leaders, accelerate collaboration, and translate vision into action—anchored by the introduction and advancement of the Global Women’s Bank (GWB) as a flagship initiative.
 
In close partnership with Ahead, under the leadership of Lucia de Luca, Global Chair of Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation at G100, G100 leveraged the Davos platform to engage senior policymakers, diplomats, business leaders, investors, and global institutions. The Ahead Spark Night Dinner set the tone for these engagements, bringing together Nobel Laureates, senior diplomats, and private-sector leaders in an environment designed to foster trust, strategic alignment, and long-term collaboration. Ahead played a pivotal role in facilitating targeted introductions and meetings with prospective strategic partners for the Global Women’s Bank.
 
Strategic dialogues included meetings with Anou Lunia Singhvi, Founder of The Invisible Thread, and with the Uttar Pradesh Finance Minister at the Pavilion of India, reinforcing the integration of public policy, global trade, and women-led financial innovation. The Women Leaders Reception at the Ameron Resort Hotel further strengthened cross-sector and cross-regional connections among women leaders shaping global economic and social agendas.
 
G100’s commitment to measurable, impact-driven collaboration was further advanced through the Business Avengers initiative—conceived as a task-force multiplier leveraging technology and artificial intelligence to recalibrate collective action. Engagements with the Bezos Earth Fund, Fast Forward, Northly, Accenture, and partners from the United Nations ecosystem provided opportunities to formally present key strategic documents, including the GWB framework, the WEF ASEAN Resolution, the YBK Ecosystem Book, and the report “G100 – 100 Days to Connect and Collaborate.” These discussions focused on scaling solutions, mobilizing capital, and aligning global stakeholders around shared outcomes.
 
The agenda further expanded through G100’s participation in the WE Lead Women Leadership Lounge, organized in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, with a central focus on unlocking women’s economic participation. Within this forum, Dr. Hartini formally handed over the Global Women’s Bank (GWB) proposal to Sally A. Paull, Executive Vice President of Human Resources (EVP HR), Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Tarrytown, New York, inviting engagement through integrated platforms for financial inclusion, enterprise development, and sustainable impact.
 
Thought leadership remained a defining feature of the G100 presence. A masterclass by Anou Lunia Singhvi offered nuanced insights into invisible systems shaping global value chains and influence. This was complemented by participation in the Human Change Foundation House Reception, marking the launch of the documentary Your Attention Please. Engagements with Tristan Harris, Founder of the Human Change Foundation, and Ileana, its Executive Director, facilitated meaningful dialogue at the intersection of technology, ethics, and human-centered systems, with the Global Women’s Bank presented as a timely and transformative response.
 
G100 further strengthened its engagement with global finance and investment leaders through meetings with Linda Pereira, G100 Global Chair for Communication, Advocacy & Mediation, during an Investment Migration Council convening. A strategic lunch hosted by Zurich Asia Pacific, led by Tulsi Naidu, CEO Asia Pacific and Group Executive Committee Member, convened senior leaders from Deutsche Bank, JP Morgan, and the international investment community at Goals House Davos. Moderated by Bettina of CNN, discussions centered on strengthening climate resilience across Asia Pacific’s critical infrastructure, highlighting the role of sustainable finance in long-term economic stability.
 
Diplomatic engagement remained a core pillar of the G100 agenda. Meetings with Dato’ Guna Mahalingam, Honorary Consul of Malaysia, and Nor Azman Taib, Chargé d’Affaires of the Embassy of Malaysia in Berne, provided platforms to present the G100 and Global Women’s Bank vision to diplomatic and business audiences through the SWISSCHAM Davos programme. Informal cultural engagements, including the Grand Indonesia Night, further reinforced global solidarity, trust, and shared purpose.
 
The Davos engagements culminated at the Ahead Davos Headquarters with a G100 High-Level Meeting, where Dr. (h.c.) Hartini Osman, G100 Club Global President, hosted the Mission Million Coffee Hour. During this gathering, Dr. Osman articulated a compelling vision for a World Bank for Women, alongside the presentation of the strategic report “100 Days to Connect and Collaborate.” This exchange underscored the power of community-led leadership, cross-sector collaboration, and visionary thinking in shaping global systems.
 
The collaboration between G100 and Ahead was further reinforced by the leadership of Lucia de Luca, CEO and Co-Founder of Ahead, in her role as Global Chair of Pay Parity & Corporate Transformation at G100. Collectively, these engagements reaffirmed a shared commitment to advancing equity, leadership, and systemic transformation, while underscoring the indispensable role of women in shaping the conversations, decisions, and institutions that will define our shared global future.
 
Convenors:
Datin Dr. (H.C) Hartini Binti Osman, G100 Global Chair, Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication Wing

excerpt: Leave No One Behind: Advancing Inclusion for Women and Girls… Read more
content_html:
Leave No One Behind: Advancing Inclusion for Women and Girls with Disabilities in the SDG Era

G100 France Meetings alongside AAEEH, 9 October 2025

 
On October 9, as part of the celebration of the International Day of the Girl Child and the activities organized around the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) Week, the Association d’Aide à l’Education de l’Enfant Handicapé (AAEEH) hosted an international conference at the French National Assembly and online. The conference gathered global experts, policymakers, and advocates to discuss inclusive education, gender equality, and disability rights within the framework of the SDGs.

Five years before the 2030 SDG deadline, the event aimed to revisit SDGs 4 (Quality Education), 5 (Gender Equality), 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), 10 (Reduced Inequalities), and 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) in relation to disability and the empowerment of girls and women with disabilities. The main objective was to identify concrete ways to fulfill the global promise of “leaving no one behind” by 2030 through the collaboration of multiple stakeholders from government, international organizations, and civil society.

French Member of Parliament Céline Hervieu, G100 Founder Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, and G100 SDG Wing Chair France and President of the Association d’Aide à l’Education de l’Enfant Handicapé (AAEEH), Dr. Ernestine NGO MELHA, delivered the opening remarks. Their messages highlighted the urgency of addressing inequalities faced by women and children with disabilities and the need for inclusive policies that prioritize access to education, equal opportunities, and social participation for all.

A roundtable discussion, moderated by Dr. Ernestine NGO MELHA, provided a platform for in-depth analysis of the progress and persistent challenges related to the inclusion of people with disabilities in educational settings, policy-making, and international development initiatives. Experts from UNESCO, AFD – French Development Agency, Handicap International – Humanity & Inclusion, MINAH (Togo), AAEEH, and G100, along with participants from different countries, shared successful experiences, best practices, and innovative solutions for advancing inclusive education and gender equality.

The discussions emphasized that inclusion goes far beyond accessibility—it encompasses representation, full participation, and visibility from an early age. Participants agreed that empowering girls and women with disabilities requires breaking barriers, promoting leadership, and ensuring that their voices are heard in decision-making spaces.

Key Takeaways:

The inclusion of persons with disabilities goes beyond accessibility; it is also a matter of representation, full participation, and visibility from a young age.

A holistic, intersectional, multisectoral, and multi-stakeholder approach is necessary to define policies, implement programs and initiatives, and ensure that disability situations are adequately considered in all aspects of development.

The conference concluded with a guided tour of the National Assembly, symbolizing openness, participation, and the shared commitment to building an inclusive society where everyone—regardless of ability or gender—has an equal opportunity to thrive.

Convenor:
Ernestine Melha
G100 France Country Chair, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGS) Wing

content_html:
Shaping Tomorrow’s World Through Women-Led Leadership for an Inclusive and Sustainable Future

G100 Global Summit 2025, Lisbon, Portugal, 11-12 Dec 2025    

 
The G100 Global Summit, held online over two consecutive days in December and broadcast live from Lisbon, brought together women leaders, decision-makers, experts, and changemakers from across the world for a high-level global dialogue on leadership, sustainability, innovation, advocacy, and social impact. Convened under the auspices of the G100 network, the Summit served as a dynamic international platform to amplify women’s voices, foster cross-sector collaboration, and contribute to shaping a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable future.
 
The event was chaired by Global President Bodil Valero and presented by Linda Pereira, Global Chair for Communication, Advocacy & Mediation, and Eliana Medeiros, UK Country Chair for Communication, Advocacy & Mediation. Their leadership and vision were instrumental in shaping both the strategic direction and the overall tone of the Summit. The Summit was organized by CPL Events & Consultancy and delivered through a live digital broadcast via the BeThere Global platform, which partnered with the G100 Global Summit to ensure a seamless, high-quality online experience and enable global participation across multiple regions and time zones.
 
The Summit opened with Linda Pereira, who set the conceptual and strategic framework for the two-day programme and reaffirmed the role of communication, advocacy, and mediation as catalysts for global change. This was followed by welcome remarks from Bodil Valero, G100 President at the time, and Harbeen Arora Rai, Founder of the G100, who reinforced the global mission, shared values, and collective ambition of the G100 network.
The Opening Ceremony also featured a special institutional message from the Honourable Portuguese Deputy Minister for Youth and Equality, Carla Rodrigues, underlining the relevance of the Summit’s themes at policy level and highlighting Portugal’s commitment to gender equality, inclusive leadership, and youth empowerment.
 
All sessions of the G100 Global Summit remain fully available on demand, allowing both participants and new viewers to watch or rewatch the content at their own pace. Participants who attended the live event may access the recordings by signing in with the same credentials used during the Summit, ensuring continued access to all plenary sessions, panels, parallel tracks, and workshops.
 
Those who did not participate in the live event may also access the full content by visiting the official event webpage, where they can register on the platform and follow the instructions provided to gain access to the sessions. All sessions, information, and access are available via the BeThere platform through the official website of the event at https://g100globalsummit.org/. This extended on-demand availability reinforces the Summit’s commitment to inclusivity, continuity, and knowledge sharing, ensuring that its insights, discussions, and outcomes remain accessible to a global audience beyond the live event dates.
 
The first day explored leadership mindsets for the 21st century, authentic leadership, and alliance-building in times of global uncertainty. Early sessions addressed women’s participation in political life, ethical leadership grounded in values, attention as a transformative force, and collective responsibility in reshaping narratives around women and power.
 
A high-level G100 panel examined how women leaders navigate a rapidly changing global landscape, followed by discussions on building trust, purpose-driven leadership, and the importance of character before competence. The afternoon programme unfolded through parallel thematic sessions focusing on leadership lessons drawn from global and historical perspectives, peacebuilding and sustainability, strategic communication as a leadership tool, and women’s empowerment through resilience, entrepreneurship, and innovation.
 
The first day concluded with a session dedicated to mental health, reinforcing the message that women’s wellbeing is not merely an individual concern, but a collective and structural leadership responsibility.
 
The second day shifted the focus towards impact creation, advocacy, and the future of the global economy, with a strong emphasis on women-led solutions. Parallel sessions addressed women leading in times of pressure, transformation, and reinvention, as well as food systems, food security, environmental sustainability, human development, hunger-free world initiatives, intersectionality, community impact, and regenerative approaches.
 
Further sessions explored women’s leadership in innovation, artificial intelligence, the digital economy, and global governance, alongside discussions on freedom from violence, wellbeing, and economic empowerment. A dedicated session showcased women-led businesses and global acceleration initiatives, highlighting pathways from local insight to global impact and reinforcing the importance of collaborative, international ecosystems.
 
The Summit also created space for reflection and creativity, including a meditative art experience designed to reconnect leadership with inner awareness, balance, and purpose. The programme concluded with a session on advocacy-driven leadership, strengthening women’s voices in the global economy, followed by a Closing Ceremony that brought together the hosts to reflect on shared insights, commitments, and the collective responsibility to translate dialogue into action.
 
The G100 Global Summit reaffirmed the power of women-led dialogue, cooperation, and action at a global level. By convening diverse voices across regions, sectors, and disciplines, the Summit created a meaningful space for exchange, inspiration, and strategic alignment. More than an event, the G100 Global Summit stood as a collective call to action, underscoring that shaping tomorrow’s world requires courageous leadership, inclusive policies, and sustained collaboration, with women firmly at the centre of global transformation.
 
Convenor:
Linda Pereira, G100 Global Chair, Communication, Advocacy & Mediation Wing
Bodil Valero, G100 Globel Security & Defence Wing and Global President 2025

The evening was alive with energy—rich conversations, meaningful connections, warm embraces, and a shared sense of purpose filled the space, reflecting the strength of this growing community.
 
The celebration was further enriched by the presence of leaders from other G100 UK Wings, including Tanya Hadzhieva and Maria Asuncion, underscoring the spirit of collaboration and unity that defines the G100 movement.
 
Taking the stage, UK Chair Effie Kanyua outlined the Wing’s bold vision for 2026. In a world where women are increasingly marginalised by geopolitical forces, the rise of biased and unsafe AI technologies, and persistent systemic inequalities, she emphasized the urgent need for women to stand together—supporting, amplifying, and protecting one another.
 
A standout moment of the evening was the launch of the “Give 100. Gain a Future” campaign. This powerful initiative calls on members to dedicate 100 hours of their time and expertise toward coaching, mentoring, strategic guidance, or pro bono contributions, transforming collective wisdom into meaningful action and long-term impact.
 
Perfectly aligned with this year’s International Women’s Day theme, “Give to Gain,” the campaign will anchor the Wing’s upcoming IWD engagements, bringing the community together through shared contribution and purpose.
 
As G100 UK MAC continues to grow, it remains committed to building an influential and inclusive network of women leaders across media, arts, and communications. With ambitious expansion plans ahead, women who share this vision are warmly invited to connect with Effie Kanyua or Shelley Stuart to explore membership opportunities.
 
The evening concluded with sincere appreciation for the G100 MAC UK Board, and special recognition for Andrea Zara, whose leadership and dedication delivered an unforgettable celebration—one that captured the essence, momentum, and promise of G100.

Advancing Justice-Centered Governance for a Sustainable Global Future

G100 Global Dialogue – UN Headquarters Along with Global  Conference on Peace, Governance & Sustainable Development, USA, 4 February 2026

    

A distinguished G100 Global Strategy Dialogue was convened at the United Nations Headquarters, New York, under the leadership of the G100 Law & Justice Wing. The dialogue brought together global legal and policy leaders to examine the critical intersections of law, justice, and sustainable development in an increasingly complex global landscape.

The session was led by Hon. Carmen Velasquez, Justice of the Supreme Court of New York and G100 Global Chair – Law & Justice, whose leadership set the tone for an insightful and forward-looking dialogue. Discussions focused on reinforcing justice-centered governance, strengthening institutional accountability, and advancing legal frameworks that uphold equity, inclusion, and the rule of law as foundational pillars of sustainable development.

Participants explored how robust justice systems play a vital role in addressing systemic inequalities, protecting human rights, and enabling economic and social resilience. Emphasis was placed on the need for gender-responsive legal policies, cross-border cooperation, and multi-stakeholder engagement to effectively respond to global challenges and support long-term development goals.

The dialogue also highlighted the importance of aligning legal institutions with global sustainability agendas, ensuring that justice remains central to policy formulation, implementation, and international cooperation. Meaningful exchanges and shared insights underscored the role of women leaders in shaping transformative legal reforms and fostering ethical and inclusive decision-making at national and international levels.

This high-level engagement reaffirmed G100’s commitment to advancing principled leadership, inclusive justice systems, and collaborative global action. Outcomes from the dialogue will inform future initiatives, advocacy efforts, and strategic engagements led by the G100 Law & Justice Wing, contributing to a more just, equitable, and sustainable world.

Convenor:

H.E. Justice Carmen R. Velasquez, G100 Global Chair, Law & Justice Wing

title: Overview: The Global Chair Role
excerpt: The global chair role G100 Club comprises 100 wings. Each… Read more
content_html:
The global chair role  

G100 Club comprises 100 wings. Each wing is led by a Global Chair. 

Role: 

The Global Chair is a senior leadership role within the G100 ecosystem, designed for accomplished global leaders who wish to contribute their commitment, creativity, consciousness, and calibre toward advancing the mission of G100: strengthening women’s leadership in all walks of life and bridging gender gaps.

Global Chairs act as strategic stewards and thought leaders, role models and activators, community builders and system changers, guiding the direction of their respective wings and inspiring leadership globally across 100 countries.

The role of the Global Chair includes wing building, network stewardship, evolving recommendations and actions, convening meetings, presenting G100 at various conferences, designing wing campaigns, guiding country chairs’ initiatives, et al.

Each chair also has a partner male ally (Denim Club) to help bridge gaps in gender solidarity. We also have an ELLEGOSSSE framework with 10 policy principles covering 100 recommendations that can be further followed up by the wings. Together, we drive change as a global solidarity for gender equality.

Invitation as a Global Chair is upon nomination by the G100 Secretariat, and we also welcome recommendations from fellow Global Chairs. Membership is free.

The role of a Global Chair is a high-visibility role with privileged access to fellow Global Chairs and senior leaders through the network and its meetings.

Actions: 

Denim Club: The Global Chair nominates one Denim Club Global Partner—an influential He-for-She champion in support of the Global Chair and the wing.

Country Chairs: Each Global Chair nominates 100 women in 100 countries, one in each country, as Country Chair for the wing. Likewise, each Country Chair nominates 100 women in her country, and so on. Each wing thus develops 10,000 members at optimal capacity across 100 countries. When 100 wings achieve this, we will have one million gender champions worldwide working in synergy and solidarity across every sector of the economy and society.

Global Advisory Council: The Global Chair constitutes a Global Advisory Council—an honorary council of 20–100 distinguished leaders across geographies and sectors, including male allies—to support the Global Chair in leading and building the wing’s impact and influence.

Convening Country Clubs: The Global Chair may also convene country clubs of all wings where they are resident. For example, a Global Chair residing in Sweden can support and guide the G100 country clubs—i.e., all wings represented by country chairs therein, comprising all other local chairs and members. Together, they can plan outreach programmes with local authorities and institutions, strengthening partnerships and policy influence, becoming influential actors through collective power, reaping inter-wing synergies, interdisciplinary intelligence, and interconnected impact.

Practices:

The Global Chair sets the vision and strategy, as well as quantitative and qualitative milestones, in resonance with G100 guidelines. Regarding wing coordination, the Global Chair is welcome to set the rhythm as convenient and suited to their leadership style.

Best practices include:

• Making a roadmap for a two-year tenure with priority areas, policy pillars, key initiatives, milestones, and outcomes.

• Mobilising collective leadership, encouraging all country chairs to present their own roadmaps, weaving co-creation and collaboration with global vision and grassroots engagement.

• Setting up a strong Global Advisory Council, with members internally allocated roles such as wing coordination, social media presence, identifying new country chairs, scheduling a global calendar of events with country chairs, designing digital campaigns, and exploring inter-wing synergies, et al.

• Involving the leadership of the Global Denim Club Partner to empower He-for-She allyship and support.

• Creating a social media page for the wing and a roster for country chairs to plan digital posts, enhancing the work and visibility of the wing, including introductions of all wing chairs and members.

• Engaging with institutional partners such as universities and corporates, and envisaging joint programmes.

• Presenting G100 at local, international, and multilateral events and conferences.

• Collaborating with the Global President and fellow Global Chairs to strengthen cross-wing synergies.

• Collaborating with the SHEconomy app team for digital support and amplification of specific events and summits, and using the app’s tools for co-working, etc.

Tenure: 

• Appointment is for two years, with potential renewal or transition to an advisory role.

• The role is honorary and voluntary, infused with a genuine and generous spirit of sisterhood, solidarity, service, and stewardship.

• Time commitment is flexible and aligned with one’s strategic perspective, networking prowess, and organisational deployment.

• The Global Chair may review the tenures of Country Chairs or change any wing roles at any time in the wing’s interest.

G100 Secretariat Coordination 

• The Secretariat invites and welcomes the G100 Global Chair and the Denim Club Global Partner on official social platforms, as nominated by the Global Chair.

• The Global Chair sends recommended candidates (Country Chairs, Global Advisory Council members) to the G100 Secretariat with their names, emails, countries, social media links, and wing roles. The Secretariat then sends formal invitation letters and social media banners to the nominated candidates.

• The Secretariat features all banners of chairs on the official website.

• The Global Chair welcomes Country Chairs on wing or personal social media, and Country Chairs similarly welcome their State Chairs, and so on, reflecting distributed leadership—a key feature of our organisational system.

• Enclosed presentation link for an in-depth overview and guidelines: https://www.g100.in/G100-Brochure.pdf


For queries or support, please contact:

Secretariat: Secretariat@g100.in

Advancing Women’s Leadership in Energy, Mining, and Sustainable Development in South Africa

G100 South Africa – Strategic Meetings alongside Africa Energy Indaba 2026, 3 – 5 March    

 

Through the G100 Global Women Leaders platform, Women in Mining Africa (WiM Africa), in collaboration with Women in Management, Business and Public Service South Africa (WiMBIZSA), participated in the Africa Energy Indaba exhibition. WiM Africa extended an invitation to WiMBIZSA to share the exhibition space, creating an opportunity for both organisations to jointly engage with stakeholders and present their work in advancing women’s participation in sustainable resource sectors across the continent.

The three-day exhibition provided a platform to showcase initiatives related to mining, ESG, logistics, agribusiness, and sustainable community development. Through the shared stand, both organisations highlighted the growing role of women in shaping responsible resource management and sustainable economic participation, while also demonstrating the value of partnerships that strengthen women’s leadership across resource-driven value chains in Africa.

Throughout the exhibition, representatives engaged with industry stakeholders, ESG professionals, policymakers, entrepreneurs, and emerging graduates interested in opportunities within the mining, energy, and sustainability sectors. These engagements created opportunities to exchange ideas, discuss industry challenges, and explore ways to expand women’s participation in sectors critical to Africa’s economic growth and environmental sustainability.

The collaboration between WiMBIZSA and WiM Africa proved complementary and impactful. WiM Africa brought a strong continental footprint across more than 36 African countries, advocating for women’s inclusion in mining, while WiMBIZSA highlighted its focus on advancing women’s economic participation in sustainable mineral extraction, logistics value chains, agribusiness, and community development.

The joint presence enabled both organisations to communicate a broader message: that women-led initiatives are playing a vital role in responsible resource development while contributing to sustainable local economies. The experience also underscored the practical value of the G100 platform in connecting organisations with aligned missions and enabling collaboration in visible sector forums.

A recurring theme during discussions with visitors, particularly students and young professionals, was the need for clearer pathways into ESG and sustainability-related careers within the mining and energy sectors. Overall, participation in the Africa Energy Indaba strengthened partnerships and reinforced the importance of women’s leadership in building sustainable, responsible, and inclusive resource sectors across Africa.

Convenors:

Khosi Sibisi, G100 Global Chair, Sustainable Mining ESG Wing

Dr. Comfort Asokoro-Agaji, G100 Nigeria Country Chair, Sustainable Mining ESG Wing

Lucie Bourthoumieux Gacha

Lucie Bourthoumieux Gacha

Lucie Bourthoumieux–Gacha is a corporate lawyer and strategic advisor to Heads of States with extensive expertise in international law, infrastructure financing, and economic development initiatives.

Earlier in her career, she provided advisory services on the financing and structuring of major infrastructure projects. In this role, she contributed to the structuring and financing of large-scale construction initiatives, including a bridge project designed to enhance regional connectivity and economic welfare. She also participated in drafting master plans and financial strategies for infrastructure development.

Her professional experience further includes serving as a Senior Legal Counselor to governments on international criminal and business law, as well as regulatory compliance matters.

She also played a key role in engineering the structure for an Information and Communication Technology Free Trade Zone. This work included drafting the legislation establishing the zone and coordinating international financing mechanisms. Her efforts contributed to securing foreign financial partnerships, notably with the Export-Import Bank of India.

A strategist by conviction, she strongly believes that fair economic cooperation can help prevent and resolve conflicts, including complex border and maritime disputes. She actively promoted this perspective during two years as a speaker at Oil & Gas conferences organized by the United Nations. During these engagements, she advocated for the implementation of Joint Development Zones (JDZ) between states as instruments of economic collaboration and peacebuilding. In recognition of her expertise, she has had the privilege of advising several Heads of State on maritime conflict resolution strategies.

Lucie Bourthoumieux was admitted to the Paris Bar in 1999. She earned postgraduate Master’s degrees (DEA) in Obligations and Private Law from University Paris XII, where her thesis focused on the history of European financial markets. She previously completed a Master of Law in Corporate and Business Law from the same university. In addition, she studied Economics and Finance at Sciences Po Paris and pursued studies in Arts at the École du Louvre in Paris.

Beyond her legal and strategic work, Lucie is a passionate golfer. She has leveraged the values of the game of golf to promote investment and improve business environments by organizing and financing professional golf competitions worldwide, notably in Dubai and Equatorial Guinea. She is also a grateful mother of three children.

Beyond Gender: Rethinking Economic Models With Care at the Core. 

G100 Care Economy & Women Empowerment Conference, Mexico 25 March 2026

On March 25, the Financial Empowerment and Inclusion Policies Wing in Mexico brought forward three defining certainties at the Senate of the Republic. These statements were clear, grounded, and urgent calls to action—as binding commitments to reshape growth, equity, and responsibility. 
 
The forum was about reframing the conversation —moving from acknowledgment to accountability, from awareness to action. Above all, it was a call to recognise that the future of Mexico’s economy cannot be built without fully recognising, valuing, and investing in the systems of care that sustain it every day. The conference provided moments of clarity and momentum of collective action on the future of an economic model that includes the subject of care at its core, and addresses the invisible and unrecognised costs of growth. 
 
First recognition involves seeing the care economy as infrastructure. Care work serves as the invisible yet indispensable foundation upon which all productive activity is built. Every business, every institution, and every economic system depends on it—whether acknowledged or not. Therefore, without care work, there is no workforce; without a workforce, there is no productivity; and without productivity, there is no economy. Recognising this means elevating the care economy to its rightful place as socio-economic infrastructure, ensuring it is valued, measured, and funded with the same budgetary seriousness as roads, energy, and telecommunications.

excerpt: Beyond Gender: Rethinking Economic Models With Care at the Core. … Read more
content_html:
Beyond Gender: Rethinking Economic Models With Care at the Core. 

G100 Care Economy & Women Empowerment Conference, Mexico 25 March 2026

 On March 25, the Financial Empowerment and Inclusion Policies Wing in Mexico brought forward three defining certainties at the Senate of the Republic. These statements were clear, grounded, and urgent calls to action—as binding commitments to reshape growth, equity, and responsibility. 
 
The forum was about reframing the conversation —moving from acknowledgment to accountability, from awareness to action. Above all, it was a call to recognise that the future of Mexico’s economy cannot be built without fully recognising, valuing, and investing in the systems of care that sustain it every day. The conference provided moments of clarity and momentum of collective action on the future of an economic model that includes the subject of care at its core, and addresses the invisible and unrecognised costs of growth. 
 
First recognition involves seeing the care economy as infrastructure. Care work serves as the invisible yet indispensable foundation upon which all productive activity is built. Every business, every institution, and every economic system depends on it—whether acknowledged or not. Therefore, without care work, there is no workforce; without a workforce, there is no productivity; and without productivity, there is no economy. Recognising this means elevating the care economy to its rightful place as socio-economic infrastructure, ensuring it is valued, measured, and funded with the same budgetary seriousness as roads, energy, and telecommunications.
 
Second recognition involves seeing our shared responsibility as necessary, not optional; as a fundamental condition for sustainable and inclusive development. The burden of care work cannot rest on one person or one gender; that too without pay, recognition, or social protection. Such imbalance not only limits individual potential but also weakens economic resilience. Likewise, no market that ignores this structural reality can call itself efficient, because it is built on an incomplete and inequitable foundation. True progress for all requires a cultural and systemic shift—one where care is recognised as a shared societal responsibility, supported robustly by policies, institutions, and collective will.
 
Third recognition involves seeing this change of outlook as urgent: for postponement is no longer sustainable. The world is changing rapidly—demographics are shifting, family structures are evolving, and economies are being reshaped by new realities. The pressures on care systems are growing, and the cost of inaction is becoming increasingly visible. The time is now. 
 
Mexico stands at a pivotal crossroads, with a rare opportunity to lead with vision, courage, and foresight. It can choose to be at the forefront of this transformation, setting a brave example for others. 
 
Convenor:
Dr. Gwendolyne Negrete
G100 Mexico Country Chair, Financial Empowerment & Inclusive Policies Wing

content_html:
G100 Country Clubs 

 

G100 Country Clubs refer to the totality of all the Country Clubs across the 100 wings present in a given country, 

Each Country Club is led by the Country Chair for a wing, in a country.  

Each Country Club comprises 100 or more members, who have been nominated in any of these ways: directly by the country chair; through distributed leadership of its State/Region and City/District chairs; with the support of the Denim Club Country Partner and the Country Advisory Council members — in the overall direction of the Country Chair, who works in solidarity with the Global Chair for the wing. 

Thus, at optimal capacity, every G100 wing, guided by its Global Chair, is supported by the respective wing’s 100 Country Clubs across 100 countries, each led by its Country Chair therein. 

So vertically, there are 100 countries under one wing. And horizontally, there are 100 wings in one country through the 100 Global Chairs. These are woven into the warp and weft of the Country Clubs. 

The blueprint is to have 10,000 Country Clubs (100 Clubs per wing x 100 wings).

Country Clubs are informal and voluntary groups, connecting wing leaders and members across the 100 wings in a particular country.

Country Clubs do not have any formal presence or any alternate leadership structure other than what exists wing-wise  — they are freely formed in spontaneous spirit for building synergies across wings. 

The Secretariat regularly connects the various wings’ country chairs in respective countries as well as the resident Global Chair in that country. 

To join a Country Club, one is required to apply to the wing’s leadership; sharing your profile and how you’d like to support. 

To join a wing in your country, please Contact the Secretariat.
