excerpt: G100 Next Steps for Chairs: Mandate, Mode & More: Each… Read more
content_html:
G100 Next Steps for Chairs: Mandate, Mode & More:

Each G100 Chair is tasked with forming a group of 100 women within their respective wing. G100 is structured with 100 wings, each led globally by a Global Chair.

Distributed Leadership

Global Chair nominates 100 Country Chairs across 100 countries (one per country).

Country Chair nominates 100 members in their respective country, either directly on the country advisory council or through distributed leadership. A Country Chair can also invite State Chairs, and State Chairs can invite City Chairs, to achieve the goal of 100 members or more.

Distributed leadership is recommended as it promotes further layers of leadership across the country, building energy and engagement at all community levels, which fuels the collective mission with actions at both local and global levels. However, if a Chair has an alternative approach to achieve the group of 100, it is welcome,provided a robust roadmap accompanies it. From Group of 100 to Mission Million 
  • One Global Chair nominates 100 Country Chairs.
  • Each Country Chair nominates 100 leaders in their country club

At optimal capacity, each wing will have at least:

  • 100 Country Chairs * 100 Members = 10,000 members.
  • Across 100 wings, 10,000 * 100 leads to our Mission Million.

A million women, engaged and empowered, cannot be ignored. This is our tipping point for transformation and change.

Wing Roadmap

Each wing’s vision is provided by the secretariat, with a roadmap created by the Chairs at all levels, addressing both quantitative and qualitative goals.

  • Quantitative: Build at least 100 women leaders
  • Qualitative: Establishing guidelines for each group on:
  • Community & Social Media Outreach
  • Branding & Communication
  • Wing Summit, Events, and Engagements
  • Strategy & Policy
  • Impact & Influence
  • Delegations & Travel
  • High-Level Meetings
  • Public Meet & Greet
  • Reports & Recommendations
  • Documenting Best Practices
  • Cultivating Inter-Wing Synergies
  • Timelines & Milestones
  • Annual Calendar and Roster of Responsibilities, among others.
ABC of All Chair Roles
  • A — Act To create awareness of your wing, its members, voices, values, causes, and campaigns.
  • B — Build To expand the network and community by initiating and amplifying endeavours that weave us all together in shared purpose.
  • C — Connect To engage with thought leaders, change makers, and dream catchers — so we can act and build better, together.
Next Steps for All Chairs

The following guidelines help all chairs get started. Together we build; together we benefit.

Next Steps for Global Chairs
  1. Nominate a Denim Club Partner Each G100 Global Chair is supported by a Denim Club Global Partner, a male ally and He for She Champion. The role of the Denim Club Partner is to support the Chair in her mandate.
  2. Invite Global Advisory Council Members Members can be both women and men, with all men joining as Denim Club members.
  3. Nominate Country Chairs
  4. Welcome Members on Social Media The Secretariat will send the banner and update the website. Once formalized, all members are encouraged to share the banners themselves to maximize outreach through distributed leadership.
  5. Share Wing Roadmap Encourage all members to contribute and co-create in the spirit of shared leadership and collective resourcefulness.
Next Steps for Country Chairs
  1. Nominate a Denim Club Partner : Each G100 Country Chair is supported by a Denim Club Country Partner who serves as a male ally and He-for-She Champion. The Denim Club Partner’s role is to assist the Chair in fulfilling her mandate.
  2. Invite Country Advisory Members : Advisory Council members can be both women and men. All male members join the Denim Club.
  3. Nominate State/Region Chairs : Appoint chairs at the state or regional levels to expand reach and leadership across your country.
  4. Social Media Welcome : The Secretariat will provide the banner and add new members to the website. Once formalized, all members can share the banners as well. Together, we maximize outreach through distributed leadership.
  5. Share Wing Roadmap : Encourage all members to contribute and co-create the roadmap in the spirit of shared leadership and collective resourcefulness.
Next Steps for State/Region Chairs
  1. Nominate a Denim Club Partner : Each G100 State/Region Chair is supported by a Denim Club State/Region Partner, who serves as a male ally and “He for She” Champion. The role of the Denim Club Partner is to assist the Chair in fulfilling her mandate.
  2. Invite and Nominate State/Region Advisory Council Members : These members can include both women and men, with all male members joining the Denim Club.
  3. Nominate City/District Chairs Across Your State/Region :
  4. Welcome Advisory Members and Chairs on Social Media : The Secretariat will provide a banner and update the website. Once formalized, members are encouraged to share their banners as well, amplifying outreach through distributed leadership.
  5. Share the Wing Roadmap with Members : Encourage all members to contribute and co-create in the spirit of shared leadership and collective resourcefulness.
Next Steps for City/District Chairs
  1. Nominate One Denim Club Partner : Each G100 City/District Chair is supported by one Denim Club City/District Partner who is a male ally and He for She Champion. The role of the Denim Club Partner is to support the Chair in her mandate.
  2. Invite and Nominate City/District Advisory Council Members : These can include both women and men. All male members will be part of the Denim Club.
  3. Nominate Wing Members Across Your City/District.
  4. Welcome Your Advisory Members and Chairs on Social Media : The Secretariat will provide a banner and add details to the website. Once formalized, all members are encouraged to share banners themselves. Together, we maximize outreach through distributed leadership.
  5. Share the Wing Roadmap with Members : Encourage all to contribute and co-create with a spirit of shared leadership and collective resourcefulness.
GUIDELINES FOR BANNERS Roles

The banners are made for our website and can be used on your social media. Kindly fill in the following details for the secretariat to process your banner:

  • Name:
  • Individual Designation:
  • Country:

Role in G100: We shall add the given role in G100 at the respective wing based on the invite issued. Photograph: Kindly ensure that banner photos are high-resolution and well-lit, with the face clearly visible. Please avoid heavy filters or coverings. Refer to passport photo standards for clarity and posture.

Important Notes
  • Getting Started : Begin with 5-10 nominations, building to 100 or more.
  • Procedure : Send the secretariat your nominations’ names, emails, and LinkedIn profiles. They will handle further steps, including invitations and social media banners. Inform your nominees inadvance.
  • Recommendations : Chairs can develop actions and policy suggestions aligned with 100 ELLEGOSSSE recommendations.
  • Tenures: All chairs serve a 2-year renewable tenure. Past chairs can reapply or join the advisory role.
  • Termination : Tenure may end due to dormancy or code violations. Resignations are accepted at alltimes, and internal resolutions are encouraged for interpersonal issues.
  • Coordination : Secretariat manages formalizations, reviews, nominations, terminations, and wing mergers/closures.
  • Website & Socials : Banners for all wings and chairs are updated on www.G100.in. Wings can create social media pages and/or websites for wings. Following distributed leadership, all chairs welcome on socials the next level of leadership they lead: Secretariat welcomes Global Chairs – Global Chairs welcome Country Chairs – Country Chairs welcome State Chairs – State Chairs welcome City Chairs, and so on. The G100 main page further shares the wing posts to maximise overall outreach.
  • Global Meetings : Chairs may host global meetings, following secretariat guidelines for global visibility.
  • Global President : Elected by rotation from Global Chairs, serving a one-year term, focusing onstrategic actions for global influence.
  • Founder : Supports the secretariat, especially advising Global Chairs, Global President, and the Advisory Council.
  • Secretariat : Led by the Director General, responsible for coordination.
  • Spirit: G100 fosters sisterhood and solidarity with a focus on inspiration over hierarchy. Movement between roles is flexible and based on commitment and interest.
  • Code of Conduct : G100 is non-political, non-religious, and non-dogmatic, dedicated to a vision of unity and global peace.
  • Prohibited Activities : No legal registrations, bank accounts, or fundraising in the name of G100 are allowed.
 
Partnerships

To support local events and initiatives, partner with established local organizations to serve as event collaborators, ensuring compliance and focusing on G100’s core mandate.

Core Mandate

Our mission is to be a powerful collective of women leaders advancing actions to close the gender gap, reduce barriers, and create ecosystems where women thrive.

Shaping Rural Women’s Future in Agriculture: G100–FAO Dialogue

G100 Burkina Faso Meetings, 7 April 2026 

A high-level meeting was convened at the FAO Office in Ouagadougou between representatives of the G100 Agriculture Wing and the FAO Country Office in Burkina Faso. This important engagement marked a significant milestone in strengthening dialogue and exploring strategic collaboration aimed at advancing agricultural development and women’s empowerment across the country.
 
The session commenced with welcoming remarks from the FAO Country Representative, who expressed sincere appreciation for the visit and acknowledged the importance of building partnerships with global initiatives such as G100. The G100 delegation, led by its Global Chair, introduced its members and conveyed their gratitude for the opportunity to engage in constructive and forward-looking discussions. The exchange established a positive and collaborative tone for the meeting.
 
During the discussions, G100 presented its vision, mission, and strategic priorities in Burkina Faso, placing a strong emphasis on empowering rural women and strengthening their role within the agricultural value chain. The presentation highlighted G100’s commitment to inclusive growth, capacity-building initiatives, and the development of impactful partnerships. It also underscored the importance of creating sustainable opportunities that enable women to thrive as leaders and contributors within their communities.
 
In response, the FAO acknowledged the relevance and significance of G100’s initiative and recognized its strong alignment with national and global development priorities. The organization expressed interest in supporting G100’s efforts, while also outlining key recommendations to ensure a strong foundation for collaboration. These included obtaining official legal recognition as a prerequisite for institutional partnership, accelerating administrative procedures to enhance credibility and operational presence, and engaging with national authorities. FAO further encouraged G100 to pursue long-term representation in decision-making bodies, including at the parliamentary level, to effectively advocate for rural women.
 
The FAO reaffirmed its openness to future collaboration, while emphasizing that such engagement would be contingent upon the formalization of G100’s legal and institutional status. This highlights the importance of strong governance and alignment with national frameworks in building sustainable partnerships.
 
In conclusion, the meeting was constructive and forward-looking, providing clarity on the strategic priorities and requirements necessary to establish a meaningful and lasting partnership. It also reinforced the importance of institutional structuring and formal recognition in enhancing G100’s credibility, impact, and long-term presence in Burkina Faso.

title: CSW 70 New York, USA Meetings, 9-13 March 2026
excerpt: A New Era in Global Finance: G100 Unveils Plans for… Read more
content_html:
A New Era in Global Finance: G100 Unveils Plans for a Global Women’s Bank at CSW70

G100 CSW 70 New York, USA Meetings, 9-13 March 2026 

The G100 Global President Journey 2026, led by Datin Dr. (h.c.) Hartini Osman, was successfully undertaken during the 70th Session of the United Nations Commission on the Status of Women (CSW70) in New York, United States of America. This landmark mission represents a defining step forward in advancing women’s leadership, economic empowerment, and global collaboration, highlighted by the official launch of the Global Women’s Bank (GWB) platform.
 
Held from 9 March to 13 March 2026, the mission brought together a dynamic series of high-level dialogues, forums, diplomatic engagements, institutional meetings, and international networking sessions. Designed with a clear strategic vision, the initiative focused on launching the Global Women’s Bank platform, strengthening global partnerships, promoting women’s financial inclusion, advocating for women’s leadership in global governance, and establishing impactful collaboration frameworks across public and private sectors.
 
Under the compelling theme, “Global Women’s Bank: Redesigning Finance for Dignity, Peace & Women’s Leadership,” the mission was hosted across some of New York’s most prestigious institutions, including the United Nations Headquarters, City College of New York (CCNY), Columbia University, PwC Headquarters, Hogan Lovells, the United Nations Church Center, and the Consulate General of Malaysia. The initiative was driven by the G100 Global Network, the Global Women’s Bank Initiative, the Women Economic Forum (WEF), and key strategic partners.
 
At its core, the mission was designed to introduce the Global Women’s Bank as a transformative global platform aimed at expanding women’s access to capital, leadership opportunities, and economic participation. It also reinforced the importance of elevating women’s roles across governance, finance, diplomacy, and entrepreneurship, while fostering meaningful partnerships among governments, corporations, academia, and civil society. A strong emphasis was placed on encouraging systemic reforms to build inclusive and equitable financial ecosystems.
 
The programme commenced on 9 March 2026 with the UN CSW70 Side Event, “No Peace Without Women,” held at the United Nations Headquarters. The session underscored the indispensable role of women in peace-building, diplomacy, and governance, reinforcing that sustainable peace is unattainable without women’s active participation and leadership.
 
On 10 March 2026, the United Nations Church Center Dialogue provided an important platform to present the vision and framework of the Global Women’s Bank, focusing on women’s entrepreneurship development, sustainable economic growth, and pathways to financial access and leadership. Complementing this, the G100 Strategic Breakfast Dialogue at PwC Headquarters convened global corporate leaders and decision-makers to explore actionable strategies for financial inclusion, including advancing economic autonomy, improving access to capital, strengthening corporate leadership participation, and building resilient global investment ecosystems.
 
The momentum continued on 11 March 2026 at Columbia University, where the Women Economic Forum (WEF) welcomed over 100 international participants from across Latin America and North America. The forum featured opening remarks by Datin Dr. (h.c.) Hartini Osman and served as a dynamic platform for cross-sector collaboration, advancing discussions on leadership, innovation, and economic empowerment.
 
Later that evening, the WEF Gala & Awards Night at Hogan Lovells celebrated excellence in global women’s leadership. In recognition of her outstanding contributions to advancing women’s empowerment and fostering global collaboration, Datin Dr. (h.c.) Hartini Osman was honored with the prestigious Legendary Woman Award.
 
On 13 March 2026, a key diplomatic engagement at the Consulate General of Malaysia in New York further strengthened bilateral relations and provided an opportunity to present the Global Women’s Bank vision to international stakeholders. The engagement highlighted the importance of cultural diplomacy, strategic collaboration, and institutional networking in advancing global initiatives.
 
The mission culminated with the Global Women’s Bank High-Level Dialogue & Platform Launch at the City College of New York (CCNY), with the support of H.E. Carmen Velasquez, Global Chair, and H.E. Epsy Campbell, where these ideas were previously discussed at the WEF ASEAN 2025 forum. This flagship event marked the official unveiling of the platform and featured in-depth discussions on governance structures, financial inclusion strategies, institutional partnerships, and the formation of a Global Steering Committee. The event brought together an esteemed group of international diplomats, policymakers, corporate leaders, academics, and global women leaders.
 
Across all engagements, the mission reinforced four core principles: Finance with Dignity, emphasizing fairness and equity in financial systems; Capital with Conscience, advocating for ethical and responsible investment frameworks; Growth with Equity, ensuring inclusive economic development; and Leadership with Peace, recognizing the critical role of women in fostering global stability.
 
The mission delivered significant strategic outcomes, including the successful launch of the Global Women’s Bank as a global platform dedicated to financial inclusion, leadership development, and institutional transformation. It also led to the establishment of strong partnerships across international organizations, corporate institutions, academic bodies, policy leaders, and civil society. The formation of a Global Steering Committee marks the next phase of development, focusing on governance, implementation, and long-term impact. Additionally, the mission significantly strengthened global leadership networks across North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, and the Middle East.
 
Engaging a diverse and influential group of stakeholders—including policymakers, diplomats, corporate executives, academics, civil society leaders, entrepreneurs, and development partners—the mission fostered meaningful global dialogue and collaboration. Participation from multiple countries further amplified its impact and global reach.
 
The CSW70 New York Mission has substantially elevated the visibility and credibility of the Global Women’s Bank initiative. It has strengthened diplomatic and corporate relationships, enhanced global awareness of women-centric financial systems, recognized leadership excellence, and expanded international collaboration networks, reinforcing the global positioning of the G100 platform.
 
This milestone achievement was made possible through the collective efforts and support of the G100 Global Network, the Women Economic Forum (WEF), strategic corporate partners, academic institutions, diplomatic missions, international delegates, and dedicated teams and volunteers. Their commitment and collaboration were instrumental in the success of this global mission.
 
The G100 CSW70 New York Mission 2026 stands as a landmark achievement in shaping the future of women’s leadership and global financial transformation. The launch of the Global Women’s Bank platform signals the beginning of a new era—one where women are at the forefront of shaping financial systems, governance structures, and economic policies worldwide. With a strong foundation now in place, the mission paves the way for sustained global collaboration, institutional growth, and inclusive economic empowerment. Together, we move forward toward a future where women lead, economies thrive, and societies prosper. 
 
Convenors:
Datin Dr. (H.C) Hartini Binti Osman, G100 Global Chair, Philanthropy, Business & Poverty Eradication Wing, and Global President 2026
Patricia Elias, G100 Global Chair, Government & Ministerial Advocacy Wing
Patricia Gonzalez, G100 Global Chair, Human Resources & Talent Development Wing

Mette (Mellie) Laursen

Mette (Mellie) Laursen

Mette (Mellie) Laursen is a globally recognized entrepreneur and board chair professional with extensive experience across executive management, startups, public institutions, and global corporations. She is the Founder and CEO of LinKS, established in 1998. Under her leadership, LinKS has become a pioneering platform for leadership, governance, and innovation education in her nation, engaging ministers, policymakers, and senior executives across both public and private sectors. Through decades of work, she has advanced cross-sector collaboration, emphasizing co-creation to address complex societal challenges.Her work bridges politics, science, business, and society, fostering collaborative models that drive systemic impact. Her current strategic focus is on strengthening European alliances with a global ambition. 

Through The Chairs’ Agenda, she leads an international outreach initiative for selected chairpersons endorsed by their nations, aimed at building leadership that support a resilient and future-ready world. The initiative is endorsed by the Speaker of Parliament, the Ombudsman of Denmark, global ambassadors to Denmark from more than 20 nations, and leading voices in leadership.LinKS has educated top leadership of Denmark as nation  across sectors designed and led in partnership for decades with the leading global business schools; The Wharton School and INSEAD. Her advisory work includes strategic analysis and leadership consulting for major organizations such as Ørsted, Grundfos, Volkswagen, the Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Environment, and judicial leadership bodies.Mellie and LinKS were awarded a prestigious scientific grant by the Novo Nordisk Foundation to build alliances within the European Union in quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and life sciences—further strengthening her role in advancing innovation ecosystems.

From 2017 to 2022, she served as a Global Ambassador, focusing on building international partnerships centered on livability and sustainability in the world’s megacities. This work was mandated by BLOX – Architecture and Design in Denmark and Realdania, where she contributed to strengthening the global positioning of Denmark. In this role as global ambassador, she worked closely with ambassadors to Denmark and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.Earlier in her career, she served as Practice Leader at Ernst & Young (1995–1999), specializing in strategy and process management for global corporates and public sector organizations. She began her professional journey at the Ministry of Finance in Denmark (1992–1995), where she contributed to financial legislation and welfare program frameworks, focusing on managerial and administrative policy tools.She holds a Master of Science in Economics (Cand. Polit) from the University of Copenhagen and a Master of Science in Economics and Mathematical Econometrics from the University of London.

 She is also a Certified Executive Coach at international level. Her early studies included performing arts, supported by a Rotary International Scholarship in Atlanta, Georgia.She is deeply committed to fostering global dialogue and international alliances, organizing high-level diplomatic and leadership platforms that strengthen cultural exchange and global cooperation. She hosts and leads Denmark’s most influential networks of senior women leaders through LinKS, championing gender equity and leadership development.Her initiatives include The Chairs’ Agenda (2025), Global Women’s Day (2021) for female ambassadors at BLOX, International Women’s Day events (2019 and 2020) at the Karen Blixen Museum in Rungstedlund, and the Global Women’s Forum (2016), where she led the Scandinavian delegation under the patronage of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, UAE.She has been decorated as Chevalier de l’Ordre de la Couronne of Belgium and serves on the board of a Royal Foundation in Denmark. She also holds extensive experience in chairing board positions across multiple sectors.Born in Denmark, she embodies a truly global mindset. She is married to Hugo Sato, has children, and resides between Copenhagen, Brussels, and Paris.

The G100 UK Higher Education & Industry Connect Wing, under the leadership of Country Chair Dr. Doirean Wilson BEM, proudly hosted the prestigious “Tell Me Your Story” event in collaboration with the University of East London (UEL), the Royal Docks School of Business & Law, and the Noon Centre.

Organised with the support of Dr. Colin Burton FRSA, Advisory Wing Member of the Denim Club, the event brought together an inspiring community of G100 members, distinguished guests, students, academics, professionals, and thought leaders to celebrate leadership, resilience, and the transformative power of storytelling as a catalyst for personal and societal change.

Held at UEL’s Stratford Campus, the event provided a dynamic and engaging platform for meaningful dialogue, authentic storytelling, and impactful networking. The gathering created opportunities for participants from diverse backgrounds to connect, exchange ideas, and explore the role of lived experiences in shaping leadership, inspiring innovation, and building stronger communities.

The event reflected G100’s ongoing commitment to fostering collaboration between higher education, industry, and community leadership while creating spaces where voices from across generations and sectors can be heard, valued, and amplified. Through the sharing of personal narratives and professional experiences, participants were encouraged to reflect on their own journeys and the power of storytelling in driving understanding, empathy, and positive action.

Attendees engaged in inspiring conversations that highlighted personal growth, leadership journeys, and the importance of empowering communities through shared experiences and collaboration. The discussions reinforced the value of authenticity in leadership and demonstrated how stories can serve as powerful tools for motivation, mentorship, and social impact.

G100 Indigenous Communities & Integration Wing – Indonesia Launch, 29 April 2026.

 
The G100 Indigenous Communities & Integration Wing marked a significant and memorable milestone with the official launch of its Indonesian Wing in Bali, a destination that perfectly reflects the spirit, heritage, and cultural richness at the heart of this initiative. The choice of Bali as the host location added a profound sense of authenticity and alignment with the Wing’s vision of honoring, preserving, and celebrating indigenous traditions and wisdom.

Silvia Hernández Tejero

Silvia Hernández Tejero

Silvia Hernández Tejero is a distinguished global executive with extensive leadership experience in digital and AI transformation, cloud strategy, customer experience, commercial banking, and business innovation across Europe, Latin America, and the United States. She is a globally recognized leader, who has built an outstanding career at the intersection of business transformation, technology and Leadership.

Since September 2022, she has served as Board Member at Microsoft Spain and she is now Enterprise Commercial Head for Global & Strategic Customers, leading Microsoft’s engagement and initiatives globally with some of Spain’s largest enterprises across banking, insurance, retail, energy, and telecommunications sectors. In this role, she works closely with CEOs, COOs, and C-level executives to accelerate AI transformation, cloud adoption, cybersecurity, digital modernization, automation, and innovation through Microsoft’s global ecosystem and advanced technologies.

Prior to Microsoft, Silvia served as Managing Director & Partner at Accenture, where mainly she led Cloud First in Mexico. Her leadership drove large-scale cloud migration, digital transformation, and modernization programs across industries including financial services, retail, consumer products, and resources.

Earlier, she built an international career within Santander Group and Banesto, leading global multichannel transformation across major markets including Brazil, Mexico, Argentina, Chile, Spain, Portugal, the United Kingdom, Germany, Poland, and the United States. At Banesto she led Innovation and Customer Experience Area reporting directly to the CEO, and also Commercial System and Transformation for Retail Banking. 

Throughout her career, Silvia has consistently delivered measurable business growth, strengthened customer engagement, accelerated digital transformation, and led large-scale organizational modernization programs. Her leadership has contributed to internationally recognized quality, innovation, and transformation achievements.

Silvia Hernández Tejero has received numerous prestigious recognitions, including being honored as an “Exceptional Woman of Excellence in Business” by the Women Economic Forum (WEF) Iberoamerica and being named among the “100 Successful Leaders in Spain” by Dirigentes Magazine.

Academically, she completed the General Management Programme (PDG) at IESE Business School and the Leading Change and Organizational Renewal Program at Harvard Business School and Cloud Transformation Program at MIT. She holds a Bachelor’s degree in Economic Science & Business from the University of Valladolid, along with master’s degrees in Quality Management and Marketing.

Women Leading the Future of Inclusive & Resilient Cities at WUF13

G100 Baku Azerbaijan – WUF Meetings, 20 May 2026

 

The G100 Smart & Sustainable Cities Wing successfully convened its distinguished networking event, “Housing in an Interconnected World: Women Leading Inclusive & Resilient Urban Futures,” during the World Urban Forum 13 (WUF13) held in Baku, Azerbaijan, on 20 May 2026. The session brought together an inspiring gathering of global leaders, urban experts, policymakers, academics, innovators, and changemakers to engage in meaningful dialogue on the transformative role of women in shaping inclusive, resilient, and sustainable urban environments for future generations.

Held within the framework of WUF13, the event served as an important international platform for discussions surrounding housing, urban development, climate resilience, sustainable infrastructure, and community empowerment. Participants from diverse sectors and regions exchanged experiences, perspectives, and best practices while highlighting innovative and practical approaches to building cities that are equitable, adaptive, and future-ready. The session reinforced the importance of collaboration and shared responsibility in addressing the rapidly evolving challenges facing urban communities across the world.

The discussion strongly emphasized the importance of placing women at the center of urban planning, governance, and decision-making processes. Speakers highlighted that inclusive leadership is essential for addressing complex urban challenges and ensuring that the voices and needs of all communities, particularly vulnerable and underrepresented groups, are reflected in both policy and practice. The conversation further explored how women’s leadership contributes significantly to creating more connected, compassionate, and sustainable urban systems.

A key takeaway from the session was the understanding that resilience extends far beyond physical infrastructure and technological advancement. Participants noted that strong communities, social inclusion, equal access to opportunities, education, and collaborative governance are equally critical in building cities that can adapt, respond, and thrive in the face of social, economic, environmental, and climate-related challenges. The dialogue underscored that truly resilient cities are those that prioritize people-centered development and foster a strong sense of belonging and participation among citizens.

The event also highlighted the urgent need for integrated and forward-looking urban solutions that incorporate climate resilience, sustainability, digital innovation, and inclusive economic growth. Participants stressed the importance of cross-sector and cross-regional partnerships in accelerating progress toward more sustainable and inclusive urban futures. The exchange of ideas demonstrated the value of international cooperation and collective action in advancing urban transformation on a global scale.

Throughout the session, participants reaffirmed the importance of empowering women as leaders, innovators, and decision-makers in shaping the cities of tomorrow. The discussions reflected a shared vision of creating urban environments that are not only smart and sustainable but also equitable, accessible, and resilient for all members of society.

The event concluded with a collective commitment to advancing the vision of smart and sustainable cities through continued collaboration, knowledge exchange, strategic partnerships, and women’s leadership. The valuable insights and perspectives generated during the session will help inform future initiatives, strengthen international cooperation, and contribute to global efforts aimed at building resilient, inclusive, and sustainable urban communities worldwide.

Convenor:

Zeynep Bodur Okyay, G100 Global Chair, Smart & Sustainable Cities Wing

Empowering Through Stories: G100 “Tell Me Your Story”

G100 UK Club Meetings, London, 11 June 2026 

The G100 UK Higher Education & Industry Connect Wing, under the leadership of Country Chair Dr. Doirean Wilson BEM, proudly hosted the prestigious “Tell Me Your Story” event in collaboration with the University of East London (UEL), the Royal Docks School of Business & Law, and the Noon Centre.

Organised with the support of Dr. Colin Burton FRSA, Advisory Wing Member of the Denim Club, the event brought together an inspiring community of G100 members, distinguished guests, students, academics, professionals, and thought leaders to celebrate leadership, resilience, and the transformative power of storytelling as a catalyst for personal and societal change.

Held at UEL’s Stratford Campus, the event provided a dynamic and engaging platform for meaningful dialogue, authentic storytelling, and impactful networking. The gathering created opportunities for participants from diverse backgrounds to connect, exchange ideas, and explore the role of lived experiences in shaping leadership, inspiring innovation, and building stronger communities.

The event reflected G100’s ongoing commitment to fostering collaboration between higher education, industry, and community leadership while creating spaces where voices from across generations and sectors can be heard, valued, and amplified. Through the sharing of personal narratives and professional experiences, participants were encouraged to reflect on their own journeys and the power of storytelling in driving understanding, empathy, and positive action.

Attendees engaged in inspiring conversations that highlighted personal growth, leadership journeys, and the importance of empowering communities through shared experiences and collaboration. The discussions reinforced the value of authenticity in leadership and demonstrated how stories can serve as powerful tools for motivation, mentorship, and social impact.

The programme featured an outstanding panel of distinguished speakers, including internationally acclaimed singer, actress, and artist Dr. Patti Boulaye OBE, G100 Wing Advisory Member; Dwain Chambers, one of Britain’s most decorated track sprinters and G100 Denim Club Member; Sudha Srivastava FRSA, G100 Club England SDGs Region Chair; Detective Susan Wilkinson of the Metropolitan Police Service; and Ify Anyaegbu, Founder and Executive Director of FACEYOUTH and a leading advocate for Women in STEM and Diversity.

Each speaker brought a unique perspective and a deeply personal narrative, sharing the challenges, setbacks, and defining moments that shaped their journey to success. Their stories offered valuable insights into perseverance, reinvention, leadership, and the importance of remaining committed to one’s purpose despite adversity.

Through their powerful testimonies, the speakers highlighted themes of resilience, courage, determination, and service, inspiring attendees to embrace their own leadership potential and pursue their aspirations with confidence and conviction. Their experiences resonated strongly with the audience, encouraging participants to view obstacles not as barriers but as opportunities for growth, learning, and transformation.

The interactive nature of the event fostered meaningful engagement between speakers and attendees, creating an atmosphere of openness, reflection, and mutual support. Students and emerging leaders particularly benefited from the opportunity to hear directly from accomplished professionals whose journeys illustrated that success is often shaped by persistence, adaptability, and a willingness to learn from challenges.

Beyond celebrating individual achievements, the event reinforced the importance of community, mentorship, and collaboration in creating inclusive and sustainable pathways for future leaders. It also highlighted the critical role that educational institutions and industry partnerships play in nurturing talent, fostering innovation, and preparing the next generation to address complex global challenges.

The “Tell Me Your Story” event concluded with enthusiastic engagement from attendees and further strengthened the growing network of leaders, educators, students, and changemakers committed to advancing inclusive leadership and empowering communities through dialogue and shared learning experiences.

As G100 continues to champion women’s leadership and global collaboration, initiatives such as “Tell Me Your Story” serve as powerful reminders that stories have the ability to inspire action, bridge differences, and create lasting impact across communities, industries, and generations.

excerpt: Food Security as Human Security: International Leaders Call for Collective… Read more
content_html:
Food Security as Human Security: International Leaders Call for Collective Action 

G100 Global Summit on Food Sovereignty & Zero Hunger, 26 June 2026 

The First International Congress on Food Security marked the beginning of a new international dialogue within G100, bringing together women leaders, experts, and practitioners from different regions of the world to address one of humanity’s most pressing challenges: ensuring food security and strengthening food sovereignty for present and future generations.

Jointly organized by the G100 Security & Defence and the G100 Zero Hunger Mission, the Congress created a global platform for sharing knowledge, regional experiences, and innovative approaches that contribute to Sustainable Development Goal 2 – Zero Hunger. Discussions highlighted that food security extends beyond food production, encompassing human security, public health, environmental sustainability, resilient economies, and the well-being of communities.

The initiative was originally proposed by Marlene Argote, Bolivia Country Chair of the G100 Security & Defence, who envisioned creating an international forum dedicated to food security and food sovereignty as essential components of human security. The Congress was jointly led by Bodil Valero, Global Chair of Security & Defence, and Karen Brugés, Global Chair of the Zero Hunger Mission, reflecting G100’s commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration and women’s leadership in addressing global challenges.

Opening the Congress, Bodil Valero welcomed participants by introducing G100 as the global platform founded by Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, emphasizing that security must be understood not only from a territorial perspective but also through the lens of human security, where access to food is a fundamental pillar of peace, resilience, and sustainable development.

Building on this vision, Karen Brugés introduced the international framework of food security through the definition established by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), highlighting that food security exists when all people have physical, social, and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food. She emphasized that advancing Zero Hunger requires strengthening food systems that preserve nutrition, improve livelihoods, and ensure equitable access to food for present and future generations.

Throughout the Congress, international leaders demonstrated that while food insecurity manifests differently across regions, common challenges demand shared solutions. Silvia Vázquez presented Argentina’s paradox of being a leading food-producing nation while facing high levels of food insecurity, emphasizing the strategic role of family farming and agroecological transition. Marlene Argote highlighted the importance of protecting native seeds, preserving ancestral knowledge, and strengthening local production as the foundation of food sovereignty. From Africa, Silvia Llopart shared innovative community initiatives in The Gambia, including organic fertilizers, solar-powered cold storage, and women’s empowerment as practical responses to food insecurity.

Food Security as Human Security: International Leaders Call for Collective Action 

G100 Global Summit on Food Sovereignty & Zero Hunger, 26 June 2026 

The First International Congress on Food Security marked the beginning of a new international dialogue within G100, bringing together women leaders, experts, and practitioners from different regions of the world to address one of humanity’s most pressing challenges: ensuring food security and strengthening food sovereignty for present and future generations.

Jointly organized by the G100 Security & Defence and the G100 Zero Hunger Mission, the Congress created a global platform for sharing knowledge, regional experiences, and innovative approaches that contribute to Sustainable Development Goal 2 – Zero Hunger. Discussions highlighted that food security extends beyond food production, encompassing human security, public health, environmental sustainability, resilient economies, and the well-being of communities.

The initiative was originally proposed by Marlene Argote, Bolivia Country Chair of the G100 Security & Defence, who envisioned creating an international forum dedicated to food security and food sovereignty as essential components of human security. The Congress was jointly led by Bodil Valero, Global Chair of Security & Defence, and Karen Brugés, Global Chair of the Zero Hunger Mission, reflecting G100’s commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration and women’s leadership in addressing global challenges.

Opening the Congress, Bodil Valero welcomed participants by introducing G100 as the global platform founded by Dr. Harbeen Arora Rai, emphasizing that security must be understood not only from a territorial perspective but also through the lens of human security, where access to food is a fundamental pillar of peace, resilience, and sustainable development.

Building on this vision, Karen Brugés introduced the international framework of food security through the definition established by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), highlighting that food security exists when all people have physical, social, and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food. She emphasized that advancing Zero Hunger requires strengthening food systems that preserve nutrition, improve livelihoods, and ensure equitable access to food for present and future generations.

Throughout the Congress, international leaders demonstrated that while food insecurity manifests differently across regions, common challenges demand shared solutions. Silvia Vázquez presented Argentina’s paradox of being a leading food-producing nation while facing high levels of food insecurity, emphasizing the strategic role of family farming and agroecological transition. Marlene Argote highlighted the importance of protecting native seeds, preserving ancestral knowledge, and strengthening local production as the foundation of food sovereignty. From Africa, Silvia Llopart shared innovative community initiatives in The Gambia, including organic fertilizers, solar-powered cold storage, and women’s empowerment as practical responses to food insecurity.

The discussions also showcased innovative pathways for strengthening food systems. Chef Juliana Romero demonstrated how gastronomy can contribute to food security by supporting local producers, reducing food waste, and promoting community-led initiatives such as urban gardens and community kitchens. Sharon Persovski shared California’s experience in addressing urban food insecurity through public assistance programs, urban agriculture, and technological innovation. Marianela Mirpuri invited participants to reflect on the relationship between nutrition, health, and sustainability, emphasizing the impact of excessive sugar consumption and ultra-processed foods on long-term well-being.

Complementing these perspectives, Karen Brugés presented Amber Economy – Preserving Food Value, a framework that proposes recognizing food as a multidimensional asset with nutritional, economic, social, territorial, and environmental value. During her presentation, she also introduced the recently published book Economía del Impacto Alimentario: Hacia una Economía Ámbar (Food Impact Economy toward an Amber Economy), presented as a contribution to the international dialogue on food security, sustainable food systems, and food value preservation.

The Congress also provided a broader strategic perspective through Amalia Díaz Enríquez, who presented a systemic approach based on seven interconnected dimensions of food security, underscoring the need for coordinated public policies, science, investment, and international cooperation. Natalia Ocampo complemented this vision with a regional diagnosis of Latin America, highlighting the need to reduce post-harvest losses, strengthen traceability, and expand financing opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly those led by women.

The Congress concluded with a shared commitment to continue strengthening collaboration between the G100 Security & Defence and the G100 Zero Hunger Mission while expanding future editions to include additional G100 Missions, new countries, more languages, and broader international participation. Participants reaffirmed that achieving Zero Hunger requires collaboration across governments, academia, civil society, entrepreneurs, and local communities to build more resilient, inclusive, and sustainable food systems.

The organizing committee extends its sincere appreciation to all speakers for their valuable contributions to this inaugural edition and offers special recognition to Alison Lam for her dedication as Technical Lead, ensuring the successful coordination and seamless delivery of the Congress, and to María Antonieta Quijada for her valuable support in coordinating the collaboration between Security & Defence and the Zero Hunger Mission, as well as for the development of the official Congress agenda flyer.

The First International Congress on Food Security represents the beginning of a long-term international platform for dialogue, cooperation, and action. G100 invites women leaders, researchers, entrepreneurs, policymakers, academic institutions, and organizations worldwide to join this growing global network and contribute to advancing food security, food sovereignty, and innovative solutions that accelerate progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 2 – Zero Hunger.

content_html:
H.E. Justice Dr. Jane Ansah

H.E. Justice Dr. Jane Ansah

H.E. Justice Dr. Jane Mayemu Ansah, SC, JA (Rtd), Vice President of the Republic of Malawi, is a distinguished Malawian jurist, legal scholar, author, and stateswoman. She is the second female Vice President of the Republic of Malawi, having assumed office following the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) victory in the General Elections held on 16 September 2025. A Senior Counsel (SC) and retired Justice of Appeal (JA), she has devoted decades of service to advancing justice, constitutional governance, electoral integrity, and human rights in Malawi and across Africa. Born on 11 October 1955 in Lilongwe, Malawi, she is the second-born daughter of the late Mr Kenneth Macpherson Mjojo and Mrs Ferrie Mjojo. She earned her Bachelor of Laws (LLB) degree from the University of Malawi, Chancellor College, in 1978. She later obtained a Master of Laws (LLM) in International Human Rights in 1996, followed by a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in International Human Rights from the University of Nottingham, United Kingdom, in 2002. She began her judicial career as a Judge of the High Court of Malawi, serving from 1997 to 2012. In 2006, she was appointed the first female Attorney General of the Republic of Malawi, a position she held for seven years. Following her tenure as Attorney General, she returned to the judiciary and served as a Justice of Appeal of the Supreme Court of Appeal of Malawi from 2012 until her retirement from the Bench in October 2020. She was appointed Chairperson of the Malawi Electoral Commission in 2016 and served in that capacity until June 2020. During her tenure, she oversaw significant electoral processes and also served as President of the Electoral Commissions Forum of SADC (ECF-SADC), strengthening regional cooperation among electoral management bodies. She has served as Chairperson and member of numerous boards and committees in Malawi and within the African Union (AU), contributing to governance, public administration, and institutional development at both national and continental levels.In 2024, she entered active politics after retiring from the judiciary. In June 2025, she was elected as the running mate to Professor Arthur Peter Mutharika under the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP). Following the party’s victory in the General Elections held on 16 September 2025, she assumed office as the second female Vice President of the Republic of Malawi.She is an accomplished author whose scholarly work focuses primarily on human rights and legal development. She has written several books, publications, and academic papers, including her notable work, The Right to Development and the Malawian Law, which is available through Amazon.She is a committed Christian and serves as the National Overseer of Christ Citadel International Church, reflecting her dedication to faith, leadership, and community service alongside her distinguished public career.

Advancing Women’s Leadership Across ASEAN

G100 ASEAN Meetings 2026, Philippines Along with WEF – ASEAN, 18-20 June 2026

  

G100 ASEAN Meetings 2026 – Philippines, held from 18–20 June 2026 at the Grand Duchess Ballroom, Great Eastern Hotel, Quezon City, Philippines, in collaboration with the Women Economic Forum (WEF) ASEAN 2026 Philippines, brought together distinguished women leaders, government officials, diplomats, policymakers, entrepreneurs, business executives, academics, and changemakers from across ASEAN and the international community. Guided by the theme, “Women Leaders: Creating a SHEconomy Environment of Inclusive Economic Growth and Sustainable Development,” and the guiding message, “Together, WE Navigate the Future,” the meetings served as a strategic platform to strengthen regional cooperation, foster meaningful partnerships, advance women’s leadership, and promote inclusive and sustainable development across the region.

The programme commenced with the arrival of international delegates on 17 June 2026, who were welcomed at a reception hosted by the Department of Tourism, with transportation and logistical support provided by the Department of Transportation and the Philippine Coast Guard, ensuring a seamless experience for all participants.

The Official Opening Ceremony featured the Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony, Entry of Colors, an Ecumenical Prayer, the singing of the participating countries’ national anthems, the WEF ASEAN 2026 Philippines Hymn, and a cultural performance showcasing the rich heritage of the Philippines. Welcome addresses were delivered by Dr. Maricor M. Malitao, Executive President of WEF ASEAN 2026 Philippines, and Quezon City Mayor Joy G. Belmonte, represented by City Councilor Doc Ellie Juan. Inspiring messages were also delivered by Dr. Harbeen Arora-Rai, Founder of G100 and the Women Economic Forum, and Datin Dr. (hc) Hajah Hartini Binti Osman, G100 Club Global President and WEF ASEAN President, emphasizing collaboration, innovation, and the advancement of a thriving SHEconomy.

The meetings featured keynote addresses by H.E. Dato’ Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony, Ambassador of Malaysia to the Philippines; Assistant Secretary Ma. Christina Gaerlan Aquino of the Department of Tourism; and Hon. George Erwin M. Garcia, Chairman of the Commission on Elections (COMELEC), highlighting women’s leadership, ethical governance, democratic participation, regional cooperation, and sustainable economic development.

Special highlights included an inspiring presentation by the Delegation of India, a message of support from the Confederation of Asia-Pacific Chambers of Commerce and Industry (CACCI), and messages from Senator Loren Regina B. Legarda and Senator Christopher Lawrence “Bong” T. Go, reaffirming the Philippines’ commitment to empowering women and promoting inclusive economic growth across ASEAN.

The meetings concluded with the formal presentation and acceptance of the WEF ASEAN 2026 Philippines Resolution by the Department of Trade and Industry, reaffirming the collective commitment of government, business, and civil society to advancing women’s economic empowerment throughout the region. The Gala Dinner and WEF ASEAN 2026 Awards Night celebrated outstanding leaders and organizations for their contributions to leadership, entrepreneurship, innovation, public service, and social impact, while a Heritage Tour on 20 June 2026 provided delegates with an enriching cultural experience of the Philippines’ historic landmarks.

The successful hosting of the G100 ASEAN Meetings 2026 – Philippines and the Women Economic Forum (WEF) ASEAN 2026 Philippines reinforced the Philippines’ leadership within ASEAN, strengthened international partnerships, generated meaningful policy and institutional outcomes, expanded opportunities for collaboration and investment, and advanced G100’s mission of empowering women as leaders and changemakers. The meetings further inspired a shared commitment to building a resilient, innovative, and inclusive SHEconomy, where women continue to drive sustainable development, regional cooperation, and transformative global impact.

Convenor:

Dr. Maricor M. Malitao, G100 Global Chair, Business Chambers & Partnerships Wing

Vision

To create an equal, progressive and inclusive environment for women worldwide.

Mission

To provide the thought leadership on what needs to be done for inclusivity, safety, and economic and social empowerment of women globally — closing gender gaps and reaching parity within this decade.

Why G100?

Because we are not waiting a hundred years for gender parity.

With collaboration and co-creation, we are committed to join our forces and strengths, globally and at grassroots, for a better world — defining, designing and determining a new future for ourselves with equity, equal opportunity, inclusion and economic empowerment of women, and of all, through the inclusive agency of women, supported by men champions.

  • Gender parity is possible this decade through collective action.
  • Shared vision and collaboration drive progress.
  • G100 empowers women and advances their aspirations.
  • Global network amplifies voices for equality.
  • Promotes gender equality and sustainable development.
  • Supports women leaders through global networking.
  • Encourages mentorship, collaboration, and leadership.
  • The Denim Club engages male allies to support women.
  • Inclusive participation from women and men is key to parity.

G100 Denim Club

G100 is also supported by The Denim Club: a group of 100 He-for-She champions globally, drawn from business, corporate and political life — each leading a sector of influence in support of gender parity and equality.

They advocate for gender equity and balance, work to remove barriers to women’s leadership, commit to greater C-suite representation for women, and help fuel funding for female founders.

Why “Denim”? It’s symbolic of common ground. While men may be from Mars and women from Venus, and girls grow up in pink and boys in blue, denim belongs to everyone equally — a place of comfort for cool, candid conversation. The sturdy fabric stands for the solid dialogue between genders, and the strength of solidarity we aspire to. Together, we can co-create a better, balanced world for all.

Global President

 The Global President leads G100’s worldwide movement with a clear, bold vision: an equal, inclusive future for women in this decade, not the next.
She works hand-in-hand with Global Chairs, Country Chairs and sector wings to set priorities, build global alliances and drive high-impact initiatives.
Beyond strategy, the Global President is the voice of G100 in global forums, ensuring that women’s leadership, safety and economic empowerment stay at the centre of the world’s agenda.

Advisory Members

Advisory Members form G100’s global brain trust: senior leaders who have shaped policy, built institutions, led movements and transformed industries.
They do not just advise; they co-create. From gender-responsive policies to funding for women-led ventures, they help G100 turn ideas into action at scale.
Their role is to ensure that G100’s work is grounded in evidence, aligned with global best practices, and bold enough to close gender gaps in this decade.

content_html:
Driving Gender Equality Through Collective Global Leadership:

G100 Presents Recommendations for G7 at the Global Leadership by Women Summit 2026, Marseille, France, 6 July 2026

 

 

In the leadership of Datin Hartini Osman, G100 Club Global President 2026, the G100 Club proudly presented its Eight Recommendations for G7 in this year of the French Presidency, toward driving greater gender equality and closing the gaps in areas such as STEM and Financial Inclusion.

The recommendations were officially presented by the G100 Club Global President 2026 before an audience of distinguished international leaders, policymakers, and changemakers.

Grounded in the ELLEGOSSSE Framework—Education, Leadership, Legal Protection, Economic Empowerment, Governance, Ownership, Solidarity, Sustainability, Security, and Equality—the recommendations outline practical and measurable actions to advance women’s leadership, inclusive economic growth, sustainable development, and lasting peace.

A key recommendation was the establishment of a Global Women’s Bank, a dedicated international financial institution aimed at expanding access to affordable finance, investment opportunities, and digital banking services for women and women-led enterprises worldwide. This proposal reflects the G100 Club’s commitment to creating sustainable financial ecosystems that empower women as catalysts of economic transformation.

The G100 Club expressed its hope that these recommendations will contribute meaningfully to the ongoing discussions of the French G7 Presidency and inspire stronger international collaboration toward a future where women are equal partners in shaping economies, governance, innovation, and peace.

Convenor: Datin Hartini Osman, G100 Global Chair, Philanthropy, Business, & Poverty Eradication, and G100 Club Global President 2026
Special thanks to: Chiara Corazza, President of Women Economic Forum Europe, Special Advisor to the Global Leadership by Women Summit, and G100 Presidents Advisory Council Member.

content_html:
Building with Sisterhood

Our networks are powered by distributed leadership and sisterhood, along with a multimodal approach to connection and community development.

Connections begin in many places. Some start on our website or through email. Others begin in a WhatsApp group, a social media thread, an online call or townhall, a direct message, at a local event, or at meetings and conferences.

This creates an innovative field rich with possibility — oriented by calendar, shaped by culture, grounded in sisterhood, guided by values, empowered by vision, and carried forward by a volunteering spirit.

Our Values We persevere and progress together through care, coherence, and resilience, by acting with empathy and creating clarity while staying flexible and strong. We honor complementarity, collaboration, and vision through shared roles and intentional purpose, and we practice vigilance, values, and velocity by responding to community needs, respecting time and culture, and enabling action with speed and sisterhood.

How We Work We are entrepreneurial and responsive to diverse needs. We are flexible in form, resilient in flow, and resourceful in talent. We are mindful of different leadership styles, and respectful of each other.

We work nimbly, amply, and joyfully by sharing roles across a web of people. We are all upheld and buoyed by the power of our collective efforts.

We build with initiative, interaction, intentionality, and integration.

We thrive within ecosystems of exchange and cooperation — adding our bit to the whole, and receiving the same in return from a powerful collaborative.

How We Move Forward We remain connected in spirit and enable action with speed and sisterhood — regardless of the channel or tool to connect.

This is how we connect. This is how we grow. This is how we move forward, together.
